\mathbb EG_N^2\le a_h^2\delta^2+\sigma_*^2/N.
\tag{KU.R5}
$$

The already proved complete-kernel extinction bound gives
$H_N\le e_N=(1-a_*)^N\to0$ in either population. Subtracting the actual
extinction expectation before dividing by the actual survival probability
gives the explicit bound

$$
|\mathbb E[G_N\mid\mathrm{survival}]-\mathbb EG_N|
\le\frac{e_N|a_h|\delta+
 \sqrt{e_N(a_h^2\delta^2+\sigma_*^2/N)}}{1-e_N}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{KU.R6}
$$

The two conditioned mean differences therefore tend to $a_h\delta$.
The same pointwise inequality and Jensen prove the survivor assertion.
Insert either lower bound into the proposed affine inequality and let
$N\to\infty$ to obtain the required positive remainder. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:corollary} Taking a concave power does not fix revival normalization
:label: cor-ku-strict-gap-revival-concave-obstruction

For every fixed $r>0$, neither the raw nor the survivor-conditioned complete
kernel admits a population-independent multiplicative bound for
$\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}^{r/2}$ on all nonextinct inputs. In the same strict-gap
construction, with $m=|a_h|\delta>0$, every raw output coupling satisfies

$$
\mathbb E\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}^{r/2}\ge
q_x^{r/2}(m/2)^r
\left(1-\frac{32\sigma_*^2}{Nm^2}\right)_+.
\tag{KU.R7}
$$

For survivor-conditioned couplings replace the last fraction by
$32\sigma_*^2/[Nm^2(1-e_N)]$.
The entering cost is $(2\alpha\delta^2/N)^{r/2}$ and tends to zero,
whereas these lower bounds tend to a strictly positive constant.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Chebyshev and (KU.R5) give probability at most
$16\sigma_*^2/(Nm^2)$ for either averaged coordinate to differ from its own
raw mean by at least $m/4$. In any coupling the union of these two events
has probability at most their sum. On its complement the difference of the
averaged coordinates has absolute value at least $m/2$.
The pointwise completed-square inequality gives
$\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}\ge q_x|G_N-\widetilde G_N|^2$, proving (KU.R7).
Under original survivor conditioning each marginal's deviation probability
is at most its unconditioned value divided by its survival probability,
which is at least $1-e_N$. This proves the asserted conditional version
without using concave Jensen or presuming unchanged conditional means.
The limiting lower bounds exclude a finite coefficient independent of $N$.
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:proposition} Prescribed coupling costs and optimal alive transport have different quantifiers
:label: prop-ku-prescribed-coupling-versus-optimal-transport

Let $\mathscr Q_{\rm phys}$ denote $\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}$ with
$\lambda_a=0$. For two full physical output laws $P_S,P_T$, define

$$
\mathcal W_{2,N}^2(P_S,P_T)
=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P_S,P_T)}\int\mathscr Q_{\rm phys}\,d\pi.
                                                               \tag{KU.T1}
$$

For every prescribed coupling $\pi_*$,
$\mathcal W_{2,N}^2(P_S,P_T)
\le\int\mathscr Q_{\rm phys}\,d\pi_*$. A lower bound on this one
coupling cost therefore gives no lower bound on the optimal distance.

For equally weighted empirical phase-space measures
$\mu_z=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{z_i}$ and
$\mu_{\widetilde z}=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{\widetilde z_i}$,
using the positive quadratic $q$ of
{prf:ref}`thm-ku-preparation-keystone` as ground squared distance,

$$
W_{2,q}^2(\mu_z,\mu_{\widetilde z})
=\min_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N}\frac1N
 \sum_iq(z_i-\widetilde z_{\sigma(i)})
\le\frac1N\sum_iq(z_i-\widetilde z_i).                         \tag{KU.T2}
$$

This applies to full slots or to equally sized alive pools with the
corresponding normalization. When alive counts differ, the two
alive empirical measures instead use their own normalized optimal
transport plan. A fixed full-slot pairing is not automatically a
transport plan between them.

A cost calculation for the raw complete update also does not
automatically apply after separately normalizing each law by its
survival probability. In particular,
{prf:ref}`thm-ku-allalive-source-coupling-obstruction` concerns its
prescribed coupling, not optimal alive transport. Its physical raw
calculation is unchanged if terminal killing is disabled for that
update, but its lower bound is not thereby an optimal-transport lower
bound or a survivor-conditioned theorem.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The prescribed coupling is one member of the infimum in (KU.T1).
For (KU.T2), empirical transport plans are doubly stochastic matrices
scaled by $1/N$. Minimizing their linear transport cost admits a
permutation minimizer by the finite Birkhoff decomposition; the identity
permutation gives the inequality. Thus even a positive lower bound on
the fixed-row cost cannot bound this smaller empirical cost from below.
Different alive counts change both marginals and the admissible plans.

If a raw coupling is conditioned on both outputs surviving, its first
marginal is conditioned on the joint event, which generally differs
from conditioning the first output on its own survival. Its marginals
need not be $Q_N(S,\cdot)/Q_N1(S)$ and
$Q_N(T,\cdot)/Q_N1(T)$. Those two normalized laws require a separate
coupling calculation. The near-tie theorem forms landing positions and
retained velocities before applying terminal marks; removing that final
marking therefore leaves its physical path calculation unchanged.
It changes none of the infimum directions above. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Near-tie cost of the prescribed source coupling
:label: thm-ku-allalive-source-coupling-obstruction

Use the real-coordinate canonical reference kernel of
`18a_keystone_uniform_coupled.md`, with quadratic objective
$U(x)=|x|^2/2$, reward $R=-U$, terminal box $D=[-2,2]^3$, and either
dense viscosity normalization. In particular,

$$
\begin{gathered}
h=0.04,\quad \gamma=1,\quad b_O=1,\quad \nu=0.3,\quad \rho=1,\quad
V=2,\quad \alpha_c=0.5,\quad \sigma_J=\sigma_x=0.1,\\
R_x=R_v=\epsilon_D=\epsilon_C=2,\quad \lambda_{\rm alg}=1,\quad
\delta_D=10^{-3},\\
A_r=A_s=2,\quad \eta_r=\eta_s=0.1,\quad
p_r=p_s=1,\quad \sigma_{r,\min}=\sigma_{s,\min}=0.1,\quad
s_c=1,\quad \epsilon_c=10^{-6}.
\end{gathered}
$$

Couple the actual measurement laws maximally and independently across
rows, use the conditional maximal source-token coupling (KU.17), share
the corresponding recipient Gaussian jitters, and share the corresponding
OU and final-position Gaussians. Use the stated component-Haar coupling.
All Gaussians retain their complete, unbounded laws.

Fix $\alpha,\gamma_P>0$, $\alpha\gamma_P>\beta^2$, and $\lambda_a\ge0$.
For complete marked physical states define

$$
\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}(S,\widetilde S)
=\frac1N\sum_i\left[
\alpha|x_i-\widetilde x_i|^2
+2\beta(x_i-\widetilde x_i)\cdot(v_i-\widetilde v_i)
+\gamma_P|v_i-\widetilde v_i|^2
+\lambda_a(a_i-\widetilde a_i)^2\right].
$$

For every even $N=2n\ge4$, take $n$ rows at $+e_1$ and $n$ rows at
$-e_1$, with every velocity zero and every mark alive. Call this state
$S_N$. Let $\widetilde S_{N,\varepsilon}$ be its translation by
$\varepsilon e_1$, with the same velocities and marks, where
$0<\varepsilon\le0.1$. Both entering states lie in the terminal box.
Put

$$
\begin{gathered}
t=h/2,\qquad c=e^{-\gamma h},\qquad a_1=1-t^2(1+c)>0,\qquad
\alpha_0=\alpha-\beta^2/\gamma_P>0,\\
w_0=e^{-2/9},\qquad \theta_0=\frac{w_0}{1+w_0},\qquad
c_g=\frac1{2\sqrt2\,(4.41+10^{-6})}.
\end{gathered}
$$

For the raw complete update, including both viscous kicks, the cap and
terminal marking, the prescribed coupling satisfies

$$
\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}(S_N,\widetilde S_{N,\varepsilon})
=\alpha\varepsilon^2
\tag{KU.O14}
$$

and

$$
\mathbb E\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}(S_N^+,\widetilde S_{N,\varepsilon}^+)
\ge\frac{\alpha_0 a_1^2\theta_0^3c_g}{2}
\left[(2-\varepsilon)^2+3\sigma_J^2\right]\varepsilon.
\tag{KU.O15}
$$

Consequently, no $\kappa>0$ and deterministic sequence $r_N\to0$
can satisfy

$$
\mathbb E\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}(S^+,\widetilde S^+)
\le(1-\kappa)\mathscr Q_{\rm mark}(S,\widetilde S)+r_N
\tag{KU.O16}
$$

for this coupling at every admissible entering pair and every even $N$.
The conclusion remains valid for the physical quadratic obtained by
setting $\lambda_a=0$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
**Measurement probabilities.** Since all velocities are zero, a
same-site companion has feature distance zero. The cross-site feature
distance in the translated swarm is

$$
\Delta_\varepsilon
=\frac{2(1+\varepsilon)}{3+\varepsilon}
 +\frac{2(1-\varepsilon)}{3-\varepsilon}
=\frac{4(3-\varepsilon^2)}{9-\varepsilon^2}
\le\frac43=\Delta_0.
$$

Thus the common cross-site weight for either role is
$w_\varepsilon=\exp(-\Delta_\varepsilon^2/8)\ge w_0$.
For each row the cross-site companion probability is

$$
\theta_{N,\varepsilon}
=\frac{nw_\varepsilon}{n-1+nw_\varepsilon}
\ge\theta_{N,0}\ge\theta_0.
\tag{KU.O17}
$$

For each specified opposite-site label, its individual companion
probability $w/(n-1+nw)$ increases with $w$. Hence the maximal
measurement coupling assigns common cross-site labels total mass exactly
$\theta_{N,0}$. Call this event a shared high mark. The measurement
couplings of distinct rows are independent. Two specified distinct rows
therefore both have shared high marks with probability
$\theta_{N,0}^2$. This calculation retains self exclusion and holds
uniformly in $N$.

**The actual fitness gap.** In $S_N$, every raw reward is $-1/2$.
Its standardized reward array is therefore identically zero, and every
reward factor is $1.1$. Each realized raw diversity array has only the
same-site and cross-site values. A row with a high mark has maximal
diversity, and hence maximal realized fitness. It accepts no cloning
donor, including high-mark donors, for every assignment of the other
measurements. This also includes the assignment in which every mark is
high and the standardized diversity array is zero.

For $n\ge2$, $0<\theta_{N,0}<1$. A specified low-mark recipient
and high-mark donor consequently occur with positive probability, and
their cloning donor probability is positive. Their raw diversities are
strictly different, so the increasing diversity logistic gives a strictly
positive gate. Thus the baseline swarm already has positive
measurement-averaged cloning activity with the configured diversity
exponent $p_s=1$.

In the translated swarm, the raw rewards at the minus and plus sites
are respectively $-(1-\varepsilon)^2/2$ and
$-(1+\varepsilon)^2/2$. Their shared mean is
$-(1+\varepsilon^2)/2$ and their shared variance is
$\varepsilon^2$. The standardized rewards at those sites are exactly
$+z_\varepsilon$ and $-z_\varepsilon$, where

$$
z_\varepsilon
=\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+0.01}}\in(0,1).
$$

Take a plus-site recipient $i$ and a minus-site candidate donor $j$.
When both have shared high marks, their translated raw diversities are
equal. Their translated diversity factors consequently equal the same
value $G_s\ge\eta_s=0.1$, with the realized global mean and
standardizer retained. Their fitness difference is

$$
\widetilde F_j-\widetilde F_i
=G_s\,[G_r(z_\varepsilon)-G_r(-z_\varepsilon)]
=2G_s\tanh(z_\varepsilon/2).
$$

For $0\le u\le1/2$, $\tanh u\ge u/2$. Indeed,
$(\tanh u-u/2)'=\operatorname{sech}^2u-1/2>0$ there;
$\cosh(1/2)\le\sum_{k\ge0}4^{-k}=4/3<\sqrt2$
proves the last inequality. Thus, using
$\varepsilon\le0.1$,

$$
\widetilde F_j-\widetilde F_i
\ge\frac{\varepsilon}{2\sqrt2}.
$$

The actual recipient denominator is at most
$s_c(F^*+\epsilon_c)=4.41+10^{-6}$. Therefore its clipped gate
obeys

$$
\mathfrak a(\widetilde F_i,\widetilde F_j)
\ge c_g\varepsilon.
\tag{KU.O18}
$$

The clipping inequality follows because $c_g\varepsilon<1$ in the
stated interval. Both the zero gate of the baseline recipient and this
positive translated gate use actual sampled fitnesses. No fitness
average has been inserted before the positive-part or clipping operation.

**A linear mismatch mass.** On the shared-high event for $i$, the
baseline source-token law is the point mass $(0,i)$. Consequently,
conditional maximal token coupling pairs every translated accepted token
with that baseline persistence token. Sum the translated accepted mass
over all minus-site donors $j$. For each such $j$, the shared-high
event for $i,j$ has probability $\theta_{N,0}^2$, and (KU.O18) holds
uniformly over the other measurements. The cloning donor law is
independent of the measurement draws and assigns the minus site total
mass $\theta_{N,\varepsilon}$. Hence the probability that row $i$
has baseline persistence and translated cross-site copying, with those
shared high marks, is at least

$$
\theta_{N,0}^2\theta_{N,\varepsilon}c_g\varepsilon
\ge\theta_0^3c_g\varepsilon.
\tag{KU.O19}
$$

On this event its prepared position discrepancy is exactly
$(2-\varepsilon)e_1-\sigma_J\zeta_i$, with a standard
three-dimensional Gaussian $\zeta_i$ independent of all measurements
and source tokens. Its conditional second moment is
$(2-\varepsilon)^2+3\sigma_J^2$. In particular the Gaussian tail
has been integrated, rather than discarded.

**The complete position update.** Every frozen slot velocity is zero.
Every accepted-component mean and relative velocity is consequently
zero, and every Haar collision leaves the prepared velocities zero.
The first viscous force vanishes under both normalization choices for
every prepared position array, including all jitter realizations. The
quadratic external force gives $u=-t x^C$. The two BAOAB drifts,
the shared OU innovation and the shared final-position innovation
therefore give the exact full positional difference

$$
x_i^+-\widetilde x_i^+
=a_1(x_i^C-\widetilde x_i^C).
\tag{KU.O20}
$$

The second viscous kick, second external force and velocity cap occur
after the position that appears in (KU.O20) has been formed; they change
the final velocity and leave this position unchanged. Terminal marking
retains that physical position in both alive and dead slots. Thus
(KU.O20) is valid for the raw complete marked kernel, regardless of
the realized terminal indicators.

Complete the metric square:

$$
\alpha|d|^2+2\beta d\cdot u+\gamma_P|u|^2
=\alpha_0|d|^2+
\gamma_P|u+(\beta/\gamma_P)d|^2
\ge\alpha_0|d|^2.
$$

The status term is nonnegative. Sum (KU.O19)--(KU.O20) over the $N/2$
plus-site rows, discard the other nonnegative terms, and integrate their
independent Gaussian jitters. This proves (KU.O15). The entering
translation, zero velocity discrepancy and equal marks prove (KU.O14).

**Failure of a vanishing-residual margin.** Set

$$
K=\frac{\alpha_0a_1^2\theta_0^3c_g}{2}
(1.9^2+0.03)>0.
$$

For every $\varepsilon\in(0,0.1]$, (KU.O15) is at least
$K\varepsilon$. Choose a fixed
$\varepsilon_0\in(0,\min\{0.1,K/(4\alpha)\})$.
Then $K\varepsilon_0>4\alpha\varepsilon_0^2$.
If $r_N\to0$, take an even $N$ large enough that
$r_N<2\alpha\varepsilon_0^2$. The proposed right side in
(KU.O16) is less than $3\alpha\varepsilon_0^2$, whereas its actual
left side is greater than $4\alpha\varepsilon_0^2$.
This is a contradiction for every $\kappa>0$.
In particular an $O(N^{-2})$ residual fails. With
$\varepsilon_N=1/N$, the lower bound is $K/N$, while both the
initial metric and such a residual are $O(N^{-2})$.
The proof used no status penalty, so $\lambda_a=0$ gives the same
conclusion. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:remark} Scope of the obstruction
:label: rem-ku-allalive-source-coupling-obstruction-scope

The theorem refutes a global quadratic margin for the specified maximal
measurement and source-token coupling with shared physical innovations.
It concerns actual all-alive inputs with arbitrarily small discrepancies,
positive diversity exponents, positive measured cloning activity and
untruncated Gaussian innovations. The incoming reward ties and sampled
same-mark ties are retained. Its lower bound survives removal of the
terminal-status penalty and is independent of a small alive fraction.

The theorem addresses the raw one-update coupling required by (KU.F1).
It gives no lower bound on the optimal Wasserstein distance between the
two complete output laws, and it does not refute a different coupling,
a block contraction theorem or the finite-population QSD theorem.
Survival conditioning and any alternative metric require their own
complete calculations.
:::

:::{prf:lemma} Gaussian smoothing makes a small mixture-weight change quadratic in optimal transport
:label: lem-ku-gaussian-mixture-weight-smoothing

Let $\gamma_m=\mathcal N(m,\sigma^2I_d)$ and
$\gamma_n=\mathcal N(n,\sigma^2I_d)$, $\sigma>0$, and put
$\mu_a=(1-a)\gamma_m+a\gamma_n$. For
$a,b\in[0,a_0]$, $a_0<1$, with $D_{mn}=|n-m|$,

$$
W_2^2(\mu_a,\mu_b)
\le\frac{|a-b|^2D_{mn}^2}{1-a_0}
       \exp(D_{mn}^2/\sigma^2).                               \tag{KU.T3}
$$

In contrast, coupling the component labels maximally and using one
common Gaussian innovation for both component labels costs
$|a-b|D_{mn}^2$. Thus a prescribed source coupling can have cost
linear in the changed mixture mass while an alternative coupling has
quadratic cost. For independent products of $N$ such mixtures and the
normalized ground cost $N^{-1}\sum_i|z_i-\widetilde z_i|^2$,
the same upper bound (KU.T3) holds independently of $N$.

The product conclusion assumes independent rows. It is not an
assertion that the canonical gas's globally standardized measurements
or component collisions have a product law, nor that (KU.T3) gives
a coefficient smaller than one for that complete gas. Component-dependent
clone-jitter covariances and the complete phase-space pushforward also
require their own estimates before this illustration can be applied.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The case $m=n$ is immediate. Otherwise rotate and translate coordinates
so the two means differ by $D=D_{mn}$ only in the first coordinate.
The common perpendicular Gaussian can be coupled identically, reducing
the construction to one dimension. Write $f_0,f_D$ for its two Gaussian
densities, $F_0,F_D$ for their distribution functions, and
$\rho_u=(1-u)f_0+uf_D$. For a common uniform $U\in(0,1)$ let
$Z_u=F_{\rho_u}^{-1}(U)$. Its marginals are $\rho_u$, and
differentiating the strictly increasing distribution function gives

$$
\frac{dZ_u}{du}
=\frac{F_0(Z_u)-F_D(Z_u)}{\rho_u(Z_u)},\qquad
F_0(z)-F_D(z)=D\int_0^1f_{rD}(z)\,dr.                         \tag{KU.T4}
$$

Since $\rho_u\ge(1-a_0)f_0$ throughout the parameter interval,
Jensen's inequality and the elementary Gaussian likelihood integral yield

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\left|\frac{dZ_u}{du}\right|^2
&\le\frac{D^2}{1-a_0}
 \int_0^1\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{f_{rD}(z)^2}{f_0(z)}\,dz\,dr\\
&=\frac{D^2}{1-a_0}\int_0^1 e^{r^2D^2/\sigma^2}\,dr
\le\frac{D^2e^{D^2/\sigma^2}}{1-a_0}.                         \tag{KU.T5}
\end{aligned}
$$

The middle identity follows by completing the square in the Gaussian
exponent. These finite integrals justify the parameter integration;
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
$\mathbb E|Z_a-Z_b|^2\le|a-b|
\int_{\min(a,b)}^{\max(a,b)}\mathbb E|dZ_u/du|^2du$,
which proves (KU.T3). Under the stated label coupling, the mismatch
event has probability $|a-b|$ and position discrepancy exactly $D$,
proving its linear cost. Taking independent copies of the quantile
coupling in each row and averaging their costs proves the product bound.
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:proposition} Optimal alive positional transport can expand inside a common Rastrigin well
:label: prop-ku-rastrigin-alive-transport-expansion

Use the unchanged real-coordinate canonical update with the numerical
parameters of {prf:ref}`thm-ku-allalive-source-coupling-obstruction`,
either dense viscosity normalization, and the separable Rastrigin
objective and reward

$$
U(x)=\sum_{r=1}^3\{x_r^2+10[1-\cos(2\pi x_r)]\},\quad
R=-U,\quad F_r(x)=-2x_r-20\pi\sin(2\pi x_r).                \tag{KU.A1}
$$

For every $N\ge2$ and $0<\delta\le0.004$, take all marks alive and
all velocities zero. In the first swarm every position is
$x_-=(1/2-\delta/2)e_1$; in the second every position is
$x_+=(1/2+\delta/2)e_1$. Both fitness arrays tie exactly under
the active configured fitness law. Put

$$
\eta=t^2(1+c),\quad \tau^2=t^2q^2+s^2,\quad
\phi_h(u)=u+\eta[-2u-20\pi\sin(2\pi u)],\quad
m_\pm=\phi_h(1/2\pm\delta/2).                               \tag{KU.A2}
$$

Before terminal killing, the output positional arrays have the product
laws $\rho_\pm^{\otimes N}$ with
$\rho_\pm=\mathcal N(m_\pm e_1,\tau^2I_3)$. For the normalized
positional array transport cost, and also for optimal expected transport
between the random full empirical position measures,

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_2^2(\rho_-,\rho_+)
&=|m_+-m_-|^2>1.2996\,\delta^2,\\
\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\rho_-^{\otimes N},\rho_+^{\otimes N})}
 \mathbb E_\pi W_2^2\!\left(
 \frac1N\sum_i\delta_{X_i},\frac1N\sum_i\delta_{Y_i}\right)
&=|m_+-m_-|^2.                                                \tag{KU.A3}
\end{aligned}
$$

If each complete output is instead conditioned on at least one survivor
in $D=[-2,2]^3$, the law of a uniformly sampled alive position is
exactly $\bar\rho_\pm=\rho_\pm(\cdot\mid D)$ for every $N$.
These actual normalized alive marginals satisfy

$$
W_2^2(\bar\rho_-,\bar\rho_+)>(1.12\,\delta)^2.              \tag{KU.A4}
$$

The same strict lower bound holds for the expected positional $W_2^2$
between the two alive empirical measures under every coupling of the
two survivor-conditioned full output laws. The entering alive measures
have distance squared $\delta^2$. Thus this is an optimal-transport
counterexample to global one-step monotonicity for alive positional
$W_2$, and for the usual Euclidean phase-space $W_2$ by projection.
It is not a conclusion about every weighted hypocoercive metric,
eventual convergence or a block estimate.

Both initial first coordinates lie in the same deterministic
overdamped basin: the scalar flow $\dot u=-2u-20\pi\sin(2\pi u)$
from either point converges to $0$. This basin statement concerns that
deterministic flow, not the noisy swarm law.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Every sampled separation in a consensus swarm equals the configured
floor, and each swarm has a constant reward array. Standardization
therefore yields zero in both channels. All optional cloning gates
vanish, so the preparation persists with zero velocity. The first
viscous force is zero for both normalizations. The actual BAOAB landing
map (KUK.1) is consequently
$X_i^+=\phi_h(u)e_1+tq\xi_i+s\chi_i$ with independent row
innovations. B2 and the cap do not alter these positions. This proves
the stated product Gaussian laws without changing any active parameter.

For $y=1/2+\delta/2$, $x=1/2-\delta/2$, the exact force gap is

$$
\frac{F_1(y)-F_1(x)}{\delta}
=-2+40\pi\frac{\sin(\pi\delta)}{\delta}>350.                \tag{KU.A5}
$$

Indeed, $\sin u\ge u-u^3/6$ for $u\ge0$ and
$9<\pi^2<10$ give a lower bound
$-2+360[1-10(0.004)^2/6]>350$. The sine inequality follows by
integrating three times the nonnegative third derivative
$1-\cos u$ of $\sin u-u+u^3/6$ from zero.
With $t=0.02$ and $c=e^{-0.04}>0$,
$\eta=0.0004(1+c)>0.0004$. Hence
$m_+-m_-=\delta+\eta[F_1(y)-F_1(x)]>1.14\delta$.
Gaussians with identical covariance have squared transport distance
equal to their squared mean separation: translation gives the upper
bound and Jensen gives the lower bound. For any empirical pair,
$W_2^2$ is at least the squared separation of their barycenters.
Jensen over an arbitrary coupling therefore gives the same mean-gap
lower bound in (KU.A3). Translating every row with common innovations
attains it. Since $1.14^2=1.2996$, (KU.A3) follows.

We next verify the survival-normalized statement, rather than
transferring the raw coupling. On the entire interval $[x,y]$,
$|F_1(u)|<3$, $u\in[0.498,0.502]$, and $\eta<0.0008$.
Thus $m_\pm\in[0.49,0.51]$. Also

$$
q^2=(1-e^{-0.08})/2<0.04,\quad s^2=0.0004,\quad
\tau^2<0.000416<0.0204^2.                                  \tag{KU.A6}
$$

For $Z_m\sim\mathcal N(m,\tau^2)$ define its truncated mean
$T(m)=\mathbb E[Z_m\mid-2\le Z_m\le2]$. Differentiation of the
bounded-domain Gaussian integrals gives

$$
T'(m)=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Z_m\mid-2\le Z_m\le2)}{\tau^2}
>0.99,\qquad 0.49\le m\le0.51.                              \tag{KU.A7}
$$

Here is an explicit verification of the lower bound. For
$Z=(Z_m-m)/\tau\sim\mathcal N(0,1)$, the truncation interval
contains $[-68,68]$, because its closest face is at distance at
least $1.49$ and $1.49/0.0204>68$. Write $A$ for this interval.
Integration of the Gaussian density gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(A^c)&\le2\phi(68)/68<10^{-6},\\
\mathbb E[Z^2\mathbf1_{A^c}]&
\le2(68+1/68)\phi(68)<137\,10^{-6},\\
\mathbb E[|Z|\mathbf1_{A^c}]&\le2\phi(68)<2\,10^{-6}.
                                                               \tag{KU.A8}
\end{aligned}
$$

The tail inequality uses
$1-\Phi(r)\le\phi(r)/r$, obtained by integrating $z/r\ge1$
over $z\ge r$. For the numerical bounds it suffices that
$\phi(68)<e^{-2312}<10^{-6}$, since
$e^{2312}>2312^2/2>10^6$. Consequently
$|\mathbb E[Z\mid A]|<3\,10^{-6}$ and
$\mathbb E[Z^2\mid A]>1-137\,10^{-6}$.
Their difference gives conditional variance greater than $0.99$,
proving (KU.A7). Integrating that derivative between $m_-$ and
$m_+$ yields
$T(m_+)-T(m_-)>0.99(1.14\delta)>1.12\delta$.

The row positions are independent before marking. Conditional on any
realized nonempty mark vector, every alive row has position law
$\bar\rho_\pm$, independently of which row labels survived.
Uniformly sampling one of those rows therefore gives
$\bar\rho_\pm$ exactly, and conditioning further only on a nonempty
vector preserves that law. Its first-coordinate mean is $T(m_\pm)$;
the other two coordinate means are zero by reflection. Jensen gives
(KU.A4). Likewise, the conditional expectation of the barycenter of
the entire alive empirical measure is $T(m_\pm)e_1$.
Applying the empirical barycenter inequality and then Jensen to any
coupling of the two conditioned arrays proves its stated lower bound.
Projection to position cannot increase the standard Euclidean
phase-space transport cost, so the phase-space assertion follows.

Finally, the deterministic force is strictly negative on $(0,0.502]$.
On $(0,1/2]$, the sine is nonnegative and the $-2u$ term is strict.
For $u=1/2+v$, $0\le v\le0.002$,
$F_1(u)=-1-2v+20\pi\sin(2\pi v)
\le-1+40\pi^2v<-0.2$. Smooth uniqueness prevents a positive
trajectory from crossing the equilibrium $0$. Each such trajectory
decreases to a limit; continuity of the force and its strict sign
away from $0$ force that limit to be $0$. This proves the common-well
statement while leaving the noisy convergence question separate.
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:definition} Strict-gap native two-row family
:label: def-kugc-two-row

Take the canonical Viscous Euclidean Gas in $d=3$, $N=2$, with

$$
h=0.04,\quad t=h/2,\quad c=e^{-h},\quad
b_h=t(1+c),\quad A=1-b_ht,\quad
\nu=0.3,\quad\rho=1,\quad U(x)=|x|^2/2,
$$

and all the original reference preparation parameters. Let

$$
S_a:\quad x_1=-ae_1,\quad x_2=be_1,\quad
v_1=v_2=0,\quad a_1=a_2=1,\qquad b=0.9,
\quad1\le a\le1.001.
$$

Here the notation $a_1,a_2$ denotes alive marks; $a$ is the physical
radius parameter. The boundary box remains $[-2,2]^3$. Since every
measurement row has exactly one distinct eligible companion, both raw
diversity measurements are the same smoothed norm
$\sqrt{|z_1-z_2|^2+10^{-6}}$. Their actual global standardization is
exactly zero, without replacing sampled diversity by an expectation.
The reward difference and standardized values are

$$
D(a)=\frac{a^2-b^2}{2},\qquad
z(a)=\frac{D(a)}{\sqrt{D(a)^2+0.04}},\qquad
Z_{r,1}=-z(a),\quad Z_{r,2}=z(a).
$$

Let $G(z)=2/(1+e^{-z})+0.1$ and $\varepsilon=10^{-6}/1.1$.
The two actual retained fitnesses are

$$
F_1(a)=1.1G(-z(a)),\quad F_2(a)=1.1G(z(a)),
$$

and the sole possible accepted edge is $1\to2$, with probability

$$
p(a)=\frac{G(z(a))-G(-z(a))}{G(-z(a))+\varepsilon}
=\frac{2.2-2f(a)}{f(a)+\varepsilon},\qquad f(a)=G(-z(a)).
\tag{KUSC.1}
$$

This gate is strictly between zero and one on the whole stated interval.
At $a=1$,

$$
F_1=0.9775734716359625,\quad F_2=1.4424265283640378,
\quad p=0.4755167715766428.
$$

The fitness gap is $0.4648530567280753$ and the gate is unsaturated.
This example therefore does not use a complete or near fitness tie.
:::

:::{prf:lemma} Exact full-step position law
:label: lem-kugc-position-law

For either viscosity normalization, the actual output positions are

$$
x_i^+=AX_i+tq\xi_i^O+s\xi_i^x,\qquad
q^2=(1-e^{-2h})/2,\quad s^2=0.01h,
\tag{KUSC.2}
$$

where row two always has $X_2=be_1$, and row one has
$X_1=-ae_1$ with probability $1-p(a)$ or
$X_1=be_1+0.1\zeta_1$ with probability $p(a)$.
All displayed Gaussian vectors are independent within a marginal.
Consequently the row-one first-coordinate law is the exact mixture

$$
\rho_a=(1-p(a))\mathcal N(-Aa,\sigma_0^2)
             +p(a)\mathcal N(Ab,\sigma_1^2),
$$

$$
\sigma_0^2=t^2q^2+s^2=0.0004153767307226729,\qquad
\sigma_1^2=A^2(0.1)^2+\sigma_0^2=0.010399696566721815.
\tag{KUSC.3}
$$

*Proof.* When there is an accepted component, both frozen velocities
are zero. Its component mean and relative velocities are zero, so
its shared Haar collision output is zero for every Haar realization.
Without an accepted edge both velocities also remain zero. Thus the
first viscous force is exactly zero in either normalization. The first
force kick is $-tX_i$, the two drifts and the OU stage give
$(1-t^2(1+c))X_i+tq\xi_i^O$, and final position diffusion adds
$s\xi_i^x$. The second potential and viscous kicks, followed by the
velocity cap, change velocities only. Terminal classification attaches
the mark and retains these positions even on exit. This proves (KUSC.2).
The Gaussian jitter is independent of the gate and of both kinetic
innovations; integrate it exactly to obtain (KUSC.3).
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:theorem} The prescribed common-source quadratic ledger cannot contract globally
:label: thm-kugc-source-quadratic-obstruction

Couple $S_1$ and $S_{1+\delta}$ by the actual common-source maximal
plan, shared accepted-row jitter, shared component rotations where
components agree, and shared kinetic Gaussians, for $0<\delta\le0.001$.
Let the normalized positional cost be
$P^+=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^2|x_i^+-\widetilde x_i^+|^2$.
The exact full-step expectation is

$$
\mathbb EP^+=\frac{A^2}{2}\left[
(1-p(1+\delta))\delta^2+
(p(1+\delta)-p(1))\big((1+b)^2+3(0.1)^2\big)
\right].
\tag{KUSC.4}
$$

For its first-coordinate projection, replace $3(0.1)^2$ by $(0.1)^2$.
The entering positional cost is $\delta^2/2$. Direct differentiation gives

$$
p'(1)=4.90316448668362,\qquad
\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\frac{\mathbb EP^+}{\delta}
=8.909766764728248>0.
\tag{KUSC.5}
$$

For every fixed positive definite paired phase quadratic form
$G=\begin{psmallmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\\beta&\gamma_P\end{psmallmatrix}$,
with minimum eigenvalue $\lambda_->0$, and every nonnegative terminal
status cost, its complete-output expectation is at least
$\lambda_-\mathbb EP^+$. Its input value is $\alpha\delta^2/2$.
Hence it cannot have nonpositive drift at every entering pair under
this prescribed coupling. Every signed recipient, incoming donor,
collision, force, cap and terminal term of the exact ledger sums to
this positive output cost; no refinement of an upper-bound constant
can reverse its actual sign.

*Proof.* Monotonicity of $p(a)$ follows from (KUSC.1). Common acceptance
has mass $p(1)$ and places both prepared populations at the same positions
with the same jitter; their full outputs coincide. Common persistence
has mass $1-p(1+\delta)$ and leaves a row-one prepared difference
$\delta e_1$. Its final position difference is $A\delta e_1$.
The residual plan has mass $p(1+\delta)-p(1)$ and pairs cloning
from $be_1$ with persistence at $-e_1$. Its final row-one difference
is $A[(1+b)e_1+0.1\zeta_1]$. Row-two final positions coincide
in every branch. Integrate the unrestricted jitter second moment
and apply (KUSC.2); this gives (KUSC.4).

For $f(z)=0.1+2/(1+e^z)$,

$$
\frac{dp}{dz}=-\frac{(2.2+2\varepsilon)f'(z)}{(f(z)+\varepsilon)^2},
\qquad \frac{dz}{da}=\frac{0.04a}{[D(a)^2+0.04]^{3/2}}.
$$

Substitute $a=1$ to obtain (KUSC.5). Positive definiteness gives
$Q\ge\lambda_-P^+$ pointwise irrespective of the actual output
velocities, so the B2 viscous kick, cap and velocity cross term cannot
remove the lower bound. Terminal status penalties are nonnegative
and initial marks agree. Since the positive linear term dominates
every fixed input quadratic coefficient as $\delta\downarrow0$,
the claimed global drift closure is impossible for this coupling.
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Gaussian-first coupling also does not give global one-step Euclidean contraction
:label: thm-kugc-optimal-one-step-obstruction

The actual first-coordinate transition mean is

$$
m(a)=A[-a(1-p(a))+bp(a)],\qquad
m'(1)=A[-(1-p(1))+(1+b)p'(1)]=8.784633961156265.
\tag{KUSC.6}
$$

For every coupling of the two full output laws, even one formed after
their Gaussian mixtures have been integrated,

$$
\frac12\mathbb E\sum_i|x_i^+-\widetilde x_i^+|^2
\ge\frac12|m(1+\delta)-m(1)|^2.
$$

Thus the optimal normalized positional $W_2^2$ ratio to its input
cost has lower limit at least

$$
\liminf_{\delta\downarrow0}
\frac{W_{2,\rm pos}(P_2(S_1,\cdot),P_2(S_{1+\delta},\cdot))^2}
{\delta^2/2}\ge[m'(1)]^2=77.16979383150002>1.
\tag{KUSC.7}
$$

*Proof.* Integrate (KUSC.3), then differentiate the explicit mean.
For any coupling, Jensen applied to the row-one first-coordinate
difference gives the displayed lower bound. The derivative limit
proves (KUSC.7). Adding velocities or marks to an ordinary Euclidean
phase/status transport cost cannot decrease this projection lower
bound. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:lemma} Exact Gaussian-mixture tangent transport cost
:label: lem-kugc-gaussian-tangent

Let $C_a$ and $\rho_a$ be the one-dimensional mixture CDF and density
in (KUSC.3). The squared $W_2$ tangent norm of this density family is
the finite explicit integral

$$
J(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{[\partial_a C_a(x)]^2}{\rho_a(x)}\,dx,
\quad
\partial_aC_a=p'(a)(C_1-C_0)+(1-p(a))A\varphi_0,
\tag{KUSC.8}
$$

where $\varphi_0$ is the $\mathcal N(-Aa,\sigma_0^2)$ density and
$C_0,C_1$ are the two Gaussian CDFs. Its lower bound is
$J(a)\ge[m'(a)]^2$. With

$$
\mathcal X(a)=\frac{\sigma_1^2}
 {\sigma_0\sqrt{2\sigma_1^2-\sigma_0^2}}
\exp\left[\frac{A^2(a+b)^2}{2\sigma_1^2-\sigma_0^2}\right],
$$

an entirely explicit upper bound is

$$
J(a)\le\frac{2p'(a)^2\sigma_1^2}{p(a)}[\mathcal X(a)-1]
+\frac{2(1-p(a))^2A^2}{p(a)}\mathcal X(a).
\tag{KUSC.9}
$$

At the native pair $a=1$, the logarithm of this upper bound is
$178.8870500829268$, while the lower bound is $77.16979383150002$.
The Gaussian-first coupling restores quadratic local regularity
instead of the source-first linear cost, but its actual one-step
derivative still exceeds one.

*Proof.* Differentiating the density continuity equation in $a$
gives velocity $v_a=-\partial_aC_a/\rho_a$. Equivalently, for its
quantile $T_a(u)=C_a^{-1}(u)$,
$\partial_aT_a(u)=-\partial_aC_a(T_a(u))/\rho_a(T_a(u))$.
Changing variables $u=C_a(x)$ gives (KUSC.8). The Gaussian tails,
positive mixture weights and $\sigma_1>\sigma_0$ imply integrability.
Moreover $m'(a)=\int v_a\rho_a$, so Cauchy--Schwarz gives the lower
bound. Completing the square in the two Gaussian densities gives
$\int\varphi_0^2/\varphi_1=\mathcal X(a)$.

For completeness the scalar Gaussian negative-Sobolev estimate is

$$
\int(C_0-C_1)^2/\varphi_1\le
\sigma_1^2\int(\varphi_0/\varphi_1-1)^2\varphi_1
=\sigma_1^2[\mathcal X(a)-1].
$$

Indeed integration by parts identifies its left side with the
variational supremum of
$2\int\phi(\varphi_0-\varphi_1)-\int|\phi'|^2\varphi_1$.
Cauchy--Schwarz and the Gaussian Poincare inequality give the bound.
The latter follows directly from the Mehler semigroup $T_t$ for
$\mathcal N(m,\sigma_1^2)$: differentiate its variance,
$\operatorname{Var}\phi=2\sigma_1^2\int_0^\infty
\int|(T_t\phi)'|^2\varphi_1\,dt$, use
$(T_t\phi)'=e^{-t}T_t\phi'$, Jensen and invariance, and integrate
$2\int_0^\infty e^{-2t}dt=1$. These calculations first apply to
smooth bounded functions and extend by truncation.
Finally $\rho_a\ge p(a)\varphi_1$ and $(u+v)^2\le2(u^2+v^2)$
give (KUSC.9). $\square$
:::

:::{prf:theorem} A fully computed positive full-marked concave-cost regime
:label: thm-kugc-concave-local

Use the actual same source/Haar/Gaussian coupling as (KUSC.4) and
the full marked distance

$$
d_{\rm mark}(S,T)^2=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^2
[|x_i-y_i|^2+|v_i-w_i|^2+(a_i-\widetilde a_i)^2].
$$

For the reference pair, every $0<\delta\le2.09\,10^{-5}$ obeys

$$
\mathbb E\,d_{\rm mark}(S_1^+,S_{1+\delta}^+)^{1/2}
\le0.76225\,d_{\rm mark}(S_1,S_{1+\delta})^{1/2}
\tag{KUSC.10}
$$

in either viscosity normalization. This retains unbounded Gaussian
jitter and both kinetic innovations, the physical viscosity kernel,
the velocity cap and terminal mark mismatch.

*Proof.* Write $r=1/2$, $H=t(c+A)$,
$\ell=e^{-1/2}/\rho$, and
$\mu_\chi=2\Gamma((d+1)/2)/\Gamma(d/2)$, the exact mean norm of
$N(0,2I_d)$. On common persistence, first alignment vanishes. The
row-one position difference is $A\delta e_1$ and the OU velocity
difference is $ct\delta e_1$. In row normalization $N=2$ has one
neighbor and $K/Z=1$, so its second viscous force is exactly
$\nu(z_{\rm other}-z_i)$. The resulting squared Lipschitz factor
for the physical normalized phase distance is at most

$$
L_{\rm row}^2=A^2+(H+t\nu ct)^2+(t\nu ct)^2
=0.9999776973498014.
$$

For count normalization, use the actual Gaussian gradient maximum
$\ell$ on its physical separation and the common-OU velocity
$z_2-z_1=ct(1+b)e_1+q(\xi_2^O-\xi_1^O)$. Set

$$
B_0=ct[1+\ell A(1+b)],\qquad B_1=\ell Aq,\qquad
\overline B=B_0+B_1\mu_\chi,\quad
\overline{B^2}=B_0^2+2B_0B_1\mu_\chi+2dB_1^2.
$$

The two raw velocity discrepancies are bounded respectively by
$\delta[H+(t\nu/2)B]$ and $\delta(t\nu/2)B$. The cap is
$1$-Lipschitz. Consequently

$$
\mathbb E L_{\rm count}^2\le A^2+H^2+
2H(t\nu/2)\overline B+2(t\nu/2)^2\overline{B^2}
=1.000043382452391.
$$

These are exact Gaussian first/second moments of the displayed
upper profiles, without a bounded-innovation event.
Common acceptance has zero complete-output discrepancy. On common
persistence, the physical $r$-power cost is therefore at most
$(\delta/\sqrt2)^r(\mathbb EL^2)^{r/2}$.
For terminal marks, only row one's position can differ. Its final
Gaussian coordinate differs by the deterministic shift $A\delta$.
The two boundary crossing intervals have total probability at most
$2A\delta/\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_0^2}$. Subadditivity of the
$r/2$ power adds at most $B_{\rm mark}\delta$ to the marked cost,
where

$$
B_{\rm mark}=2^{-r/2}\frac{2A}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_0^2}}
=32.89430560995521.
$$

For the residual source branch, every capped output velocity has
norm below $2$. Its normalized squared velocity discrepancy is at
most $16$, its status cost at most one, and its averaged positional
cost is $A^2[(1+b)^2+3(0.1)^2]/2$. Jensen therefore bounds its
$r$-power cost by

$$
C_R^r=\left[17+A^2((1+b)^2+0.03)/2\right]^{r/2},\qquad
C_R^2=18.817146210151844.
$$

On $1\le a\le1.001$, the gate derivative has the proved upper bound

$$
P_*'=\frac{1.1+\varepsilon}{[f(1.001)+\varepsilon]^2}
\frac{0.04(1.001)}{[D(1)^2+0.04]^{3/2}}
=5.157789805744965.
$$

Here $|df/dz|\le1/2$, $D(a)\ge D(1)$, $a\le1.001$,
and $f(a)\ge f(1.001)$ justify each inequality. Thus residual
mass is at most $P_*'\delta$. Summing all three source branches gives

$$
\mathbb E d_{\rm mark}^r\le
q_r(\delta/\sqrt2)^r+C\delta,\qquad
q_r=(1-p(1))(\mathbb EL^2)^{r/2},\quad
C=B_{\rm mark}+P_*'C_R^r=43.63672440240339.
$$

For count normalization $q_r=0.5244889166729909$; for row
normalization $q_r=0.5244803040574045$.
The explicit radius condition
$\delta\le[(1-q_r)/(2C2^{r/2})]^{1/(1-r)}$ yields contraction
factor $(1+q_r)/2$. Its count value is
$2.0991429436504158\,10^{-5}$ and its row value is
$2.099218985095488\,10^{-5}$. Rounding the radius down and the
factor up gives (KUSC.10). As a direct outward-rounded check of
the displayed elementary formulas, 40-digit interval arithmetic gives

$$
0.76172611400244962308886686478095578250014
\le q_r+C2^{r/2}(2.09\,10^{-5})^{1-r}
\le0.76172611400244962308886686478095578250061
$$

for count normalization. This interval is below $0.76225$; the row
factor is smaller because its $\mathbb EL^2$ is smaller.
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:remark} Implemented centered, regional and phase estimates
:label: rem-ku-evaluator-and-obligation

The original pressure coordinate is the common-alive structural
$W=N^{-1}\sum_{I_{11}}|\Delta\delta_{x,i}|^2$.
Its exact within/between decomposition is (KULP.2)--(KULP.4),
and its complete centered preparation is (KUAN.15a)--(KUAN.15d).
The raw fixed-slot quadratic used in Section 7.1 is an auxiliary
comparison; its revival or translation amplification is not a
counterexample to that centered theorem. None of those diagnostics
requires changing the original Keystone method.

`fragile.fractalai.theory.keystone_uniform` evaluates the actual
sampled global standardizers, logistic-product fitness, conditional
source tokens, maximal token coupling, signed cloning variance,
component preparation, both dense B kicks, OU, cap and terminal marks.
It supplies dimension-only Gaussian row-column estimates, uncapped
quadratic, Rastrigin and native Styblinski--Tang moment budgets,
energy-based extinction envelopes and current-survivor inverse-mass
bounds. Equal and near-equal fitness values are included.

`fragile.fractalai.theory.landscape_phase` evaluates native Rastrigin
roots in the proved brackets, exact unrestricted periodic-force jitter
moments, the count B2/OU force correlation, Gaussian box moments,
complete source/jitter/kinetic phase flux, conditional count covariance,
and actual alive within/between variance. The Gaussian exterior remains
in every partition. Its floating outputs are diagnostics of the stated
analytic identities, rather than interval arithmetic certificates.

The evaluated regional bound (KUR.2)--(KUR.4) composes the original
signed source estimate with a population-independent positional
coefficient $\lambda=.7989420407893824$ and explicit conservative
floor $C_{\rm reg}=.20613357968212598$, under its declared source-core
and source-pressure hypotheses. The sharper (KUL.12) retains actual
signed gate, source and kinetic covariances. Centroid/orbit motion,
phase occupation and crossing terms remain separate. The computed
floor is not a theorem that the unchanged noisy population stays
inside that core; its actual departures use the proved Gaussian
flux and terminal-normalization formulas.

The QSD phase balance retains both actual crossing and centered
killing flux, (KLQ.6)--(KLQ.10). Exact signed-coordinate symmetries
supply $h_N(gS)=h_N(S)$ and equal QSD/Doob weights for symmetry-related
phases at every $N$, (KLQ.16). Inequivalent well orbits retain their
own transition and extinction coefficients, including the existing
population-dependent crossing scale. Thus population-independent
regional estimates do not assert population-independent mixing
between distinct attainable phases.

The weighted phase adjugate (KLQ.14) is an exact identity, not an
independent primitive eigenfunction bound. The path comparison
(KLQ.14b) states its independent within-phase oscillation hypothesis
explicitly. The earlier finite-$N$ primitive eigenfunction certificate
remains valid with its displayed population dependence; it cannot
be relabeled as a uniform global certificate. Likewise the
fixed-horizon dense kinetic population limit has the actual
Chapter 19 input hypotheses; it is not the full quantitative
bounded-measurable-test premise of Chapter 06a's growing-horizon rate.

The configuration and analytic conditions are part of each theorem.
Different history, elite, metric, curl, substep-boundary, arithmetic,
reward or force branches require their executed-map estimates.
No configured force, noise law, velocity cap or boundary has been
changed to obtain the regional result.
:::

:::{prf:definition} Actual landing map and the population energy budget
:label: def-kurc-record

Use the complete native reference record of
{prf:ref}`def-ku-conditioning-record`: $d=3$, $D=[-2,2]^3$,
$h=.04$, $\gamma=b_O=\rho=1$, $\nu=.3$, $\sigma_J=\sigma_x=.1$,
$V=2$ and $\alpha_{\rm col}=.5$. All measured rewards/diversities,
standardizations, companion roles, acceptance gates, mandatory revival,
component-Haar rotations, both viscous B stages, unbounded Gaussian
innovations, the original radial cap and terminal marking remain unchanged.
The configured force in this record is

$$
F_k(x)=-2x_k-20\pi\sin(2\pi x_k).
$$

Write $t=h/2$, $c=e^{-\gamma h}$, $b=t(1+c)$,
$\eta=bt$, $\tau^2=t^2q^2+s^2$, and

$$
g(x)=(1-2\eta)x-20\pi\eta\sin(2\pi x),\qquad
V_c=(1+2|\alpha_{\rm col}|)V=4.
\tag{KURC.1}
$$

Freeze the complete measured source/gate/component pattern and its Haar
rotations before jitter. Its actual frozen sources satisfy
$\mu_i\in\overline D$; if $A_i$ is its actual copy/revival indicator,
then $X_i=\mu_i+A_i\sigma_J Z_i^J$. Conditional on the complete
preparation, the actual final positions are

$$
X_i^+=g(X_i)+bU_i+\tau Z_i,\qquad
U=W_XV^{\rm col}.
\tag{KURC.2}
$$

The $Z_i$ are independent standard $d$-dimensional Gaussians. The first
viscous matrix uses every realized jitter. In both normalizations it is
stochastic at $t\nu=.006$, so $|U_i|\le V_c$. Both $U$ and its row
correlations remain in the actual law.

For every realization of preparation,

$$
\|U\|_{2,N}\le E_\nu,
\qquad E_\nu=\begin{cases}
V,&\text{count normalization},\\
\min\{V_c,V(1-t\nu+t\nu\sqrt C)\},&\text{row normalization},
\end{cases}
\tag{KURC.3}
$$

where $C$ is any proved upper bound for the nonself Gaussian-row column
mass. The singleton has zero viscosity and uses $E_\nu=V$ in either mode.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The original two A drifts give $X^+=X+b[W_XV^{\rm col}+tF(X)]$
plus $tq\xi^O+s\xi^x$. B2 and the radial velocity cap leave these
positions unchanged; their actual effects on the retained velocity have
not been substituted. The independent row Gaussian sums have covariance
$\tau^2 I_d$, proving (KURC.2).

For any frozen connected component, write its entering velocities as
$\bar v+\widetilde v_i$. Orthogonality of its actual common Haar matrix
gives

$$
\sum_i|\bar v+\alpha_{\rm col}O\widetilde v_i|^2
=n|\bar v|^2+\alpha_{\rm col}^2\sum_i|\widetilde v_i|^2
\le\sum_i|v_i|^2.
$$

This is a component identity and therefore survives the entire measured
graph law. Every retained entering speed is capped by $V$, so the
collision energy is at most $V^2$. The count matrix contracts the
unweighted normalized second moment. For the row matrix,
$\|P_X\|_{2\to2}\le\sqrt C$ follows from its row sums one and column
sums at most $C$, by rowwise Jensen followed by column summation. Thus
$\|W_X\|_{2\to2}\le1-t\nu+t\nu\sqrt C$. The rowwise bound also
gives $\|U\|_{2,N}\le V_c$. This proves (KURC.3) without a degree floor,
independent collision rows, or a maximum Gaussian over $N$. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:lemma} Monotone Rastrigin landing geometry
:label: lem-kurc-monotone-map

The actual reference map is odd, globally strictly increasing, and maps
$[-2,2]$ into itself. More precisely,

$$
g'(x)\ge1-\eta(2+40\pi^2)=.6887959111964013>0,
\qquad g(2)=2-4\eta=1.9968627368973564.
\tag{KURC.4}
$$

Set $L=2$, $R=bV_c<L$ and define the unrestricted accepted-row floor

$$
p_1=\left[\int_{\mathbb R}
 \ell_{L-R,\tau}\bigl(g(L+\sigma_J z)\bigr)\phi(z)\,dz\right]^d,
\qquad
\ell_{a,\tau}(m)=\Phi((a-m)/\tau)-\Phi((-a-m)/\tau).
\tag{KURC.5}
$$

Every accepted row has an own-jitter-dependent lower landing probability
$G_i(Z_i^J)$ with conditional mean at least $p_1$, independently of the
other rows' jitters. This refers to lower indicators or lower conditional
probabilities; the actual landing probabilities need not be independent
before full preparation.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Differentiate the actual sine formula to obtain (KURC.4). Oddness and
monotonicity, together with its endpoint value, give the asserted image
of the source interval. For each realized $U_i$, the cube
$[-L+R,L-R]^d$ translated by $bU_i$ is contained in $D$ because
$|bU_i|\le R$. Hence the actual row landing probability is at least

$$
G_i(Z_i^J)=\prod_{k=1}^d
\ell_{L-R,\tau}\bigl(g(\mu_{i,k}+\sigma_J Z_{i,k}^J)\bigr).
\tag{KURC.6}
$$

The function $x\mapsto\ell_{L-R,\tau}(g(x))$ is even and
nonincreasing on $x\ge0$. Its superlevel sets are centered intervals.
The probability that a Gaussian of fixed variance and mean $\mu$ lies
in any such interval is even and nonincreasing in $|\mu|$: differentiate
its two CDF endpoints. Layer-cake integration proves the same assertion
for the convolution in (KURC.5). Its minimum for $|\mu|\le L$ is
therefore attained at $\mu=L$. Conditional independent coordinate
jitters give $\mathbb E G_i\ge p_1$. No cutoff has been imposed on
either Gaussian, and the force at every jittered position is the actual
configured sine force. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:lemma} Convex energy profile for an unaccepted row
:label: lem-kurc-convex-box-profile

Put $k=b/\tau$, $Q(z)=1-\Phi(z)$ and

$$
\epsilon_D=\exp[-2L^2/\tau^2],\qquad
\psi(r)=(1-\epsilon_D)^d
 \left[Q\left(\frac{kr}{\sqrt d}\right)\right]^d.
\tag{KURC.7}
$$

For every unaccepted row of the actual prepared array,
its conditional probability of being alive is at least $\psi(|U_i|)$.
Moreover $e\mapsto\psi(\sqrt e)$ is decreasing and convex on
$[0,\infty)$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
For this row $X_i=\mu_i\in\overline D$, so (KURC.4) gives
$|g(X_{i,k})|\le L$. Its conditional landing probability is consequently
at least the product of interval probabilities at absolute means
$L+b|U_{i,k}|$. If $z=k|U_{i,k}|$ and $A=2L/\tau$, that interval
probability equals $Q(z)-Q(z+A)$. Direct translation in the Gaussian
integral gives

$$
Q(z+A)=e^{-A^2/2}\int_z^\infty e^{-Au}\phi(u)\,du
\le e^{-A^2/2}Q(z),\qquad z\ge0.
\tag{KURC.8}
$$

For completeness the elementary identity

$$
Q(z)=\frac1\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}
 e^{-z^2/(2\sin^2\theta)}\,d\theta,
\qquad z\ge0,
\tag{KURC.9}
$$

follows by differentiating for $z>0$: substitute
$u=\cot\theta$ in the derivative to obtain $-\phi(z)$, then use
the value $1/2$ at zero. Thus $e\mapsto Q(k\sqrt e)$ is a positive
mixture of exponentials in $e$ and is log-convex. Jensen applied to
its logarithm, with $e_k=|U_{i,k}|^2$, gives

$$
\prod_k Q(k|U_{i,k}|)
\ge \left[Q(k|U_i|/\sqrt d)\right]^d.
$$

Together with (KURC.8) this proves the row floor. Finally the right
side of (KURC.7), as a function of $e=r^2$, is itself a positive
$d$-fold integral of exponentials in $e$, using (KURC.9). It is
therefore decreasing and convex, including at zero by continuity.
$\square$
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Population-uniform survival with every gate pattern retained
:label: thm-kurc-actual-global-survival

Define, with the continuous convention $H(0)=p_1$,

$$
H(u)=u\psi(E_\nu/\sqrt u)+(1-u)p_1,\qquad
a_* =\min_{0\le u\le1}H(u)>0.
\tag{KURC.10}
$$

For every nonextinct entering state, every population $N\ge1$,
and $\theta\ge0$, the actual terminal alive count obeys

$$
\mathbb E_S e^{-\theta M^+}
\le[1-(1-e^{-\theta})a_*]^N,
\qquad
\Pr_S(M^+=0)\le(1-a_*)^N,
\qquad \mathbb E_S(M^+/N)\ge a_*.
\tag{KURC.11}
$$

This is a Laplace-transform bound and its displayed consequences.
Full stochastic binomial domination is not inferred from this transform.
No lower bound on a fitness difference, acceptance frequency or source
phase mass is a premise.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Condition on the complete pre-jitter information from (KURC.2), and
let $uN$ be its number of unaccepted rows. Conditional on every jitter,
the actual terminal indicators are independent Bernoulli trials with
parameters $p_i$. Put $T=1-e^{-\theta}$. The conditional transform is
$\prod_i(1-Tp_i)$.

For the unaccepted subset, (KURC.3), the previous lemma and energy
Jensen imply, pathwise in every jitter,

$$
\frac1{uN}\sum_{i:A_i=0}p_i
\ge \psi\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac1{uN}\sum_{i:A_i=0}|U_i|^2}\right)
\ge\psi(E_\nu/\sqrt u).
\tag{KURC.12}
$$

Concavity of $\log(1-Tp)$ bounds their product by
$[1-T\psi(E_\nu/\sqrt u)]^{uN}$. This is a deterministic envelope
independent of all jitters, so it can be pulled out before integrating
the accepted-row factors. Replace each accepted factor by
$1-TG_i(Z_i^J)$ from (KURC.6). These replacement factors depend only
on their own independent jitters. Their product integrates to at most
$(1-Tp_1)^{(1-u)N}$, while every measured gate and Haar correlation
has remained frozen. Weighted AM--GM now gives

$$
\mathbb E[e^{-\theta M^+}\mid\text{pre-jitter information}]
\le(1-TH(u))^N\le(1-Ta_*)^N.
$$

Average the original measured pattern law. Letting $\theta\to\infty$
gives extinction, and the right derivative at zero gives the first
moment. Positivity of $a_*$ follows from continuity and positivity of
both endpoints and every interior value of $H$. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:corollary} Chernoff, inverse-alive and QSD survival consequences
:label: cor-kurc-conditioning-consequences

For any proved $0<a\le a_*$, put $c_0=(1-\log2)/2$. Then

$$
\Pr_S(M^+/N<a/2)\le e^{-c_0aN},\qquad
Q_N1(S)\ge1-(1-a)^N.
\tag{KURC.13}
$$

After conditioning on actual survival, for every $r>0$,

$$
\mathbb E_S[(N/M^+)^r\mid M^+>0]
\le (2/a)^r+\left(\frac r{e c_0a}\right)^r.
\tag{KURC.14}
$$

The same bounds hold after mixing an arbitrary entering survivor law.
Every compatible QSD has survival eigenvalue
$\alpha_N\ge1-(1-a)^N$, and the one-step survivor denominator obeys

$$
C_{{\rm surv},N}\le\frac1{1-(1-a)^N}\le\frac1a.
\tag{KURC.15}
$$

:::

:::{prf:proof}
Use (KURC.11) at $\theta=\log2$ and Markov's inequality;
$(1-a/2)^N\le e^{-aN/2}$ gives (KURC.13). If the actual extinction
probability is $\delta$, subtract it before conditioning:
$\Pr(0<M^+<aN/2)\le e^{-c_0aN}-\delta$.
Division by $1-\delta$ can only decrease the upper bound
$e^{-c_0aN}$. Split the inverse moment at $M^+=aN/2$ and use
$(N/M^+)^r\le N^r$ on its surviving complement. The supremum of
$N^re^{-c_0aN}$ over positive real $N$ is
$(r/(ec_0a))^r$. Integration against a QSD proves the eigenvalue
bound; (KURC.15) follows directly. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:lemma} Reference coefficients certified without changing the noise
:label: lem-kurc-certified-reference

For the reference record one may use, for every $N\ge1$,

$$
\boxed{a_{
\rm count}=2\cdot10^{-6},\qquad
a_{\rm row}=7\cdot10^{-11}.}
\tag{KURC.16}
$$

The row singleton also admits $a_{\rm count}$. Thus the uniform
survivor multipliers in (KURC.15) are respectively at most
$500000$ and $10^{11}/7$. These conservative finite constants are
not claims that the true survivor probability is this small.

Here is a finite certificate for the accepted coefficient. Let
$z_j=-8+j/25$, $j=0,\ldots,400$, $L_*=L-bV_c$, and set

$$
\underline p_1=
\left[\sum_{j=1}^{400}
 [\Phi(z_j)-\Phi(z_{j-1})]
 \ell_{L_*,\tau}(g(L+\sigma_Jz_j))\right]^3.
\tag{KURC.17}
$$

Because $L+\sigma_Jz\in[1.2,2.8]$ on this interval, its integrand
apart from the Gaussian density is decreasing. Consequently
$p_1\ge\underline p_1>1.41317461517\cdot10^{-5}$.
Take $r_0=103/50$ and write

$$
\widetilde\psi(r)=[Q(kr/\sqrt3)]^3,\qquad
B_0=\widetilde\psi'(r_0)/(2r_0),\qquad
A_0=\widetilde\psi(r_0)-B_0r_0^2.
\tag{KURC.18}
$$

Explicit interval evaluations give

$$
\begin{aligned}
1.35529853339420\cdot10^{-5}<A_0
 &<1.35529853339421\cdot10^{-5},\\
2.05146788376870\cdot10^{-6}<A_0+4B_0
 &<2.05146788376872\cdot10^{-6}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{KURC.19}
$$

For row normalization, the same existing column-shell proof (KUK.7)
admits the sharper finite upper bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
C^{(M)}={}&2e^2+9^3\left[1+
 \sum_{m=0}^{M-1}
 \left(2e^{-a r^{2m}}+e^{-\beta r^m}\right)
 +2e^{-a r^{2M}}
       \left(1+\frac1{2a(\log r)r^{2M}}\right)
 +e^{-\beta r^M}
       \left(1+\frac1{\beta(\log r)r^M}\right)\right],\\
&a=35/128,\qquad\beta=3/8,\qquad r=5/4.
\end{aligned}
\tag{KURC.20}
$$

At $M=40$ this gives $C^{(40)}<7188$. Use the explicit larger
integer $C=7188$ in (KURC.3). Then

$$
E_\nu=2(.994+.006\sqrt{7188})=3.005384882922879,
\qquad \widetilde\psi(E_\nu)>7.45304452175\cdot10^{-11}.
\tag{KURC.21}
$$

:::

:::{prf:proof}
The right-endpoint sum (KURC.17) is a lower integral sum with exact
Gaussian masses, discarding only nonnegative contributions outside
$[-8,8]$. Convexity in energy gives the supporting line
$\widetilde\psi(\sqrt e)\ge A_0+B_0e$, with $B_0<0$.
For count normalization $E_\nu^2=4$. If $u$ is the unaccepted
fraction, the same energy argument therefore gives the lower rate

$$
(1-\epsilon_D)^3(A_0u+4B_0)+(1-u)\underline p_1
\ge(1-\epsilon_D)^3(A_0+4B_0),
$$

since $\underline p_1>(1-\epsilon_D)^3A_0$.
Also $\log\epsilon_D=-19259.624837630152<-200\log10$.
Equations (KURC.19) prove its lower bound $2\cdot10^{-6}$.

For (KURC.20), retain the first $M$ terms of the original column
series. Each remaining decreasing summand is bounded by its first
term plus its integral. Substitute $v=a r^{2x}$ or
$v=\beta r^x$, and use
$\int_z^\infty e^{-v}\,dv/v\le e^{-z}/z$.
This proves the exact expression before numerical evaluation.
For row normalization Jensen alone bounds the rate by
$u\psi(E_\nu/\sqrt u)+(1-u)\underline p_1$.
Its perspective term is convex, and its derivative at $u=1$ is
$\psi(E_\nu)-E_\nu\psi'(E_\nu)/2<1.42\cdot10^{-9}
<\underline p_1$. Hence the minimum is at $u=1$.
Equation (KURC.21) and $\epsilon_D<10^{-200}$ prove the stated
row coefficient.

All quoted enclosures can be checked by finite elementary interval
arithmetic. One explicit Gaussian-CDF recipe is the integrated
exponential series

$$
\Phi(x)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \sum_{n=0}^{400}\frac{(-1)^n x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)2^n n!}
 +R_{400}(x),\qquad |R_{400}(x)|<10^{-200},\quad |x|\le8.
$$

The alternating remainder is bounded by its next term because
the summands decrease after $n\ge32$; that next term at $8$
is below $10^{-200}$. Outside $[-8,8]$, use
$0<Q(x)\le\phi(x)/x$ for $x\ge8$ and symmetry. This tail
bound is at most $6.4\cdot10^{-16}$ and suffices for every
enclosure displayed above. Evaluate the elementary coefficients
and arguments by interval exponentials/sines and exact integer
factorials. Thus the certificate concerns the original integrals,
not a clipped Gaussian simulation. $\square$
:::

:::{prf:remark} Values from the exact one-dimensional optimization
:label: rem-kurc-sharper-values

The unrestricted integral (KURC.5) is approximately

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{normalization}&E_\nu&\text{minimizing }u&a_*\\\hline
\text{count}&2&.9634116560416744&2.17483625744411\cdot10^{-6}\\
\text{row}&3.005361285498921&1&7.455154672651456\cdot10^{-11}
\end{array}
\tag{KURC.22}
$$

These are diagnostic rounded values. The completely certified
