constant or absorbed into a newly chosen face coefficient.
This identifies a local curvature energy on the actual
native line/complement connection support. It is distinct
from both the executed scalar ray interaction action and
an unrestricted independent $SU(3)$ field ensemble.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Write the area bivector as
$L_{ab}(u,v)=u_av_b-u_bv_a$, $a<b$.
Then $\mathcal F(u,v)=\sum_{a<b}\mathcal F_{ab}L_{ab}$.
The original Poisson Delaunay/CSR cycle law is equivariant
under every orthogonal spatial map. Its area vectors
$u\times v$ therefore have an invariant second-moment
matrix after summing the rooted cycles.
Coordinate sign reflections make off-diagonal entries
zero; coordinate permutations make all diagonal entries
equal. Their trace is the sum of squared areas.
Consequently
$E\sum L_{ab}L_{cd}=c_{\rm Del}\mathbf1_{\{(a,b)=(c,d)\}}$
at intensity one. No independence of different faces
is used. The star moments in Section 2 show finiteness;
the explicit positive tetrahedron event in Section 5
shows $c_{\rm Del}>0$.

At intensity $\zeta>0$, scaling all spatial vectors
by $\zeta^{-1/3}$ turns the original unit-intensity
Poisson star into its intensity-$\zeta$ star.
The area products therefore scale by $\zeta^{-4/3}$,
with cycle multiplicities unchanged. Expansion of
the Frobenius square gives
$E_{\Pi_\zeta}\sum\|\mathcal F(u,v)\|_F^2
=c_{\rm Del}\zeta^{-4/3}\sum_{a<b}\|\mathcal F_{ab}\|_F^2$.
Multiply by the original root density $p(x)$ and
the proved coefficient $1/24$ in (NSWT.8).
This gives exactly (NSWT.14).
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact original common-source action variation and its limit
:label: thm-nswt-common-source-variation

Use the same full-slot composite channel with unit
coefficients and fixed calibration, and let $f$ be
continuously differentiable with compact support in
a strict chart. Its support enlargement must pass
(NSWT.1). For any fixed real vector $a$, make the
original simultaneous Gaussian source shift
$G_i\mapsto G_i+\theta a$ in every original row.
Retain every resulting force, cap, final state and
terminal status in the complete executed record.
Let $A_N^f$ denote the original action observable
of Section 4. Then the exact finite-$N$ identities are

$$
A_N^f(G+\theta a)=A_N^{f(\,\cdot+\theta s_0a)}(G),
$$

$$
\left.\partial_\theta EA_N^f(G+\theta a)\right|_0
=s_0 EA_N^{a\cdot\nabla f}(G)
=E\left[A_N^f(G)\sum_i a\cdot G_i\right].
\tag{NSWT.15}
$$

The same native source first variation has the limit

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}E\left[A_N^f\sum_i a\cdot G_i\right]
=
\frac{s_0c_{\rm Del}}{24}
 \int (a\cdot\nabla f)(x)p(x)^{-1/3}
                    \sum_{b<c}\|\mathcal F_{\kappa,bc}(x)\|_F^2\,dx .
\tag{NSWT.16}
$$

This is the original collective Gaussian source score
and its local curvature-energy response, with all
same-record faces retained. The source changes the
complete original transition, rather than rephasing
an independently supplied edge.
An additional final-alive or source deletion readout
retains its own boundary/mask variation; it is not
assigned this full-slot identity.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
In this original consensus transition the shifted
pre-B2 coordinates are
$z_i^\theta=z_i+q\theta a$ and
$Y_i^\theta=Y_i+s_0\theta a$.
Every original spatial difference, viscous velocity
difference and Gaussian weight is identical.
Thus both the count and the nonself row B2 force
are unchanged exactly. The recorded B2 colors change
by the common unitary diagonal matrix
$D_\theta=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\kappa q\theta a})$,
so $P_i^\theta=D_\theta P_iD_\theta^\dagger$.
Their exact canonical endpoint transports transform
by that same conjugation. Every composite loop and
its unitary Wilson defect is therefore unchanged.
The availability norm/overlap mask is also unchanged.
The full-slot Delaunay geometry is merely translated;
its incidences, orientations and unit coefficients
are identical. The actually executed final potential
kick, cap and terminal status may change; those
retained outputs do not enter this particular
matched-B2 full-slot composite observable.
This proves the first equality in (NSWT.15).

Differentiate only the translated $f$.
For each fixed $N$ the deterministic polynomial
bound (NSWT.9) gives integrable domination.
Gaussian change of variables in all original sources
proves its equal score expectation; its linear score
is unbounded and retains its full Gaussian law.
Section 4 and (NSWT.14), applied to the continuous
compact test $a\cdot\nabla f$, now give (NSWT.16)
without taking a limit of a growing-$N$ score by
an unjustified uniform-integrability claim.

Equivalently the shifted limiting connection is
$D_\theta P_\kappa(x-s_0\theta a)D_\theta^\dagger$,
and its curvature is conjugated and translated.
The native density becomes $p(x-s_0\theta a)$.
Changing variables in its original curvature
energy leaves precisely the translated $f$
whose derivative was just computed. Thus the
finite source calculation and the local energy
variation refer to the same native supported law.
:::

## 2_fractal_set/21_native_spatial_action_variation.md

:::{prf:definition} Complete native ray-action data
:label: def-nsav-complete-register

Retain every execution and consumed observation field of
{prf:ref}`def-nspc-complete-register` and
{prf:ref}`def-npg-complete-record`: algorithm/variant, landscape and
provider, all fitness and normalization parameters, donor pools and
their simultaneous assignment law, clone gates, revival, jitter,
component collision marks, both kicks, independent real Gaussian
innovations, domain and boundary schedule, actual cap, history
coverage, event identities, finite-value/eligible masks, precision,
budgets and error policies. The positive results below specify included
parameter regimes of this complete record. They do not replace the
unchanged positive-final-noise reference by those regimes.

The algorithm tag for every positive dense count/row theorem is
the EXISTING canonical real-coordinate dense viscous gas. Its
force is the one in Rust `QftExecutionConfig.viscosity`, evaluated
by `src/kinetic.rs`'s `recorded_force`: every eligible nonself
Gaussian pair is retained; count normalization uses eligible
count, and `row_normalized=true` uses its actual positive row
mass, with no $10^{-12}$ denominator floor. Its only zero-mass
branch is the executed zero-force branch. Graph-viscosity
feedback is not configured in this tag. The original archive
ray instrument below applies to this algorithm's recorded states.
The Python CSR/Delaunay force variant has its different graph
and mass-floor parameters. In particular its $N=2,d=3$ empty
graph fallback is not assigned this dense two-row force or swap.
Floating Gaussian underflow, finite streams and numerical
error branches keep their actual zero-mass/rounded outcomes;
the global exact row cancellations below concern the specified
real-coordinate execution tag, where $K_\rho>0$.

The literal action is the archive instrument in
`algorithmic-gas/crates/algorithmic-gas/src/physics/qft/run_observables.rs`,
experiments $1,11,15,23,24,29$. It constructs, from the actual
`before` and `final_population` arrays,

$$
r_e=\frac{x_e+iv_e}{\sqrt{|x_e|^2+|v_e|^2}},\qquad
\ell_{ab}=\frac{r_a^\dagger r_b}{|r_a^\dagger r_b|},\qquad
L_T=\ell_{ab}\ell_{bc}\ell_{ca},\qquad W_T=1-\Re L_T.
\tag{NSAV.1}
$$

The original eligible test uses `include_truncated`; the ray norm
must strictly exceed $\delta_r=10^{-12}$ and be finite, and each
normalized overlap must strictly exceed $\delta_\ell=10^{-10}$.
Unavailable triangles are counted and omitted from the loop/action
arrays. An unavailable phase is not assigned a value by this instrument.
The graph is the actual `FractalSet::from_archive` graph: a current
companion produces the ordered triangle
$(\mathrm{pre}\ i,\mathrm{final}\ i,\mathrm{pre}\ j)$,
with CST, IA and reversed IG boundary. IA and this triangle exist
also when the recorded clone was not accepted. Identical distance and
cloning triangles are deduplicated, with both channels retained.
Historical/unresolved/self sources retain the literal graph rules;
they are not replaced by current numerical slots. There is no CSR
three-final-vertex triangle in this archive action.

Each returned $W_T$ has its literal unit coefficient. The output
contains per-face values rather than a newly weighted probability
density. A sum of these actual values below is explicitly such an
observable. The `angle` control only chooses the local rephasing
comparison, and the numerical phase-variation comparison uses the
fixed step $10^{-5}$. Neither changes the original $L_T$ or supplies
an algorithmic source. The matched B2 color coefficient
$\kappa=m\ell_0/\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$, physical coordinate units,
and a covariance-metric ridge do not enter (NSAV.1). Their own
instruments remain in the complete record; they are not inserted
into this raw-component ray formula.

The original cap is
$C_V(w)=Vw/(V+|w|)$ for its configured finite $V>0$, and
$C_\infty(w)=w$ when `velocity_cap=None`.
The results using real densities and conditional Gaussian fibers
refer to the real independent-Gaussian execution convention.
Fixed-stream and rounded executions retain their actual pushforward
laws and are not assigned these continuous densities.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Literal first-step support and the terminal ray field at origin consensus
:label: thm-nsav-consensus-ray-support

Use the exact origin-consensus, quadratic count/row, $d=3$,
$\sigma_x=0$, $q,t,\rho,\nu>0$ branch of
{prf:ref}`def-nspc-complete-register`. The original first-update
interaction-ray action has empty support for every $N$:
every triangle contains an unavailable pre ray. This holds even
where the actual terminal B2 color projector is available and its
derived spatial curvature is non-Abelian.

The actual final velocity at a terminal node is

$$
u_i=C_V\big[(1-t^2\lambda)z_i+tF_N(z_i)\big],\qquad
Y_i=tz_i.
\tag{NSAV.2}
$$

On every compact spatial chart separated from $y=0$, the evaluated
terminal-ray field converges in $C^1$ in probability to

$$
r_{\mathrm{ray}}(y)
 =\frac{1+i a_V(|y|)}{\sqrt{1+a_V(|y|)^2}}\frac{y}{|y|},
\qquad P_{\mathrm{ray}}(y)=\frac{yy^T}{|y|^2},
\tag{NSAV.3}
$$

where $u(y)=a_V(|y|)y$ is evaluated from (NSAV.2) using
the actual count/row limit of {prf:ref}`thm-nspc-native-force-interpolant`.
Explicitly, before the cap,

$$
a_\infty(R)=\frac{1-t^2\lambda}{t}-\nu r_0
 \begin{cases}a_0e^{-R^2/(2B)},&\mathrm{count},\\1,&\mathrm{row},\end{cases}
\quad
a_V(R)=\frac{V a_\infty(R)}{V+R|a_\infty(R)|}.
\tag{NSAV.4}
$$

All ray norms and terminal eligible marks retain their actual
threshold/domain tests. On a strict available interior chart the
terminal ray connection has

$$
A_{\mathrm{ray}}=d\arctan a_V(|y|),\qquad
F_{\mathrm{ray}}=0.
\tag{NSAV.5}
$$

Thus the same record gives the exact comparison
$F_{\mathrm{ray}}=0$ versus the explicit noncommuting B2 color
curvature of {prf:ref}`thm-nspc-noncommuting-curvature` when
$\kappa\ne0$. Their vectors and measured edge maps are different.
No curvature coefficient from the B2 color connection can be
assigned to this literal ray action in this branch.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Every pre state has $x_i=v_i=0$, so its original ray norm is
zero. Each archive interaction triangle has two pre vertices;
the overlap lookup therefore fails for every such triangle.
No selected companion, positive terminal color or later cap can
change this literal missing pre-event ray.

The second kick is evaluated at $Y=tz$ with potential force
$-\lambda Y$ and the original viscous force $F_N$.
The unchanged terminal cap gives (NSAV.2). The force functions
converge in $C^2$ on compact sets. The map $C_V$ is $C^1$ on
all real velocity space with continuous bounded first derivative,
including at zero. Consequently its evaluated velocity function
converges in $C^1$ on each compact set. Ray normalization is
smooth wherever its norm is separated from zero; on a chart
separated from $y=0$ the norm is at least $|y|$. Thus its native
evaluated ray map has the claimed $C^1$ convergence. This does
not impose twice differentiable cap behavior at $w=0$.

The count/row force limits are real scalar multiples of $y$,
so the terminal capped velocity is exactly the real radial
vector in (NSAV.4). Factoring its complex scalar from
$y+iu(y)$ proves (NSAV.3). Put $n=y/|y|$ and
$\theta=\arctan a_V(|y|)$. Since $n^Tdn=0$,
$-i(e^{i\theta}n)^\dagger d(e^{i\theta}n)=d\theta$.
Its curvature vanishes. Equivalently the line projector is
real radial and the scalar Berry two-form
$2\Im[(D_an)^TD_bn]$ is identically zero. The statement
remains valid across a zero of $a_\infty$, by the proved $C^1$
regularity or this projector formula. The non-Abelian B2
color curvature was calculated from a different projector
$[-n\odot e^{i\kappa y/t}][-n\odot e^{i\kappa y/t}]^\dagger$;
the comparison follows from their displayed exact formulas.
:::

:::{prf:corollary} Available shifted-consensus archive faces are exactly flat
:label: cor-nsav-shifted-consensus-face

For any originally eligible entering consensus
$x_i=x_*,v_i=v_*$ with available common pre ray, every
resolved current archive interaction triangle has
$L_T=1$ and $W_T=0$, for every executed innovation,
clone/collision/kick/cap outcome and parameter value.
Its smooth-stratum actual source variation is zero.
The complete available-face mask/count may still depend
on the innovation and retains its own weak source response.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Both pre-event rays in a current triangle are the same
unit vector $r_*$. If its final ray is $r$, its product
is $(r_*^\dagger r/|r_*^\dagger r|)
(r^\dagger r_*/|r^\dagger r_*|)(r_*^\dagger r_*)=1$.
This uses neither a clone-acceptance restriction nor a
post velocity approximation. Its derivative on an available
branch is zero. Crossing an unavailable overlap or final
eligible mark changes support, so the mask/count conclusion
is kept separate.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact ray-face derivative and original Gaussian weak score
:label: thm-nsav-native-source-variation

On any originally available face and smooth source branch,
let $Q_{ab}=r_a^\dagger r_b$. For its actual simultaneous
source tangent $\delta$,

$$
\delta\Theta_T=
 \Im\sum_{(a,b)\in\partial T}
 \frac{(\delta r_a)^\dagger r_b+r_a^\dagger\delta r_b}{Q_{ab}},
\qquad
\delta W_T=\sin\Theta_T\,\delta\Theta_T.
\tag{NSAV.6}
$$

Here $\Theta_T=\arg L_T$ may be locally lifted; its
formula is independent of that lift. At a persisted slot
with fixed original real pre rays $a,b$, it is equivalently

$$
\delta\Theta_T=
\Im\left[
 \frac{a\cdot(\delta Y+i\delta u)}{a\cdot(Y+iu)}+
 \frac{b\cdot(\delta Y-i\delta u)}{b\cdot(Y-iu)}
\right].
\tag{NSAV.7}
$$

For a fixed complete pre-O preparation on a full-eligible
smooth quadratic $\sigma_x=0$ B2 branch, write $z_i=cv_{1i}+qG_i$,
$Y_i=p_i+tz_i$, and
$w_i=z_i-t\lambda Y_i+tF_i(Y,z)$. The ORIGINAL source
$G_i\mapsto G_i+\theta f_i$ has

$$
\delta z_i=qf_i,\quad \delta Y_i=tqf_i,\quad
\delta w_i=(1-t^2\lambda)qf_i+t\delta F_i,\quad
\delta u_i=DC_V(w_i)\delta w_i.
\tag{NSAV.8}
$$

Put $\Delta z_{ij}=z_j-z_i$, $\Delta Y_{ij}=Y_j-Y_i$
and $K_{ij}=e^{-|\Delta Y_{ij}|^2/(2\rho^2)}$.
The fully coupled count derivative is
$\delta F_i=(\nu/N)\sum_{j\ne i}K_{ij}
[\delta\Delta z_{ij}-\rho^{-2}\Delta z_{ij}
(\Delta Y_{ij}\cdot\delta\Delta Y_{ij})]$.
For row normalization replace $N$ by
$D_i=\sum_{j\ne i}K_{ij}$ and add
$-F_i\delta D_i/D_i$, with
$\delta D_i=-\rho^{-2}\sum_{j\ne i}K_{ij}
\Delta Y_{ij}\cdot\delta\Delta Y_{ij}$.
Thus all simultaneous $\delta z_j$ and actual prepared
position differences are kept. Other fixed eligibility
strata retain their literal masked row sums. For $w\ne0$,

$$
DC_V(w)=\frac{V}{V+|w|}I
 -\frac{Vww^T}{|w|(V+|w|)^2},\qquad DC_V(0)=I.
\tag{NSAV.9}
$$

For every bounded measurable observable $O$ of the COMPLETE
executed output, including all retained mask/retessellation
branches, its original weak source identity is

$$
\left.\partial_\theta E O(D(G+\theta f))\right|_0
 =E\left[O(D(G))\sum_i f_i\cdot G_i\right].
\tag{NSAV.10}
$$

The exact coarse likelihood score is
$E[\sum_i f_i\cdot G_i\mid D]$. Formula (NSAV.6)
is the actual smooth-stratum action-observable variation;
it is not a replacement for this coarse score or for
its threshold boundary contributions. The original
experiment-24 comparison perturbs one supplied edge
phase, for which its derivative is $\Im L_T$; that
comparison is distinct from the coupled source (NSAV.8).
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The differential of the argument of any nonzero complex
$Q$ is $\Im(dQ/Q)$. Its positive real modulus
normalization contributes no argument, so the loop
product rule gives (NSAV.6). Positive normalization of
the final ray also contributes no argument. The two
variable overlaps with real fixed pre rays are
$a\cdot(Y+iu)$ and $b\cdot(Y-iu)$, proving (NSAV.7).
The unchanged BAOAB update and original radial cap
give (NSAV.8)--(NSAV.9) by differentiation. In particular
the capped derivative includes its radial term; the
viscous derivative includes every other source row and
the row denominator derivative.

Freeze the complete preparation, including its actual
cloning, jitter and shared collision marks. Change variables
in the independent standard Gaussian integral for
$G+\theta f$. The shifted density is
$\varphi(G-\theta f)$, whose derivative at zero is
$\varphi(G)\sum_i f_i\cdot G_i$. Its local derivatives
are bounded by an integrable Gaussian times a polynomial,
so bounded $O$ gives differentiation under the integral.
The observation executes the same complete native map
under the shifted source, including all hard branches.
Average over the unchanged preparation law. Disintegration
against $D$ gives its coarse score. For an independent
edge-phase perturbation $L_T\mapsto e^{i\theta}L_T$,
direct differentiation gives $\partial_\theta W_T=\Im L_T$;
it does not differentiate the force, positions or cap.
:::

:::{prf:definition} Original two-walker small-thermostat regime
:label: def-nsav-two-face-regime

Use the existing $N=2,d=3$ quadratic gas with its included
$\lambda=0$ landscape, zero entering velocities and originally
eligible positions

$$
x_1=e_1,\qquad x_2=(e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2.
\tag{NSAV.11}
$$

Both current companion channels use their existing nonself
count-one current pools. For two eligible walkers the other
walker is their only possible companion, under their actual
configured sampler. Retain its report, including both graph
channels. No historical/external source pool is substituted.
Use the existing end-of-step boundary schedule and a domain
whose interior contains both points, for example the unchanged
box $[-2,2]^3$. Geometry is passive; no externally unequal
volume/fitness provider is fed back into this regime.

The constant landscape gives equal rewards, and the unique
nonself distance in either direction gives equal diversity.
Every configured well-defined common fitness transform and
normalizer therefore gives equal fitness. The original
positive-difference acceptance rule makes both living gates
exactly zero. There is no accepted clone or recipient jitter;
its configured $\sigma_J$, the collision coefficient and Haar
marks remain in the complete record. Every entering velocity
is zero, so every component collision leaves them zero.
Both first kicks are zero. Mandatory revival is not invoked.

Keep $h>0$, $t=h/2$, $\nu,\rho>0$, friction and the final
velocity cap fixed, with $\sigma_x=0$. Let the ORIGINAL
thermostat amplitude tend to zero through its existing
parameter $q>0$:

$$
q=b_O\sqrt{(1-e^{-2\gamma h})/(2\gamma)}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{NSAV.12}
$$

with its continuous $\gamma=0$ formula $q=b_O\sqrt h$.
The consumed thermostat tag here is Rust's existing
independent `NoiseGeometry::Isotropic` factor
`FactorValues::Constant { values: [b_O] }` and
`KineticKind::Baoab.friction`. The validator allows
$\gamma=0$ independently of $b_O>0$, and its O code
uses the displayed continuous limit. A different
manual/automatic inverse-temperature tag that imposes
$q^2=(1-c^2)/\beta_{\mathrm{eff}}$ retains that relation;
it does not have $\gamma=0,q>0$ at finite positive
$\beta_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
This changes an existing configured parameter within the
same kernel, not the noise law or a force rule. The original
independent Gaussian vectors are $G_1,G_2\sim N(0,I_3)$.
The actual positions and B2 input velocities are exactly
$Y_i=x_i+tqG_i$, $z_i=qG_i$.

Put

$$
K_0=e^{-(2-\sqrt2)/(2\rho^2)},\qquad
a=\begin{cases}t\nu K_0/2,&\mathrm{count},\\t\nu,&\mathrm{row},\end{cases}
\quad D_a=(1-a)^2+a^2,
$$

$$
L_1=-e_2,\qquad L_2=(-e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2.
\tag{NSAV.13}
$$

The literal graph has two distinct ordered interaction faces,
one at each future slot. Distance/cloning channel duplication
does not count either triangle twice. The pre rays and their
cross overlap have strict original threshold margins.
The full thermostat law and final alive/overlap masks are
retained; no exceptional Gaussian source is clipped.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Joint original ray-face fluctuation, action and weak source limit
:label: thm-nsav-two-face-action

In {prf:ref}`def-nsav-two-face-regime`, let $\Theta_{i,q}$
be the principal phase of its original $i$th interaction
face whenever available. For this theorem only, record
$(a_{i,q},a_{i,q}\Theta_{i,q})$ with its original availability
indicator $a_{i,q}$; the zero coordinate on its unavailable
part is this explicitly declared masked observable, not a
value assigned to the instrument's omitted face.
Every fixed polynomial moment of
$\eta_q=(a_{1,q}\Theta_{1,q},a_{2,q}\Theta_{2,q})/q$
converges jointly under the ORIGINAL source shift
$G\mapsto G+\theta f$ to

$$
\eta_\theta=CG+\theta Cf,
\quad (CG)_1=L_1\cdot[(1-a)G_1+aG_2],
\quad (CG)_2=L_2\cdot[(1-a)G_2+aG_1].
\tag{NSAV.14}
$$

Its complete same-record covariance is

$$
\Gamma=CC^T=
\begin{pmatrix}
D_a&-\sqrt2a(1-a)\\
-\sqrt2a(1-a)&D_a
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{NSAV.15}
$$

It is positive definite for every finite $a\ge0$.
The actual limiting density, action and coarse source score
on its full two-dimensional face support are

$$
p_\theta(\eta)=\frac{
e^{-\frac12(\eta-\theta Cf)^T\Gamma^{-1}(\eta-\theta Cf)}}
{2\pi\sqrt{\det\Gamma}},\qquad
S_0(\eta)=\frac12\eta^T\Gamma^{-1}\eta
+\log(2\pi)+\frac12\log\det\Gamma,
$$

$$
j_f(\eta)=(Cf)^T\Gamma^{-1}\eta,
\qquad X_f=(Cf)\cdot\nabla_\eta,
\qquad \int X_f O\,p_0=\int O j_f\,p_0.
\tag{NSAV.16}
$$

For bounded $C^1$ tests with bounded derivative this is
also the limit of the original finite-$q$ weak source
responses. The actual original face defects satisfy,
jointly with every fixed moment,

$$
q^{-2}(a_{1,q}W_{1,q},a_{2,q}W_{2,q})
\ \Longrightarrow\ (\eta_1^2/2,\eta_2^2/2).
\tag{NSAV.17}
$$

The identity (NSAV.16) identifies the supported native
limiting face likelihood, not the full path density or
a continuum $SU(3)$ gauge action. Actual final cap,
fitness floors, original $\sigma_J$ and collision marks
have their proved scope above; no independence between
the two forces or the two face phases is introduced.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The original pre-O equalities in the register give
$z_i=qG_i$ and $Y_i=x_i+tqG_i$ exactly. Before the
terminal cap, the final velocity is
$w_i=z_i+tF_i$. In row normalization the single
nonself kernel weight cancels its own denominator,
so $F_1=\nu q(G_2-G_1)$ and $F_2=-F_1$ exactly.
In count normalization
$F_1=(\nu/2)K_q q(G_2-G_1)$, where
$K_q=\exp[-|x_2-x_1+tq(G_2-G_1)|^2/(2\rho^2)]$.
The derivative of the original Gaussian kernel is
globally bounded, giving
$|K_q-K_0|\le C_\rho tq|G_2-G_1|$.
Thus both normalizations give

$$
w_1=q[(1-a)G_1+aG_2]+O(q^2|G|^2),\qquad
w_2=q[(1-a)G_2+aG_1]+O(q^2|G|^2),
\tag{NSAV.18}
$$

with zero count-kernel remainder in the row case.
The actual cap satisfies
$|C_V(w)-w|\le |w|^2/V$ when finite; no correction
is present for $V=\infty$. Both exact viscous formulas
also give $|w_i|\le Cq|G|$ for every innovation, so
these are genuine polynomial remainder estimates,
not a clipped thermostat.

For real unit pre rays $a_i=x_i/|x_i|$ and the
other pre ray $b_i$, the original phase near the
unchanged pre position is the argument of
$[a_i\cdot(Y_i+iu_i)]
[b_i\cdot(Y_i-iu_i)](a_i\cdot b_i)$.
At $Y_i=x_i,u_i=0$ this is the strictly positive
number $|x_i|^2(a_i\cdot b_i)^2$.
Its first real-position derivative has zero phase.
Its first velocity-phase derivative is
$L_i=|x_i|^{-1}[a_i-b_i/(a_i\cdot b_i)]$.
Evaluation at (NSAV.11) gives exactly (NSAV.13).
Taylor expansion on this actual available neighborhood
and (NSAV.18) therefore prove
$\eta_q=CG+O(q(1+|G|^4))$ there, also for each
fixed shifted source $G+\theta f$.

For full moment control estimate on
$|G|\le q^{-1/4}$. All positions then remain in
the same strict interior/overlap neighborhood for
small $q$, because $q|G|\to0$. The polynomial
Taylor error has vanishing expectation to every
fixed power by the actual Gaussian moments.
On the complement, the true available phase has
absolute value at most $\pi$, the declared masked
coordinate is zero on its missing part, and
$\Pr(|G|>q^{-1/4})\le C e^{-c q^{-1/2}}$.
This dominates every power of $q^{-1}$ and proves
all claimed moments and convergence of the original
availability indicators to one. The cosine remainder
is at most $|\Theta|^4/24$, proving (NSAV.17).

Multiplying the two-row linear map gives the diagonal
variance $D_a|L_i|^2=D_a$, and its off-diagonal
entry is $2a(1-a)L_1\cdot L_2=-\sqrt2a(1-a)$.
Since $D_a\ge2|a(1-a)|$ for all real $a$,
its smaller eigenvalue is at least
$D_a(1-1/\sqrt2)>0$. This proves its full support
and the displayed original Gaussian density/action.
Gaussian integration by parts in that supported
two-dimensional law gives (NSAV.16).

The finite-$q$ source score in (NSAV.10) is the
unchanged $f\cdot G$. Joint moment convergence and
bounded tests give limiting response
$E[O(CG)f\cdot G]$. The orthogonal Gaussian
decomposition of $G$ along $\operatorname{ran}C^T$
and its independent orthogonal complement proves
$E[f\cdot G\mid CG]=(Cf)^T\Gamma^{-1}CG$.
Thus its complete simultaneous native source response
is exactly (NSAV.16). Local uniformity for fixed
bounded $\theta$ follows either from these same
Gaussian polynomial estimates or the original
Gaussian exponential likelihood. No independent
per-face or per-force approximation has been used.
:::

:::{prf:corollary} The original two-face unit coefficient matches in a positive primitive regime
:label: cor-nsav-literal-unit-action

For the complete regime (NSAV.11)--(NSAV.13), the
literal two-face unit-weight observable
$q^{-2}(a_{1,q}W_{1,q}+a_{2,q}W_{2,q})$ converges
to the native limiting face-action energy for every
face value if and only if $\Gamma=I_2$.
For $\nu,t,\rho>0$ this is exactly the included
primitive parameter condition

$$
t\nu=1\quad(\mathrm{row}),\qquad
t\nu e^{-(2-\sqrt2)/(2\rho^2)}=2
\quad(\mathrm{count}).
\tag{NSAV.19}
$$

At (NSAV.19) the two native face fluctuations are
independent standard normals, and
$S_0=(\eta_1^2+\eta_2^2)/2+\log(2\pi)$.
The actual source score and every weak first variation
of this limiting action agree with (NSAV.16).
This matches both original coefficients without
adding a face weight, changing a sampler or removing
an innovation. For every other positive parameter
regime the exact limiting discrepancy is
$\eta^T(\Gamma^{-1}-I_2)\eta/2$, including its
mixed term when $a(1-a)\ne0$. The $a=0$ endpoint
is also an algebraic match, but is not a positive
viscous coupling in this fixed primitive family.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The two face fluctuations have full support, so
equality of the two quadratic energies everywhere
is equivalent to $\Gamma^{-1}=I_2$. The diagonal
condition $D_a=1$ gives $a(a-1)=0$; the off-diagonal
entry then vanishes. Since $a>0$ in the stated
positive regime, $a=1$. Substituting its original
count/row formula proves (NSAV.19). At that value
$C$ uses $L_1\cdot G_2$ and $L_2\cdot G_1$,
whose unit variances and independence are consequences
of the original different source rows. Their same-law
Gaussian action and weak identity were proved above.
Subtracting the original unit quadratic energy gives
the stated discrepancy in all other regimes.
:::

:::{prf:corollary} Nonzero literal face action has positive original probability at every positive thermostat amplitude
:label: cor-nsav-positive-finite-action

For every $q,t,\nu,\rho>0$ and every allowed finite
cap or `None` in {prf:ref}`def-nsav-two-face-regime`,
the actual available first interaction face has
$W_1>0$ with positive unconditional probability.
This is a full original-noise event, not only the
conditional source fiber used below.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Choose an original source point $G_1=0$,
$G_2=(r/q)e_2$ for sufficiently small $r>0$.
Its actual future anchor is $Y_1=e_1$, while its
second future point is $x_2+tre_2$.
Its first kick remains zero and the actual second
kick at row one is $b e_2$, where
$b=t\nu r$ in row normalization and
$b=(t\nu/2)r
\exp[-|x_2-e_1+tre_2|^2/(2\rho^2)]>0$
in count normalization. Its final velocity is
$u e_2$ with $u=C_V(b)>0$. Choose $r$ small
enough that $u<1$; every pre/final overlap then
has modulus at least $1/\sqrt2$, its norms exceed
one or equal one, and the anchor has a strict
terminal-domain margin. The exact original loop
is $L=(1-iu)/\sqrt{1+u^2}$, so
$W_1=1-(1+u^2)^{-1/2}>0$.

All original force, cap and ray maps are continuous
on this full-eligible branch. Their finite derivative
profiles on a fixed compact source ball give a
computed positive radius $\epsilon$ preserving half
each displayed domain/norm/overlap/action margin.
For example divide each positive margin by twice
one plus its actual compact derivative bound and
take the minimum with one. These bounds are finite
Gaussian-kernel polynomials, the row coefficient
$\nu$, and the ray/cap denominators separated by
the displayed margins. Thus this is a primitive
open source event. Its original six-dimensional
Gaussian probability is bounded below by
$(2\pi)^{-3}\exp[-(|G_*|+\epsilon)^2/2]
v_6\epsilon^6>0$, where $v_6$ is the unit
six-ball volume. The pre-source gates were
identically zero, so no additional conditioned
clone event is used.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Native face law and source measure converge in total variation
:label: thm-nsav-face-density-source

In the complete two-face regime let $\mu_q$ be the
ORIGINAL law of its declared scaled masked face coordinates
$\eta_q$. Let the original signed source measure be

$$
\lambda_{q,f}(B)=E[\mathbf1_{\eta_q\in B}\,f\cdot G].
\tag{NSAV.27}
$$

Then, for each finite original source $f$,

$$
\|\mu_q-p_0\,d\eta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\|\lambda_{q,f}-j_fp_0\,d\eta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
                                      \longrightarrow0,
\tag{NSAV.28}
$$

with the Gaussian density and actual simultaneous-source
score in (NSAV.16). The same law convergence holds at
every fixed $\theta$ with its mean $\theta Cf$,
locally uniformly in $\theta$ on bounded sets.
Every unavailable/missing or other singular contribution
of the ORIGINAL law is retained; its total mass tends
to zero. No global finite-$q$ density or convergence of
pointwise action derivatives is assumed.

Write its exact Lebesgue decompositions
$\mu_q=p_q\,d\eta+\mu_q^{\mathrm s}$ and
$\lambda_{q,f}=s_{q,f}\,d\eta+\lambda_{q,f}^{\mathrm s}$.
Then $p_q\to p_0$ and $s_{q,f}\to j_fp_0$ in $L^1$,
with both singular measures tending to zero in total
variation. The ACTUAL coarse action and score on its
absolutely continuous phase sector satisfy, on every
compact face-coordinate set, convergence in Lebesgue
measure

$$
-\log p_q(\eta)\longrightarrow S_0(\eta),\qquad
\frac{s_{q,f}(\eta)}{p_q(\eta)}\longrightarrow j_f(\eta),
\tag{NSAV.29}
$$

where the ratio is used on its actual $p_q>0$ set.
The action has its actual infinite value at a zero
density; the measure of such sets in a fixed compact
core tends to zero. The original unscaled phase action
has the corresponding additive $2\log q$ change of
Euclidean coordinate volume.

At the proved original-unit matching regime (NSAV.19),
the actual coarse action and ORIGINAL measured two-face
energy obey

$$
-\log p_q(\eta)-\frac{2-\cos(q\eta_1)-\cos(q\eta_2)}{q^2}
 \longrightarrow\log(2\pi)
\tag{NSAV.30}
$$

in Lebesgue measure on every compact set, and its
actual likelihood source score tends to
$(Cf)\cdot\eta$. In every other regime the corresponding
limit is the complete constant plus quadratic
discrepancy determined by (NSAV.15)--(NSAV.16).
This strengthens weak fluctuation matching to native
coarse likelihood/action correspondence in the stated
included regime, with its original source score.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
On every fixed compact original source core the exact
force and ray calculations in Section 4 give

$$
\Phi_q(G):=\eta_q(G)\longrightarrow CG
                    \quad\hbox{in }C^1.
\tag{NSAV.31}
$$

All original face masks are one on that core for
small $q$. For count normalization, differentiate
its finite Gaussian kernel formula to get uniform
first-derivative convergence of $w_i/q$ to its
displayed linear map; the row formula is exactly
linear before the cap. The actual cap has
$DC_V(qw)\to I$ uniformly for bounded $w$,
including $w=0$. Thus its normalized velocity
has the same $C^1$ limit. The original phase is
a smooth function of $(Y,u)$ on their strict
overlap neighborhood, and its first derivative
at $(x_i,0)$ is the already computed $(0,L_i)$.
Taylor expansion of that smooth phase and the
chain rule prove (NSAV.31). This uses $C^1$ cap
regularity only, rather than an unproved $C^2$
property at zero.

Choose an orthonormal decomposition of the ORIGINAL
six-source space into $(\xi,\zeta)\in\mathbb R^2
\oplus\mathbb R^4$ with
$\xi=\Gamma^{-1/2}CG$. These are independent
standard normal coordinates and $CG=L\xi$,
$L=\Gamma^{1/2}$, a fixed positive invertible
matrix. On the convex cube $B_M=(-M,M)^6$
define the computed change of variables

$$
T_q(\xi,\zeta)=
       \big(L^{-1}\Phi_q(G(\xi,\zeta)),\zeta\big).
\tag{NSAV.32}
$$

It is $C^1$ close to the identity there. For small
$q$, $\|DT_q-I\|\le1/2$, and integration on
each source segment gives
$|T_q(z)-T_q(z')|\ge|z-z'|/2$.
Its Jacobian is uniformly positive, so it is
injective with a $C^1$ inverse on its image.
Let $\epsilon_q=\sup_{B_M}|T_q-I|_\infty\to0$.
Its image lies in the $\epsilon_q$ enlarged cube
and contains the $\epsilon_q$ shrunken cube:
for a point of the latter, the map
$z\mapsto y-(T_q(z)-z)$ sends the closed cube
to itself and is a contraction. Its unique fixed
point supplies the inverse. Enlarging $M$ slightly
when needed avoids any endpoint issue.
Consequently the symmetric difference of the cube
and its image has volume tending to zero.

The original restricted Gaussian has smooth bounded
density on this compact source cube. On the image,
its changed density is its exact value at $T_q^{-1}$
times $|\det DT_q|^{-1}$. Both converge uniformly
to their original values on the common interior;
the bounded densities and vanishing boundary shell
give $L^1$ convergence on the whole source space.
Projecting the augmented coordinates and multiplying
by $L$ contracts total variation. Thus the original
face law restricted to this source cube converges
in total variation to the corresponding restriction
of $CG$.

The identical argument applies to the ORIGINAL
signed density $\varphi_6(G)f\cdot G$, which is
smooth and bounded on the core. Its pushforward
converges in total variation to the pushforward
of that same weighted original Gaussian. Outside
the core, the two law masses are at most
$P(G\notin B_M)$; the two signed-measure masses
are bounded by
$E[|f\cdot G|\mathbf1_{G\notin B_M}]$.
Both tend to zero as $M\to\infty$, after taking
the actual $q\to0$ limit. This retains all rare
missing or critical branches and proves (NSAV.28).
The limiting weighted pushforward is $j_fp_0$
by the exact Gaussian conditional expectation
proved in Section 4. For shifted sources use the
same maps with the original Gaussian density of
mean $\theta f$. Its compact density convergence
and outside-core Gaussian tails are locally
uniform on bounded $\theta$ sets, proving the
stated shift scope.

Total variation convergence to an absolutely
continuous measure implies both $L^1$ convergence
of the displayed absolutely continuous densities
and disappearance of their retained singular
parts, by uniqueness of Lebesgue decomposition.
The limiting $p_0$ is bounded away from zero on
every compact face-coordinate set. $L^1$
convergence there implies convergence in measure;
continuity of logarithm and division at $p_0>0$
gives (NSAV.29), including vanishing measure of
the zero-density part. The same decomposition
identifies $s_{q,f}/p_q$ as its exact coarse
source score: the original signed score measure
is precisely the Radon--Nikodym source derivative
against the original output law.

On a fixed face-coordinate compact set,
$q^{-2}[2-\cos(q\eta_1)-\cos(q\eta_2)]$
converges uniformly to $|\eta|^2/2$.
At $\Gamma=I_2$ subtract this from (NSAV.29)
to obtain (NSAV.30) and its limiting likelihood
score. This argument asserts convergence of
the actual action and score in measure, not
uncontrolled convergence of derivatives of a
finite-$q$ density. Outside this primitive match,
subtract the same unit quadratic from the
already calculated $S_0$.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact finite phase pushforward on an original Gaussian source fiber
:label: thm-nsav-finite-phase-action

Use the same included $N=2$, $\lambda=0$, end-of-step,
$\sigma_x=0$ gas, but take the legitimate entering
positions $x_1=e_1,x_2=e_1+e_2$, with zero velocities.
Both current nonself companion channels are unique,
both rewards and diversities agree, and both clone
gates are again exactly zero. Retain every parameter
of {prf:ref}`def-nsav-two-face-regime`, with $q>0$
now fixed. The independent Gaussian source has the
regular conditional fiber
$z_1=0$, $z_{2,1}=z_{2,3}=0$, with remaining original
coordinate $r=z_{2,2}\sim N(0,q^2)$. This is a
conditional coordinate law of the original innovation;
the zero-valued fiber is not asserted to have positive
unconditional probability.

The actual first face has $Y_1=e_1$ and

$$
b(r)=\begin{cases}
(t\nu/2)r e^{-(1+tr)^2/(2\rho^2)},&\mathrm{count},\\
t\nu r,&\mathrm{row},
\end{cases}\qquad
u(r)=\frac{Vb(r)}{V+|b(r)|},\qquad
\Theta(r)=-\arctan u(r),\qquad
W(r)=1-\frac1{\sqrt{1+u(r)^2}},
\tag{NSAV.20}
$$

For $V=\infty$ read $u=b$. Its ray norm is at least
one, its pre cross overlap and final-to-second-pre
overlap have modulus $1/\sqrt2$, and its remaining
overlap has modulus $(1+u^2)^{-1/2}$.
Therefore its exact available phase support retains
$|\Theta|<\arccos\delta_\ell$ as well as
$|\tan\Theta|<V$ when finite. Its original future
anchor remains eligible; the second future walker
may die at the final boundary without deleting its
eligible PRE donor from this face. No unbounded
source tail is discarded.

For row normalization put $A=t\nu>0$. On this
available interval $I_V$, the actual inverse and its
Euclidean phase-density action are

$$
r(\theta)=-\frac{V\tan\theta}{A(V-|\tan\theta|)},
\quad J(\theta)=\left|\frac{dr}{d\theta}\right|
=\frac{V^2\sec^2\theta}{A(V-|\tan\theta|)^2},
$$

$$
p(\theta)=\frac{e^{-r(\theta)^2/(2q^2)}}{\sqrt{2\pi q^2}}
J(\theta),\qquad
S(\theta)=\frac{r(\theta)^2}{2q^2}
 +\frac12\log(2\pi q^2)-\log J(\theta).
\tag{NSAV.21}
$$

For $V=\infty$ these formulas are
$r=-\tan\theta/A$, $J=\sec^2\theta/A$.
The density is the AVAILABLE subdensity. The original
missing face has its remaining Gaussian mass; if the
available phase is separately conditioned, retain
its additional mass normalizer and its source derivative.
For the original shift $G_{2,2}\mapsto G_{2,2}+\epsilon f$,
its available-density likelihood score is
$j_f(\theta)=f r(\theta)/q$.
On a strict smooth branch the actual phase tangent
$X_f=qf\,d\Theta/dr$ satisfies

$$
j_f=X_f S'-X_f',\qquad
\int O'X_f p=\int O j_f p
\tag{NSAV.22}
$$

for smooth tests supported inside $I_V$.
The finite measured-action source derivative is
$\delta_f W=\sin\theta\,X_f$.
Its difference from the native phase score includes
the explicit phase reference-volume divergence $X_f'$.

In count normalization, the two original critical
coordinates of $b$ are
$r_\pm=(-1\pm\sqrt{1+4\rho^2})/(2t)$.
Away from these critical images, the exact available
phase density and weak score are

$$
p(\theta)=\sum_{r:\Theta(r)=\theta}
 \frac{e^{-r^2/(2q^2)}}{\sqrt{2\pi q^2}\,|\Theta'(r)|},
\qquad
j_f(\theta)=\frac{\displaystyle
 \sum_{r:\Theta(r)=\theta}(fr/q)
 \frac{e^{-r^2/(2q^2)}}{|\Theta'(r)|}}
 {\displaystyle
 \sum_{r:\Theta(r)=\theta}
 \frac{e^{-r^2/(2q^2)}}{|\Theta'(r)|}}.
\tag{NSAV.23}
$$

Every nonzero phase in the interior of either positive
or negative image has two original source preimages.
Both are retained. The native action is $-\log p$;
the inverse-Jacobian critical-image singularities
are the actual pushforward behavior, not a force
clipping convention or a missing extra assumption.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
On the specified original conditional fiber, B1 is
zero, $Y_1=e_1$, $Y_2=e_1+(1+tr)e_2$, and
$z_2-z_1=re_2$. The original count force at row
one is $(\nu/2)e^{-(1+tr)^2/(2\rho^2)}re_2$;
the original nonself row force is $\nu re_2$.
Its second kick and actual cap give $u_1=u(r)e_2$.
The first face overlaps consequently have product
$L=(1-iu)/\sqrt{1+u^2}$, proving (NSAV.20)
and the displayed thresholds. Its initial and final
anchor positions equal $e_1$, so the final boundary
does not kill this future ray. All B2 force rows are
evaluated before the end-of-step boundary, regardless
of the eventual second walker's terminal status.

The row map $r\mapsto u\mapsto\theta$ is strictly
monotone. Solving its actual cap and phase equations
gives the inverse and Jacobian. Gaussian change of
variables proves (NSAV.21), including its original
support mass. Its source density uses the shifted
normal coordinate with mean $\epsilon qf$, so its
logarithmic derivative at zero is $fr/q$.
The original coordinate translation gives the phase
continuity equation $\partial_\epsilon p
=-\partial_\theta(X_f p)$. Dividing by $p$ gives
$j_f=X_fS'-X_f'$. Integration against compactly
supported $O$ proves (NSAV.22); tests crossing the
threshold use (NSAV.10) with their retained mask.

For count normalization,
$b'(r)=(t\nu/2)e^{-(1+tr)^2/(2\rho^2)}
[1-tr(1+tr)/\rho^2]$. Its two simple zeros are
exactly $r_-,r_+$. Its sign and its vanishing limits
at $r\to\pm\infty$ give one negative minimum and
one positive maximum, so each nonzero interior image
has two preimages. The cap/phase maps are strictly
monotone in $b$, and add no critical points.
Split the source Gaussian integral into those
three monotone intervals and change variables in
each; summing proves its full density (NSAV.23).
Apply the same change of variables to its exact
Gaussian source-score integral to get the displayed
conditional mean score. Each critical point is
nondegenerate: at a zero of the bracket its derivative
is $-t(1+2tr)/\rho^2\ne0$, since
$1+2tr_\pm=\pm\sqrt{1+4\rho^2}$.
The local quadratic map therefore has the usual
inverse-square-root density factor, derived directly
by this same one-dimensional inverse formula.
It is locally integrable and no atom is introduced.
:::

:::{prf:corollary} Exact cap and Jacobian effects on a local Wilson comparison
:label: cor-nsav-finite-action-comparison

In the row fiber of {prf:ref}`thm-nsav-finite-phase-action`,
the available phase-density action differs from the
original measured $1-\cos\theta$ by exactly (NSAV.21).
For finite $V$, its local expansion at zero is

$$
S(\theta)-S(0)=-\frac{2|\theta|}{V}+O(\theta^2).
\tag{NSAV.24}
$$

Thus no positive $q,A,V$ makes this finite-density
first variation equal to that of the original smooth
unit face action near zero. This is the actual radial
cap's phase-volume correction, not a different
unexecuted clipping rule.

For the existing $V=\infty$ parameter value,

$$
S(\theta)-S(0)=\frac{\tan^2\theta}{2(Aq)^2}
 +2\log\cos\theta.
\tag{NSAV.25}
$$

There is a positive primitive SECOND-order local
matching regime $Aq=1/\sqrt3$:

$$
S(\theta)-S(0)=(1-\cos\theta)+\frac78\theta^4
 +O(\theta^6),\qquad
S'(\theta)=\sin\theta+\frac72\theta^3+O(\theta^5).
\tag{NSAV.26}
$$

In all uncapped regimes the quadratic discrepancy is
$[1/(2(Aq)^2)-3/2]\theta^2+O(\theta^4)$.
No finite positive $Aq$ gives a global equality with
the bounded original $1-\cos\theta$: the native
action diverges at the inverse-map endpoint whereas
that measured action remains bounded. Its threshold
truncation retains this analytic mismatch on every
nonempty neighborhood of zero. This finite fiber
comparison is distinct from the complete two-face
Gaussian fluctuation matching (NSAV.19).
:::

:::{prf:proof}
In (NSAV.21), $-\log J$ contributes
$2\log(1-|\tan\theta|/V)-\log\sec^2\theta$
relative to its value at zero. Its first term is
$-2|\theta|/V+O(\theta^2)$, whereas the Gaussian
energy is quadratic. This proves (NSAV.24).
For no cap, its Jacobian contribution is
$2\log\cos\theta$, proving (NSAV.25).
Use $\tan^2\theta=\theta^2+2\theta^4/3+O(\theta^6)$
and $2\log\cos\theta=-\theta^2-\theta^4/6+O(\theta^6)$.
At $(Aq)^2=1/3$ the quadratic coefficient is $1/2$
and the quartic coefficient is $5/6$.
Subtract $1-\cos\theta=\theta^2/2-\theta^4/24+O(\theta^6)$
and differentiate to obtain (NSAV.26).
The general quadratic coefficient follows from the
same expansion. The uncapped phase action has its
$\tan^2\theta$ divergence at $\pm\pi/2$; if a
global equality held on the threshold interval,
analytic continuation from its neighborhood of zero
would give that false equality on $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$.
Thus the literal threshold does not repair it.
:::

:::{prf:remark} The native action identification now proved
:label: rem-nsav-remaining-identification

The original archive ray-face support, first variation
and full Gaussian weak source are determined above.
The origin-consensus spatial regime has unavailable
first archive faces and a flat terminal ray line,
despite its different B2 color connection's non-Abelian
curvature. Shifted consensus has exactly unit available
ray loops. These are evaluated included algorithm
regimes, not proposed replacement transports.

The nonconsensus two-walker regime has two original
available faces with nonzero Gaussian fluctuations.
Its complete covariance, native limiting action and
source score retain both simultaneous source rows.
Both literal unit coefficients match that native
limiting action at the positive primitive viscosity
conditions (NSAV.19); all other regimes have the
explicit quadratic discrepancy. The finite phase
fiber additionally computes the actual cap/Jacobian
and count-branch mixture corrections, with full
unbounded source law and original availability mass.

These are native $U(1)$ ray fluctuation/action results.
Neither a common color-orbit algebra nor this scalar
line action identifies the full non-Abelian spatial
projector curvature action. The latter identification
still requires the native law on its actual composite
connection support and the corresponding local
force-score first variation. No original archive ray
edge, action coefficient or transition kernel has been
substituted to infer it. Multi-time/spatial joint
continuum action and physical reconstruction remain
the obligations of their separately specified
algorithm/readout regimes.
:::

## 2_fractal_set/22_native_two_face_gauge_time.md

:::{prf:definition} Native two-face temporal register
:label: def-ntfg-complete-register

Retain every parameter, original raw-component ray threshold,
archive event/version/generation label, graph rule, Gaussian
stream, boundary mark, eligible mask, numerical convention,
cap and error policy in {prf:ref}`def-nsav-complete-register`.
Use the included $N=2,d=3$, constant quadratic reward and
force $\lambda=0$, $\sigma_x=0$, end-of-step boundary,
current unique nonself count-one companion regime of
{prf:ref}`def-nsav-two-face-regime`, with fixed
$x_1^*=e_1$, $x_2^*=(e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2$.
The domain has both points strictly in its interior.
It uses the ORIGINAL positive coupling condition

$$
t\nu=1\quad(\mathrm{row}),\qquad
t\nu K_0/2=1\quad(\mathrm{count}),\qquad
K_0=e^{-(2-\sqrt2)/(2\rho^2)},\quad t=h/2.
\tag{NTFG.1}
$$

Keep $h,\rho,\nu$, friction $\gamma\ge0$ and cap
fixed and let its original thermostat amplitude $q>0$
tend to zero as in (NSAV.12). Write $c=e^{-\gamma h}$.
The consumed thermostat is the existing Rust independent
isotropic constant diffusion-factor tag $b_O$, with
BAOAB friction validated at every $\gamma\ge0$.
Its O code uses $q=b_O\sqrt h$ at $\gamma=0$,
so the positive-noise $c=1$ endpoint below is an
included configuration of THIS tag. A thermostat
tag imposing $q^2=(1-c^2)/\beta_{\mathrm{eff}}$ retains
that constraint and has $q=0$ at $c=1$ for finite
positive $\beta_{\mathrm{eff}}$; it is not assigned
the positive-noise endpoint by this name.
Allowed entering velocities are $q w_0$ for a specified
finite deterministic six-vector $w_0$; the original
zero-velocity case is $w_0=0$. This specifies the
initial-law parameter, rather than averaging hidden
initial velocities into a new force rule.

At every actual update with both walkers alive, the
constant reward is equal and their symmetric unique
nonself distance gives equal diversity, even after
their positions or velocities have moved. Their
well-defined common fitness transforms give equal
fitness, so both actual living clone gates are zero.
The collision components are singletons with zero
relative velocity. Their configured jitter, restitution
and Haar marks remain in the record but do not change
this all-alive branch. Actual revival/extinction and
outside-domain paths retain their original operations
and masks; they are not removed from its law.

Let $X_{i,n}^q,u_{i,n}^q$ be the actual final state
after $n$ complete updates, $w_{i,n}^q=u_{i,n}^q/q$,
and $G_n=(G_{1,n},G_{2,n})$ its ORIGINAL independent
standard Gaussian O sources. Each actual archive
interaction face at update $n$ has vertices
$(\mathrm{pre}\ i,n,\mathrm{final}\ i,n,
  \mathrm{pre}\ j,n)$.
Use its original principal phase and availability
indicator in the explicitly declared masked coordinate
$\eta_{i,n}^q=a_{i,n}^q\Theta_{i,n}^q/q$.
The omitted-face value of the literal report is unchanged.
Let $S(w_1,w_2)=(w_2,w_1)$ and retain
$L_1=-e_2$, $L_2=(-e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2$.
The color calibration $\kappa$ is not consumed by
this ray instrument. A graph/covariance provider is
passive and does not replace either dense viscous kick.
This is explicitly the canonical real-coordinate DENSE
algorithm tag bound to Rust `QftExecutionConfig.viscosity`
and `recorded_force`, with its actual unregularized
nonself row mass. The Python $N=2,d=3$ empty CSR fallback
and its mass-floor variant retain their different update.
Finite-arithmetic Gaussian underflow/zero-mass branches
and rounded kicks keep their original comparison errors;
they are not assigned the global exact real-coordinate swap.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Native repeated-update Gaussian limit
:label: thm-ntfg-finite-window-process

For every fixed finite $K$, the actual all-alive
probability through its first $K$ updates tends to
one. Jointly over these updates,
$X_n^q\to x^*$ and $w_n^q\to w_n$ in probability
under the original coupled source representation,
where the complete Gaussian state satisfies

$$
w_n=cw_{n-1}+SG_n,
\qquad
w_n=c^nw_0+\sum_{l=1}^nc^{n-l}SG_l.
\tag{NTFG.2}
$$

The original two-face phase coordinates converge
jointly, with every fixed polynomial moment, to

$$
\eta_{i,n}=L_i\cdot(w_{i,n}-w_{i,n-1}).
\tag{NTFG.3}
$$

The donor's own pre velocity contributes to each
individual edge and cancels in this actual triangle
sum; it is not omitted from the original edge map.
Every original measured defect satisfies jointly
$a_{i,n}^q W_{i,n}^q/q^2\to\eta_{i,n}^2/2$
with all fixed moments.

Relative to the complete limiting state filtration,
the exact native discrete conditional drift and
centered bracket per update are

$$
E[\Delta w_n\mid w_{n-1}]=(c-1)w_{n-1},
\quad E[M_nM_n^T\mid w_{n-1}]=I_6,
\quad M_n=\Delta w_n-(c-1)w_{n-1}=SG_n.
\tag{NTFG.4}
$$

The projected phase centered innovations are
$\epsilon_{i,n}=L_i\cdot(SG_n)_i$, independent
standard normals in both $i$ and $n$. Thus
$E[\eta_{i,n}\mid w_{n-1}]=(c-1)L_i\cdot w_{i,n-1}$
and their centered two-channel bracket is $I_2$
per update, or $I_2/(t_*h)$ per configured physical
clock interval $t_*h>0$. This is its derived discrete
Gaussian process, not an additional continuous-time
or continuum Yang--Mills limit.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
On the all-alive branch the first nonself row kick
is exactly $u\mapsto Su$ at $t\nu=1$.
For count normalization write its kick as
$B(K)u$, with diagonal $1-t\nu K/2$ and
off-diagonal $t\nu K/2$ in particle space.
At $K_0$, (NTFG.1) gives $B(K_0)=S$.
The Gaussian kernel is globally Lipschitz and the
fixed source-core positions move by $O_K(q)$;
therefore its actual B1 and separately reevaluated
B2 matrices are $S+O_K(q)$.
The original O step is $z=cB_1u+qG_n$.
The second kick gives $B_2z$, followed by the actual
cap. Consequently on each fixed compact source core

$$
u_n^q/q=cw_{n-1}^q+SG_n+O_K(q),
\quad
X_n^q-X_{n-1}^q
 =qt[(1+c)Sw_{n-1}^q+G_n]+O_K(q^2).
\tag{NTFG.5}
$$

In row normalization both swap identities are exact
before the cap; the finite cap has only its actual
$O(q^2|w|^2/V)$ velocity error. Induction on the
fixed $K$ proves the displayed state convergence,
with all original positions remaining inside the
strict domain neighborhood on that core. No living
gate is opened there. Increasing the original
Gaussian source core proves convergence in probability
for the full actual law.

For the phase calculation keep all THREE native
rays. At zero imaginary parts their three real
overlaps remain positive near the base points,
so the loop phase is identically zero for all
these real position perturbations. Its linear
imaginary-velocity terms at the base positions are

$$
\frac{x_i^*\cdot(w_{i,n}-w_{i,n-1})}{|x_i^*|^2}
+\frac{x_i^*\cdot w_{j,n-1}-x_j^*\cdot w_{i,n}}
       {x_i^*\cdot x_j^*}
+\frac{x_j^*\cdot w_{i,n-1}-x_i^*\cdot w_{j,n-1}}
       {x_i^*\cdot x_j^*}.
$$

They sum to precisely (NTFG.3). The old donor
terms cancel between its actual two incident
overlaps. This is the ordered interaction triangle,
not a triangle of new spatial sample points.
Taylor expansion of its original smooth phase
function on the strict ray/overlap neighborhood
gives joint convergence on each source core.

For moment control, use the original event
$\max_{n\le K}|G_n|\le q^{-1/8}$.
Deterministic finite-step kick bounds and
$|C_V(w)|\le|w|$ show all-alive scaled velocities
are at most $C_K(1+|w_0|+\sum_{n\le K}|G_n|)$.
Both positions and ray velocities stay within the
same strict neighborhood for small $q$; count
kick errors are bounded Gaussian polynomials times
$q$. The phase remainder divided by $q$ has a
vanishing fixed polynomial-moment bound on this
event. Its complement has Gaussian probability
at most $C_Ke^{-c_Kq^{-1/4}}$.
The actual available phase is bounded by $\pi$
on EVERY branch, and its declared masked coordinate
is zero when missing. Thus even actual revival,
later clone/jitter or extinction outcomes on this
exceptional event give a scaled-phase moment at
most $(\pi/q)^p C_Ke^{-c_Kq^{-1/4}}\to0$.
No rare algorithm branch or unbounded innovation
has been deleted. Cosine's fourth-order remainder
proves the defect moments by the same estimates.

The affine recursion gives (NTFG.2) and its
conditional Gaussian innovation $SG_n$.
The swap is orthogonal, so its covariance is $I_6$.
The two projected innovations consume different
original rows and each $L_i$ has norm one; they
are therefore independent standard normals.
Conditional expectation and the actual clock
normalization prove the drift/bracket assertions.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Full finite-window native phase likelihood and measured-action comparison
:label: thm-ntfg-path-action

Put $v_{i,n}=L_i\cdot w_{i,n}$ and retain the specified
initial projection $v_{i,0}=L_i\cdot w_{i,0}$. The two
original limiting channels obey
$v_{i,n}=cv_{i,n-1}+\epsilon_{i,n}$ and
$\eta_{i,n}=v_{i,n}-v_{i,n-1}$.
Let $T_K$ be the $K\times K$ lower triangular matrix
with diagonal one and

$$
(T_K)_{nl}=-(1-c)c^{n-1-l}\quad(l<n),
\quad m_{i,n}=(c-1)c^{n-1}v_{i,0}.
\tag{NTFG.6}
$$

The COMPLETE native $2K$-phase support is full real
coordinate space and has mean $m$, independent channel
covariances $T_KT_K^T$, and the exact Gaussian path action

$$
S_K(\eta\mid v_0)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^2\sum_{n=1}^K
 \left[\eta_{i,n}+(1-c)
        \left(v_{i,0}+\sum_{l<n}\eta_{i,l}\right)\right]^2
                         +K\log(2\pi).
\tag{NTFG.7}
$$

All past phases in these terms are retained, rather
than declaring the marginal phase channel Markov.
For the ORIGINAL simultaneous source shifts
$G_n\mapsto G_n+\theta f_n$, put
$g_{i,n}=L_i\cdot f_{j,n}$ with $j\ne i$.
Its induced path direction is $V_f=(T_Kg_1,T_Kg_2)$,
its volume divergence is zero, and its exact native score is

$$
j_f(\eta)=\sum_{i,n}g_{i,n}
 \left[\eta_{i,n}+(1-c)
        \left(v_{i,0}+\sum_{l<n}\eta_{i,l}\right)\right],
\qquad \int D O[V_f]e^{-S_K}d\eta
       =\int O j_fe^{-S_K}d\eta.
\tag{NTFG.8}
$$

The ORIGINAL finite-$q$ complete masked phase-path
law and its signed source-score measure converge
in total variation to this path density and score.
Their retained singular/missing mass tends to zero;
the actual absolutely continuous native path action
and score consequently converge in measure on every
compact phase-path coordinate set. The raw unscaled
phase density has its actual $2K\log q$ coordinate
volume correction.

The original sum of its unit face defects, divided
by $q^2$, converges with all fixed moments to
$Q_K(\eta)=\sum_{i,n}\eta_{i,n}^2/2$.
For $c<1$ and $K\ge2$, this differs from the native
path-action energy, even when $v_0=0$.
For $K=1$ it matches up to a constant exactly when
$(1-c)v_0=0$. For the existing zero-friction regime
$\gamma=0$ ($c=1$), it matches for EVERY finite $K$
and every finite specified $w_0$, with the full
native weak source first variation (NTFG.8).
Thus positive one-step matching does not silently
replace the complete temporal likelihood by a sum
of independently fitted face actions.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Project the actual limiting recursion (NTFG.2).
Its two innovations are the independent unit normals
already derived from the original sources. Solving
the scalar recursion and subtracting its adjacent
values gives $\eta_i=m_i+T_K\epsilon_i$.
The triangular matrix has determinant one, so this
Gaussian law has full support and its complete
Jacobian has no unknown volume correction.
The inverse formula is explicitly
$\epsilon_{i,n}=\eta_{i,n}+(1-c)
(v_{i,0}+\sum_{l<n}\eta_{i,l})$.
Multiplying its original independent normal densities
proves (NTFG.7).

The original stream source changes each innovation
by $\theta g_{i,n}$ and therefore the path by
$\theta T_Kg_i$. The unobserved orthogonal
components of each original three-source row are
independent normals with mean-zero score.
The displayed invertible path reconstructs its
projected innovations, so the coarse conditional
mean of $\sum_n f_n\cdot G_n$ is exactly (NTFG.8).
Differentiating its Gaussian mean shift and integrating
by parts gives the weak identity and zero divergence.

The actual finite-$K$ source-core map from its
$6K$ original Gaussian coordinates to the $2K$
scaled phase path is $C^1$ close to this linear
map plus its deterministic mean. Both kicks,
separately recomputed kernels, the $C^1$ cap and
all three ray derivatives have this convergence
by the finite induction in Section 2. All masks
are one on each fixed core for small $q$.
Decompose the ORIGINAL source coordinates into
their $2K$ independent projected innovations
and the $4K$ orthogonal coordinates.
Augment the computed native phase map by those
orthogonal original coordinates, multiply its
phase part by $T_K^{-1}$ and subtract the known
mean. This is a $C^1$ near-identity injective
change of variables on each fixed convex source
cube. The determinant and inverse-density argument
of {prf:ref}`thm-nsav-face-density-source` therefore
applies in dimension $6K$ without any assumption
about an unknown full output density. Outside
the cube retain the original Gaussian mass and
$E[|\sum_n f_n\cdot G_n|\mathbf1_{\mathrm{outside}}]$;
both tend to zero when the core grows. This proves
the asserted total variation, signed-score and
Lebesgue-sector action/score convergence, with
every exceptional original branch retained.

The defect convergence was proved with moments
in Section 2. If $c<1$, already the first two
terms of (NTFG.7) with $v_0=0$ contain
$(1-c)\eta_{i,1}\eta_{i,2}
+(1-c)^2\eta_{i,1}^2/2$ beyond their literal unit
quadratics. More generally its last two time
coordinates have a nonzero mixed entry for every
$K\ge2$, so the full-support quadratic cannot
equal $Q_K$ up to a constant. For $K=1$ only
the linear shift $(1-c)v_0\cdot\eta_1$ remains,
giving its exact matching condition. At $c=1$
all those memory and initial-shift terms vanish:
the ORIGINAL phase innovations are independent
unit normals for every finite time window and
the native energy is exactly $Q_K$. Its actual
source derivative is the same (NTFG.8).
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Derived stationary local Gaussian phase channel
:label: thm-ntfg-stationary-phase-law

For $0<c<1$ the Gaussian state (NTFG.2) has the
unique invariant law $N(0,(1-c^2)^{-1}I_6)$.
Its original two-face projection in that law is
a centered stationary Gaussian sequence with
independent channels and exact lag covariance

$$
R_0=\frac2{1+c},\qquad
R_k=-\frac{1-c}{1+c}c^{k-1}\quad(k\ge1).
\tag{NTFG.9}
$$

For every finite $K$, its native phase-path action
is

$$
S_K^{\mathrm{stat}}(\eta)
 =\frac12\sum_{i=1}^2\eta_i^T\mathsf R_K^{-1}\eta_i
       +K\log(2\pi)+\log\det\mathsf R_K,
\qquad (\mathsf R_K)_{nl}=R_{|n-l|}.
\tag{NTFG.10}
$$

The covariance is positive definite at every finite
$K$; the hidden initial velocity is integrated
with its DERIVED Gaussian law. Every original
finite source direction has the induced mean
$T_Kg_i$ and native score
$\sum_i(T_Kg_i)^T\mathsf R_K^{-1}\eta_i$.
It is not assigned the zero-initial-velocity action.
For $c<1$ its variance already differs from the
original unit action for $K=1$.

More explicitly, put $a_c=(1-c)/(1+c)$,
$A_K=T_K^{-1}$ and $z_i=A_K\eta_i$, whose actual
coordinates are
$z_{i,n}=\eta_{i,n}+(1-c)\sum_{l<n}\eta_{i,l}$.
The COMPLETE stationary action and source score are

$$
\begin{gathered}
\mathsf R_K=T_K(I_K+a_c\mathbf1\mathbf1^T)T_K^T,
\qquad \det\mathsf R_K=1+Ka_c,\\
S_K^{\mathrm{stat}}(\eta)
 =\frac12\sum_{i=1}^2
  \left[|z_i|^2-\frac{a_c}{1+Ka_c}
                (\mathbf1^Tz_i)^2\right]
  +K\log(2\pi)+\log(1+Ka_c),\\
j_f^{\mathrm{stat}}(\eta)
 =\sum_{i=1}^2
  \left[g_i^Tz_i-\frac{a_c}{1+Ka_c}
       (\mathbf1^Tg_i)(\mathbf1^Tz_i)\right].
\end{gathered}
\tag{NTFG.16}
$$

With the convention
$R_k=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
 e^{ik\omega}\mathfrak s_c(\omega)\,d\omega$,
its exact phase spectral density is

$$
\mathfrak s_c(\omega)
 =\frac{2-2\cos\omega}{1+c^2-2c\cos\omega},
\qquad
\mathfrak s_c(\omega)
   =\frac{\omega^2}{(1-c)^2}+O(\omega^4)
                         \quad(\omega\to0).
\tag{NTFG.17}
$$

The vanishing temporal zero mode therefore follows
from the ORIGINAL adjacent-state phase, while
every finite native path density remains full rank.

Although its predictable centered innovation bracket
is exactly $I_2$ per step, the COMPLETE additive
variance of each stationary phase channel is zero:

$$
R_0+2\sum_{k\ge1}R_k=0,\qquad
\sum_{n=1}^K\eta_{i,n}=v_{i,K}-v_{i,0},\qquad
\frac1K\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{n=1}^K\eta_{i,n}\right)
 =\frac{2(1-c^K)}{K(1-c^2)}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{NTFG.11}
$$

These are properties of the actual derived ray
phase channel; a nonzero one-step bracket is
not identified with a nonzero complete additive
fluctuation coefficient. At $c=1$ its state is
a Gaussian random walk with no invariant
probability, while the phase increments are
independent unit normals and have additive
variance one per update.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Iterating the affine state recursion gives its
normal mean $c^nw_0$ and covariance
$(1-c^{2n})(1-c^2)^{-1}I_6$.
They converge to the displayed invariant normal
law. Two chains driven by the same ORIGINAL
Gaussian sources have difference $c^n(w_0-w'_0)$;
their characteristic functions consequently
give uniqueness of an invariant probability,
or directly iterate the invariant characteristic
function and let $c^n\to0$.

In that state law
$\operatorname{Cov}(v_{i,0},v_{i,k})
=c^{|k|}/(1-c^2)$. Subtract adjacent values
at both times. Its zero lag is
$2(1-c)/(1-c^2)=2/(1+c)$, and its positive
lag is
$[2c^k-c^{k-1}-c^{k+1}]/(1-c^2)$,
which is (NTFG.9). Different projected channels
consume different independent state/source rows.
For a finite phase window, the conditional
innovation contribution $T_KT_K^T$ is positive
definite; adding the nonnegative initial-state
covariance preserves that property. This proves
the full density and (NTFG.10). A fixed original
stream source changes only its mean by $T_Kg$,
whose Gaussian derivative gives the stated
native source score.

In the derived invariant state, $v_{i,0}$ is an
independent centered normal of variance
$(1-c^2)^{-1}$. The inverse recursion gives
$A_K\eta_i=\epsilon_i-(1-c)v_{i,0}\mathbf1$.
Its covariance is $I_K+a_c\mathbf1\mathbf1^T$,
which proves the first formula in (NTFG.16).
This rank-one matrix has eigenvalue $1+Ka_c$
along $\mathbf1$ and eigenvalue one on its
orthogonal complement. Its determinant and inverse
$I_K-a_c\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/(1+Ka_c)$ follow
directly. Since $\det T_K=1$, substitution into
the already derived Gaussian density and original
source direction $T_Kg_i$ proves the remaining
explicit action and score formulas. The normal
hidden initial state is integrated, not treated
as a fitted extra innovation.

The summable stationary state covariance
$c^{|k|}/(1-c^2)$ has spectral density
$(1+c^2-2c\cos\omega)^{-1}$: summing its two
geometric series verifies the Fourier identity
directly. Taking an adjacent-state difference
multiplies that density by
$|e^{i\omega}-1|^2=2-2\cos\omega$.
This proves (NTFG.17), including its displayed
Taylor expansion because $c<1$ keeps the
denominator strictly positive.

The summable geometric covariance has the exact
zero sum in (NTFG.11). The same conclusion follows
without summing a covariance series: the original
phase is the adjacent-state difference, so its
complete partial sum telescopes. Evaluating its
endpoint variance gives the displayed formula.
Its compensated innovation remains $\epsilon$
with unit bracket, as already proved. At $c=1$
the recursion has covariance growing linearly
and its invariant characteristic-function equation
would require invariance under addition of a
nondegenerate centered Gaussian, impossible for
a probability. Its phase is exactly its independent
Gaussian innovation, proving that endpoint scope.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Quantitative original branch control and local stationary phase limit
:label: thm-ntfg-growing-window

Keep every original parameter fixed with $0<c<1$
in the complete register. Let
$d_D=\min_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i^*,D^c)>0$,
$W_0=|w_0|$, and evaluate

$$
\begin{gathered}
C_W=W_0+\frac4{1-c},\qquad C_X=t(4C_W+1),\\
d_* =\min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{1+c}{2c}}-1\right\},\\
C_d=\begin{cases}
t\nu\sqrt2 C_X/(\rho\sqrt e),&\mathrm{count},\\
0,&\mathrm{row},
\end{cases}\\
\epsilon_*=
\min\left\{\frac{d_D}{2C_X},
 \frac{10^{-2}}{C_X+C_W},\frac{d_*}{C_d}\right\},\\
C_E=(3C_W+1)C_d+C_W^2/V,\\
C_\eta=10^7C_W(C_X+C_W)+\frac{2\sqrt2 C_E}{1-c}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{NTFG.12}
$$

Here $d_*/C_d=+\infty$ when $C_d=0$, and
$1/V=0$ when the original cap is `None`.
These constants have only original parameters and
the specified entering-state/domain data as inputs.
For $0<q<1$, $n\ge1$, put

$$
M_{q,n}=4\log((n+2)/q),\qquad
\delta_{q,n}=8n e^{-M_{q,n}^2/4}.
\tag{NTFG.13}
$$

If $qnM_{q,n}\le\epsilon_*$, the ORIGINAL history
has, with probability at least $1-\delta_{q,n}$,
both walkers alive through every update $1,\ldots,n$,
its actual zero gates and unique nonself face records,
and all those literal faces available. Under the
coupled ORIGINAL source representation, on this event

$$
\begin{gathered}
\max_{l\le n}|X_l^q-x^*|\le C_XqnM_{q,n},
\qquad\max_{l\le n}|w_l^q|\le C_WM_{q,n},\\
\max_{l\le n}|w_l^q-w_l|
 \le\frac{C_E}{1-c}qnM_{q,n}^2,\\
\max_{l\le n}|\eta_l^q-\eta_l|
                         \le C_\eta qnM_{q,n}^2 .
\end{gathered}
\tag{NTFG.14}
$$

No source conditioning is imposed on the algorithm;
the full exceptional branch probability is included
in this estimate. Choose any actual update horizon
$n(q)\to\infty$ with $qn(q)^2\to0$.
For every fixed $K$, the last $K$ original two-face
phases converge jointly, with every fixed polynomial
moment, to the DERIVED stationary Gaussian channel
(NTFG.9)--(NTFG.10). The last position arrays converge
to the original base points and survival probability
tends to one. This is an actual joint parameter/time
limit of the executed gas; no invariant law for its
whole physical position process is asserted.

For a bounded Lipschitz test $O$ on that last
$2K$ phase window, its primitive expectation budget is

$$
\begin{aligned}
|E O(\eta^q_{n-K+1:n})-E_{\mathrm{stat}}O|
\le{}&\operatorname{Lip}(O)\sqrt K C_\eta qnM_{q,n}^2
       +2\|O\|_\infty\delta_{q,n}\\
&+\operatorname{Lip}(O)\sqrt{2K}(1-c)c^{n-K}
       \left(W_0+\sqrt{\frac6{1-c^2}}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{NTFG.15}
$$

The actual once-survivor-conditioned last window
has the same limit, because its conditioning event
has probability tending to one with the displayed
survival budget. Fixed final-alive masks, original
cap, both force normalizations and complete phase
source records therefore retain their derived scope.
Increasing-window action or moment assertions at
$c=1$, graph feedback, different source pools,
nonconstant reward or a thermostat-constrained
unavailable endpoint retain their actual separate
parameter regimes.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Use only the original Gaussian event
$\max_{l\le n}|G_l|\le M$, $M=M_{q,n}$.
For a six-dimensional standard Gaussian,
$E e^{|G|^2/4}=8$. Union and exponential Markov
give its complement probability at most
$8ne^{-M^2/4}=\delta_{q,n}$.
Every subsequent assertion is a deterministic
bound on this ORIGINAL event, followed by that
paid exceptional probability; the noise law is unchanged.

On an all-alive step, let $B_1,B_2$ be its actual
separately evaluated particle kick matrices.
For row normalization both equal $S$ exactly.
For count normalization
$\|B_j-S\|=t\nu|K_j-K_0|$.
The original kernel has global spatial gradient
bound $1/(\rho\sqrt e)$ and pair-difference map
norm $\sqrt2$. If every current/intermediate
position displacement is at most $C_XqnM$,
then $\|B_j-S\|\le C_d qnM\le d_*$.
Thus $\|B_j\|\le1+d_*$ and
$c\|B_2B_1\|\le c(1+d_*)^2\le(1+c)/2$.
The actual cap decreases Euclidean velocity norm,
so the scaled next velocity obeys
$|w_l^q|\le[(1+c)/2]|w_{l-1}^q|+2M$.
The radius $C_WM$ is preserved, including its
specified entering value.

Each actual pair of A drifts changes position
by at most
$qt[(1+c)(1+d_*)C_W+1]M\le C_XqM$.
Induction from $X_0=x^*$ gives the position
bound, also at A1 and at the separately evaluated
B2 force position. The condition with $d_D$
keeps every actual terminal row inside the domain,
so the asserted all-alive branch and its exact
zero clone gates are maintained at every step.
This closes the stopped induction: no alternative
gate/revival law was assumed after a possible exit.

The $10^{-2}$ condition keeps every pre and
final raw ray within the strict norm/overlap
neighborhood of the original base rays. At zero
perturbation its norm is one, its same-slot
overlap is one and its cross overlap is
$1/\sqrt2$. The displayed perturbation gives
norm at least $0.99$ and normalized overlaps
above $1/2$, larger than both original thresholds.
Thus these are the actual available recorded faces.

Subtract the original affine reference recursion
from the actual pre-cap update. With
$d=C_dqnM\le1$,
$\|B_2B_1-I\|\le2d+d^2\le3d$.
Its deterministic remainder from the two count
kicks is at most $(3C_W+1)dM$.
The actual finite-cap remainder is at most
$q C_W^2M^2/V$; it is zero for no cap.
Consequently
$|w_l^q-w_l|\le c|w_{l-1}^q-w_{l-1}|
 +C_E qnM^2$. Its geometric sum proves the
third bound of (NTFG.14).

For the phase estimate use its original raw
complex overlap product $Q$. On the indicated
position/velocity neighborhood, all three raw
ray norms are at most two, $|Q|\ge1/4$,
$|DQ|\le192$, $|D^2Q|\le480$.
These bounds follow by differentiating its
three bilinear overlaps: each factor has
modulus at most four, first derivative at most
four, and second derivative at most two.
Thus the operator second derivative of its
argument is bounded by
$480/(1/4)+192^2/(1/4)^2<10^6$.
Normalization by positive real ray norms
does not change this argument.

Crucially its phase is zero for EVERY nearby
configuration of real rays, not only at the
original base points. Taylor expand only in
imaginary velocities. The coefficient change
caused by the actual position displacements
costs at most a constant times $qnM^2$,
and its quadratic velocity remainder at most
a constant times $qM^2$ after division by $q$.
At the base point the complete linear coefficient
is exactly the already proved adjacent-velocity
expression (NTFG.3). Its difference between
actual and Gaussian velocities costs at most
$2\sqrt2 C_E qnM^2/(1-c)$ for the two-channel
vector. The larger stated $10^7$ polynomial
bound covers both phase Taylor terms, proving
the last estimate in (NTFG.14). This avoids
an erroneous quadratic cost from purely real
position changes whose phase is identically zero.

If $qn^2\to0$, eventually $n\le q^{-1/2}$,
so $M_{q,n}\le C\log(1/q)$.
Then $qnM_{q,n}\to0$ and
$qnM_{q,n}^2\to0$ by
$qn\le\sqrt q\sqrt{qn^2}$.
Moreover $\delta_{q,n}$ decreases faster than
every fixed power of $q$: its exponent is a
negative squared logarithm, whereas $n\le q^{-1/2}$.
The estimates therefore give convergence in
probability of the original last fixed phase
window to its Gaussian reference, with all
scaled-phase polynomial moments. On the exceptional
event the true masked phase is bounded by
$\pi/q$, so its $p$th moment contribution is
at most $C_{K,p}q^{-p}\delta_{q,n}\to0$;
the Gaussian reference has uniformly bounded
moments when $c<1$, and its exceptional contribution
vanishes by Cauchy--Schwarz and the same tail budget.

Couple that Gaussian reference with its already
derived invariant state using the same original
future sources. Their state difference at step
$l$ is $c^l(w_0-W_0^{\mathrm{stat}})$, and their
phase difference is
$(c-1)c^{l-1}L_i\cdot(w_{i,0}-W_{i,0}^{\mathrm{stat}})$.
The invariant Gaussian moment obeys
$E|W_0^{\mathrm{stat}}|\le\sqrt{6/(1-c^2)}$.
Combining that endpoint difference, the native
event estimates and bounded-test exceptional
budget gives (NTFG.15). Every fixed window has
the stationary limit and its stated moments.
Finally conditioning a bounded observation on
survival changes its expectation by at most
$2\|O\|_\infty P(\mathrm{nonsurvive})/
P(\mathrm{survive})$, which tends to zero by
the same original event. This proves the
once-conditioned scope without imposing an
unknown stationary law on physical positions.
:::

:::{prf:remark} Temporal correspondence and actual remaining endpoints
:label: rem-ntfg-scope

This derives both actual viscous kicks, original
stream innovations, finite-window drift/bracket,
full native phase-path action/source and a growing
native-time stationary LOCAL phase limit. At $c<1$
its native action has memory and its complete
additive phase variance is zero despite its nonzero
innovation bracket. At the independently configured
zero-friction diffusion-factor tag, $c=1$ and positive
$q$ is attainable; each finite native window instead
has independent phase increments and original-unit
path-action matching. The inverse-temperature-linked
tag retains its $q=0$ endpoint and is not assigned
that positive-noise process.

The result uses the dense real-coordinate canonical
count/row gas. Its two-row algebra is not assigned
to Python empty CSR or floored row normalization,
or to finite arithmetic underflow at extreme
unbounded source inputs. Nonzero landscapes,
asymmetric/historical donor pools, unequal reward
feedback, accepted clones and different kinetic
forces retain their original laws. The original
survival and missing-ray branches have been paid
in the stated joint limit rather than suppressed.

This two-face temporal ray channel does not identify
the different native B2 non-Abelian color connection
or its physical local algebra. It does establish
the exact complete action and fluctuation behavior
of an existing native gauge readout in substantive
included parameter regimes, including which apparent
one-step action and bracket matches persist through
the actual repeated algorithm.
:::

## 2_fractal_set/23_native_two_walker_color_reconstruction.md

:::{prf:definition} Native two-walker color register
:label: def-ntc-register

Retain the complete execution record of
{prf:ref}`def-native-complete-execution-record`.
The algorithm is its EXISTING real-coordinate canonical dense gas,
with $N=2,d=3$, current nonself count-one measurement and cloning
companions, quadratic force/reward at $\lambda=0$, unbounded alive
domain, original BAOAB step $h>0$, damping $\gamma>0$ and positive
constant isotropic Gaussian diffusion amplitude $b_O$.
Put

$$
t=h/2,\quad \nu=1/t,\quad \rho>0,\quad
c=e^{-\gamma h}\in(0,1),\quad
q^2=b_O^2(1-c^2)/(2\gamma)>0,\quad
\sigma^2=q^2/(1-c^2)=b_O^2/(2\gamma).
\tag{NTC.1}
$$

Both original viscous kicks use the configured off-diagonal
ROW normalization. There is no viscosity degree cap, volume
weighting, neighbor penalty, graph feedback, elite or history
donor, adaptive force/diffusion, curl or innovation shift.
The configured final velocity cap is `None` and the configured
terminal position diffusion is zero. These are existing parameter
branches, not deletions made inside the proof.
The actual boundary is unbounded/all-alive. The original donor
widths, fitness powers, positive standardizers and rescale,
clone schedule, acceptance scale, jitter amplitude and collision
coefficient remain arbitrary configured finite values consistent
with the canonical pipeline. The two nonself companions are
the unique other walker at every update.
Retain the original positive time calibration $t_*>0$, energy
scale $\hbar_{\rm eff}>0$ and integer recording stride $m\ge1$.

This dense real-coordinate force is directly bound to
`QftExecutionConfig.viscosity` in Rust `kinetic.rs`:
the off-diagonal Gaussian mass is its actual denominator,
without a $10^{-12}$ floor. Dense and graph viscosity are
mutually exclusive. Rust records the B1 viscous force and
the matching `force_input_velocity` with their stage/version.
Its recorded color channel consumes those inputs at B1.
The finite-float zero-mass branch and addressed finite random
stream are distinct arithmetic laws; exact Gaussian Mehler
claims below use the continuous independent-Gaussian real tag.

The Python `EuclideanGas` graph branch is different:
at $N=2,d=3$ its ordinary Delaunay/Voronoi constructions return
empty edges, so that kinetic viscous force is zero. Its Gaussian
edge row normalization also has a $10^{-12}$ mass floor.
Neither is silently identified with this dense native transition.

Use a fixed ORIGINAL supplied phase coefficient $\kappa$ and
the original strict force threshold $\delta\ge0$. For the Rust
recorded color request these are the consumed values after its
literal clamps: $\kappa\in[-\pi,\pi]$, $\delta\in[10^{-15},1]$.
Other original color instruments retain their actual threshold
and phase ranges. In particular the actual Rust angle zero is
