an available fixed-phase branch; no inferred position calibration
is frozen to manufacture it.

Let $\Delta=v_2-v_1$, $R=|\Delta|$, and
$A=\mathbf1_{\{\nu R>\delta\}}$. The available B1 colors are

$$
c_{1a}=\frac{\Delta_a}{R}e^{i\kappa v_{1a}},\qquad
c_{2a}=-\frac{\Delta_a}{R}e^{i\kappa v_{2a}}.
\tag{NTC.2}
$$

At unavailable slots the original raw normalization/mask remains
in the record. The executed ray-projector descriptor used below
is $P_i=A c_i c_i^\dagger$, zero on unavailable slots, together
with $A$. This is the existing projector derived from the
recorded colors, not an added sampled coordinate.
Raw color representatives and the common-$SU(3)$ scalar orbit
dictionary are distinguished below.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact two-walker dense-row BAOAB factor
:label: thm-ntc-native-factor

In the register above every actual cloning gate is zero.
There is no accepted clone, applied recipient jitter or
nontrivial collision component. Both B kicks are exactly
the walker-swap matrix
$S(v_1,v_2)=(v_2,v_1)$.
The complete native update satisfies

$$
v_{n+1}=cv_n+qS G_n,\qquad
x_{n+1}=x_n+t[(1+c)S v_n+qG_n],
\quad G_n\sim N(0,I_6)\ \hbox{independently}.
\tag{NTC.3}
$$

The actual B1 projector/color readout is a deterministic
function of $v_n$ through (NTC.2). Its velocity factor has
the unique invariant probability $\mu=N(0,\sigma^2I_6)$.
With that velocity marginal the entire recorded color history
is stationary for any compatible original position initial law.
The full unbounded position/velocity chain has NO invariant
probability.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The two configured reward values are identically zero.
The unique current nonself companions give the SAME symmetric
algorithmic distance to both measurement slots. Hence every
actual standardized reward and diversity value, positive rescale
and fitness is equal across the two walkers, including every tie.
Their actual acceptance scores
$(V_j-V_i)/[s_c(V_i+\epsilon_c)]$ are zero.
The alive marks are both one, so mandatory revival never applies.
The original simultaneous-copy, jitter and collision algorithms
therefore act as identities for every realized draw. Reserved
unused random addresses remain passive records.

At either kick the one off-diagonal Gaussian weight is strictly
positive at every finite position. Dividing it by its SAME
row mass gives weight one, regardless of $\rho$ and positions.
The viscous force is $\nu(v_j-v_i)$.
Since $t\nu=1$, $v_i+t\nu(v_j-v_i)=v_j$.
After B1, A1, O, A2 and B2 respectively the velocities/positions
are $Sv$, $x+tSv$, $cSv+qG$,
$x+t[(1+c)Sv+qG]$ and $cv+qSG$.
This proves the literal stage identities.

The swap is orthogonal, so $SG$ is again an original standard
Gaussian vector, independently at each update.
The stationary covariance equation is
$\sigma^2=c^2\sigma^2+q^2$.
For any invariant velocity law with characteristic function
$\phi$, iteration gives
$\phi(u)=\phi(c^nu)\exp[-q^2(1-c^{2n})|u|^2/
 [2(1-c^2)]]$. Continuity at zero identifies uniquely $\mu$.
The same formula gives convergence from any initial velocity law.

For the complete state, write
$C_n=(x_{1n}+x_{2n})/2$, $M_n=(v_{1n}+v_{2n})/2$.
Exactly,
$M_{n+1}=cM_n+q\overline G_n$,
$C_{n+1}=C_n+t(M_n+M_{n+1})$,
where $\overline G_n\sim N(0,I_3/2)$ independently.
The existing state function

$$
B_n=C_n+\frac{t(1+c)}{1-c}M_n
$$

therefore satisfies
$B_{n+1}=B_n+[2tq/(1-c)]\overline G_n$.
If a full-state invariant probability existed, its $B$ marginal
would be invariant under this nondegenerate independent Gaussian
translation. Its characteristic function would satisfy
$\phi_B(u)=\phi_B(u)e^{-t^2q^2|u|^2/(1-c)^2}$.
It would vanish at every nonzero $u$, contradicting continuity
at zero. The stationary color factor consequently does not
assert nonexistent full-position stationarity.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Native six-dimensional positive Mehler transfer
:label: thm-ntc-mehler

The velocity observable transfer is exactly

$$
\mathcal P f(v)=\int f(cv+qg)\,\gamma_6(dg)
\quad\hbox{on }L^2(\mu).
\tag{NTC.4}
$$

It is a self-adjoint positive injective contraction, with
orthogonal Hermite eigenspaces $\mathcal H_k$ of total degree $k$:

$$
\mathcal P|_{\mathcal H_k}=c^kI,\qquad
\dim\mathcal H_k=\binom{k+5}{5},\qquad
\operatorname{spec}\mathcal P=\{c^k:k\ge0\}\cup\{0\}.
\tag{NTC.5}
$$

Zero is not an eigenvalue. The constant vacuum is the unique
unit-eigenvalue sector. The native frequency Hamiltonian and
physical-energy convention are

$$
\mathsf H=-\frac1{t_*h}\log\mathcal P,\qquad
H_{\rm energy}=\hbar_{\rm eff}\mathsf H,\qquad
\mathsf H|_{\mathcal H_k}=\frac{\gamma k}{t_*}I.
\tag{NTC.6}
$$

The centered complete-velocity gap is $\gamma/t_*$, or
$\hbar_{\rm eff}\gamma/t_*$ in energy units.
For the existing recording stride $m\ge1$, its original
sampled transfer is $\mathcal P^m$ and clock $mt_*h$,
giving the SAME calibrated frequency Hamiltonian.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The stationary pair $(v_n,v_{n+1})$ is centered jointly Gaussian
with covariance blocks $\sigma^2I_6$ and $c\sigma^2I_6$.
Its law is unchanged by exchanging its two entries, which proves
self-adjointness from their actual two-time correlation.
For a standard normal vector $z=v/\sigma$, the original kernel is
$z'=cz+\sqrt{1-c^2}\,g$.
Apply it to the generating function
$\exp(u\cdot z-|u|^2/2)$:
its conditional expectation is
$\exp(cu\cdot z-c^2|u|^2/2)$.
Comparing its polynomial coefficients proves the Hermite
eigenvalues $c^k$. Gaussian integration of two generating
functions proves their orthogonality and factorial norms.

For completeness, if an $L^2$ function is orthogonal to all
these polynomials, its Gaussian-weighted moment-generating
function has all derivatives zero at zero and is entire,
by Cauchy--Schwarz with Gaussian exponential moments.
It is therefore zero on imaginary arguments. Fourier uniqueness,
or Gaussian convolution and Fourier inversion followed by
removal of that convolution, makes the function zero.
Thus the normalized Hermites form a complete orthonormal basis.
Every coefficient is multiplied by a strictly positive $c^k$,
proving positivity and injectivity. Their finite multiplicities
and $c^k\to0$ give compactness and (NTC.5), including its
non-eigenvalue zero. Spectral calculus defines the self-adjoint
log on its natural squared-Hermite-weight domain, with the
energies stated in (NTC.6). No finite edge matrix or freely
assigned exponential transfer appears in this correspondence.
:::

:::{prf:definition} Native color dictionary and history sector
:label: def-ntc-color-sector

Let $D_{\kappa,\delta}(v)=(A,P_1,P_2)$ be the actual available
ray-color dictionary above. Let $\mathcal A_D$ consist of its
bounded complex measurable functions, including constants.
Define its one-time cyclic native sector

$$
\mathcal K_{\rm cyc}
=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{
 \mathcal P^na(D): n\ge0,\ a\in\mathcal A_D\}\subset L^2(\mu).
\tag{NTC.7}
$$

For the COMPLETE color history, the physical sector is

$$
\mathcal K_{\rm hist}=
\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{
 M_{a_0}\mathcal P^{n_1}M_{a_1}\cdots
       \mathcal P^{n_j}M_{a_j}1:
 j\ge0,\ n_l\ge1,\ a_l\in\mathcal A_D\}.
\tag{NTC.8}
$$

It is the minimal closed sector containing constants and invariant
under the actual $\mathcal P$ and multiplication by original bounded
color observables. The closure of conditional predictions of ALL
finite future color cylinders is exactly $\mathcal K_{\rm hist}$.
Ordinary $\mathcal P$-cyclic closure (NTC.7) need not equal that
complete-history closure; both sectors are retained.
There is no additional Gauss projection or assumed local CAR mode.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Positive reconstruction of the complete native ray-color history
:label: thm-ntc-color-reconstruction

The stationary native two-sided color history is reflection positive
for integer-site reflection and for the original adjacent-time
reflection. Its site-reflection quotient completion is exactly
$\mathcal K_{\rm hist}$, with inner product inherited from $L^2(\mu)$.
The reconstructed one-update transfer is the RESTRICTION of
the actual native $\mathcal P$ to this sector.
It is positive, self-adjoint and injective. Its logarithm is the
restriction of (NTC.6); the vacuum is unique and every nonvacuum
frequency is an integer multiple of $\gamma/t_*$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Construct the stationary two-sided velocity law from its derived
Gaussian stationary marginal and actual reversible transition.
For a bounded future color cylinder $F$ at nonnegative times define
$J F(v_0)=E[F\mid v_0]$. Conditional on the actual $v_0$,
the past and future velocity paths are independent; the reflected
past has the SAME conditional law as the future by the proved
reversibility. Thus for cylinders $F,G$,

$$
E[\overline{F\circ\theta_0}\,G]
=\langle JF,JG\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}.
\tag{NTC.9}
$$

The null space is exactly $\{F:JF=0\}$. For cylinder products,
the original Markov conditional-expectation formula gives exactly
the words in (NTC.8); linear combinations of these products
generate bounded cylinder tests and their $L^2$ completion.
This identifies the quotient Hilbert space without assuming
observed color is itself a Markov process.

Moving every cylinder time forward by one actual update gives
$J(\tau F)=\mathcal P(JF)$.
Multiplying at time zero by $a(D)$ gives $J(aF)=M_aJF$.
Hence its image closure is invariant under both operations,
and the reconstructed transfer is the claimed native restriction.
Since $\mathcal P$ is self-adjoint, this invariant closed
subspace reduces it: its orthogonal complement is invariant
by the inner-product identity. Positivity and injectivity
therefore restrict as well.

For adjacent-time reflection $n\mapsto1-n$ and future cylinders
starting at time one, the same actual Markov disintegration gives
the form $\langle JF,\mathcal P JG\rangle$.
Its diagonal is nonnegative by the derived positivity of
$\mathcal P$. This supplies positive transfer as well as the
site-reflection Gram positivity.
Spectral calculus on the reducing sector gives its log and
energies; the constant eigenspace of the full transfer is already
one dimensional. Every statement concerns the ORIGINAL color
history of (NTC.2), including the original availability mask.
:::

:::{prf:definition} Original Gaussian threshold moment
:label: def-ntc-threshold-moment

Under the DERIVED stationary velocity law,
$\Delta\sim N(0,2\sigma^2I_3)$.
Its primitive active radial second moment is

$$
\mathfrak m_2=
E[R^2\mathbf1_{\{\nu R>\delta\}}]
=4\sigma^2
\frac{\Gamma(5/2,\delta^2/(4\nu^2\sigma^2))}
     {\Gamma(3/2)}>0
\quad\hbox{for every finite }\delta\ge0.
\tag{NTC.10}
$$

At zero threshold it is $6\sigma^2$.
The original available-color probability is likewise
$\Gamma(3/2,\delta^2/(4\nu^2\sigma^2))/\Gamma(3/2)>0$.
These are explicit integrals of original Gaussian draws.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact zero-phase projector/history gap
:label: thm-ntc-zero-phase-gap

At the original fixed phase $\kappa=0$, both
$\mathcal K_{\rm cyc}$ and $\mathcal K_{\rm hist}$
have exact nonvacuum frequency gap $2\gamma/t_*$.
In energy units the gap is $2\hbar_{\rm eff}\gamma/t_*$.
It is nontrivial for every finite threshold $\delta$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
At $\kappa=0$,
$P_1=P_2=A\,\Delta\Delta^\top/R^2$.
The full dictionary is invariant under central inversion
$(v_1,v_2)\mapsto(-v_1,-v_2)$.
Multiplication by its bounded functions and the native transfer
preserve the globally EVEN subspace of $L^2(\mu)$.
Both sectors are therefore even: every odd-total-degree
Hermite coefficient, in particular degree one, vanishes.

For $a\ne b$, the ORIGINAL bounded off-diagonal readout is
$(P_1)_{ab}=A\Delta_a\Delta_b/R^2$.
Its inner product with the degree-two Hermite polynomial
$\Delta_a\Delta_b$ is exactly

$$
E[\Delta_a\Delta_b(P_1)_{ab}]
=E[A\Delta_a^2\Delta_b^2/R^2]
=\mathfrak m_2/15>0 .
\tag{NTC.11}
$$

The last equality is angular Gaussian integration:
for the uniform sphere direction in three dimensions,
$E[n_a^2n_b^2]=1/15$. It also follows by expanding
$E|G|^4=15$ and the independent $E G_a^2G_b^2=1$.
This readout therefore has a nonzero degree-two projection.
That projection belongs already to $\mathcal K_{\rm cyc}$:
the isolated spectral projector for $c^2$ is a continuous
function of the native compact $\mathcal P$ on its spectrum,
and its polynomial approximations preserve cyclic closure.
Consequently both sectors contain an actual eigenvector
at frequency $2\gamma/t_*$, and their even parity excludes
any lower nonvacuum frequency. This proves the exact gap.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Primitive positive phase interval with exact first-mode gap
:label: thm-ntc-small-phase-gap

Put

$$
C_3=\sqrt{30}\,\sigma^4/6,\qquad
\kappa_*=
\left[\frac{\mathfrak m_2}{20\sqrt{30}\,\sigma^4}\right]^{1/2}>0.
\tag{NTC.12}
$$

For every original fixed phase $0<|\kappa|\le\kappa_*$,
intersected with its instrument's actual allowed parameter range,
both native ray-color sectors have exact gap $\gamma/t_*$
and energy gap $\hbar_{\rm eff}\gamma/t_*$.
For each pair $a\ne b$ the original projector readout has
the quantitative first-Hermite coefficient

$$
\left|E[v_{1a}\,\Im(P_1)_{ab}]\right|
\ge\frac{|\kappa|\mathfrak m_2}{120}>0.
\tag{NTC.13}
$$

Hence a nonzero native first mode is proved from the actual
Gaussian law, even at a positive hard threshold.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Let $M=(v_1+v_2)/2$, independent of $\Delta$, with
$M\sim N(0,\sigma^2I_3/2)$ and $v_1=M-\Delta/2$.
For $L=v_{1a}-v_{1b}$ define
$j(\kappa)=E[v_{1a}A\Delta_a\Delta_b R^{-2}\sin(\kappa L)]$.
Its derivative at zero is finite by original Gaussian moments.
Conditional on $\Delta$,

$$
E[v_{1a}L\mid\Delta]
=\sigma^2/2+\Delta_a(\Delta_a-\Delta_b)/4.
$$

Angular parity kills its $\sigma^2$ and cubic-cross terms
after multiplying by $A\Delta_a\Delta_b/R^2$.
The remaining term gives exactly
$j'(0)=-\mathfrak m_2/60$.

The original inequality
$|\sin u-u|\le|u|^3/6$ and
$|\Delta_a\Delta_b|/R^2\le1/2$ give

$$
|j(\kappa)+\kappa\mathfrak m_2/60|
\le\frac{|\kappa|^3}{12}E[|v_{1a}||L|^3]
\le C_3|\kappa|^3.
\tag{NTC.14}
$$

Indeed $E v_{1a}^2=\sigma^2$ and
$E L^6=15(2\sigma^2)^3=120\sigma^6$;
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the displayed constant.
The threshold indicator only decreases this remainder bound.
For $|\kappa|\le\kappa_*$ its cubic remainder is at most
$|\kappa|\mathfrak m_2/120$, proving (NTC.13).
Since $v_{1a}$ is a native degree-one Hermite function, the
actual bounded observable has a nonzero projection to
$\mathcal H_1$. The same isolated spectral-projection argument
puts it in both native sectors. The full transfer has no
frequency between zero and $\gamma/t_*$, proving the exact gap.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Every nonzero original phase has the exact joint color gap
:label: thm-ntc-all-phase-gap

For EVERY finite original fixed phase $\kappa\ne0$ and finite
threshold $\delta$, both two-row native ray-color sectors
$\mathcal K_{\rm cyc}$ and $\mathcal K_{\rm hist}$ have exact
frequency gap $\gamma/t_*$.
For $a\ne b$, the original bounded joint color readout obeys

$$
E\!\left[v_{1a}\,
 \Im\big((P_1)_{ab}(P_2)_{ab}\big)\right]
=\frac{\kappa\sigma^2}{15}
 \frac{\Gamma(3/2,\delta^2/(4\nu^2\sigma^2))}
      {\Gamma(3/2)}
 e^{-2\kappa^2\sigma^2}\ne0 .
\tag{NTC.15}
$$

This retains the two original recorded projectors and their
common force-availability event; no new trajectory variable or
phase calibration is consumed.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The two actual off-diagonal projector entries multiply to

$$
(P_1)_{ab}(P_2)_{ab}
=A\frac{\Delta_a^2\Delta_b^2}{R^4}
       e^{2i\kappa(M_a-M_b)}.
$$

The derived stationary center $M$ and difference $\Delta$
are independent. The expectation of $\Delta_a$ times
$A\Delta_a^2\Delta_b^2/R^4$ is zero by sign symmetry.
The remaining $M_a$ contribution satisfies, by differentiation
of its original Gaussian characteristic function,

$$
E[M_a\sin(2\kappa(M_a-M_b))]
=\kappa\sigma^2e^{-2\kappa^2\sigma^2}.
$$

Its independent angular/radial multiplier is
$E[A\Delta_a^2\Delta_b^2/R^4]=P(A=1)/15$.
This proves (NTC.15). The readout is a bounded function of
the actual joint dictionary, and $v_{1a}$ is a degree-one
Hermite polynomial. The nonzero degree-one spectral projection
therefore belongs to $\mathcal K_{\rm cyc}$ and hence to
$\mathcal K_{\rm hist}$, by the same native spectral calculus
already proved. The complete transfer's first positive
frequency is $\gamma/t_*$, proving equality.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Native full harmonic population and resonant recorded transfer
:label: thm-nhr-full-positive-transfer

Every actual clone gate is zero in this register.
The unchanged full state is a product of $3N$ two-coordinate
linear Gaussian chains. On each original $(x_a,v_a)$ pair put

$$
\begin{gathered}
p=1-t^2\lambda(1+c),\quad b=t(1+c),\\
D=c-t^2\lambda(1+c),\quad k=-t\lambda(c+p),\\
A=\begin{pmatrix}p&b\\k&D\end{pmatrix},\qquad
Q=q^2\binom{t}{E}(t,E)+s^2\binom{1}{0}(1,0).
\end{gathered}
\tag{NHR.4}
$$

Its exact update is $Z_{n+1}=AZ_n+\eta_n$ with independent
centered Gaussian innovations of covariance $Q$.
The full physical state has the unique invariant probability
$\mu_N=N(0,C\otimes I_{3N})$, with all original position
components followed by all velocity components. The covariance is the FINITE
primitive formula

$$
r=c^{m/2}\in(0,1),\qquad
A^m=rI,\qquad
C=\frac1{1-r^2}
       \sum_{l=0}^{m-1}A^lQ(A^l)^\top\succ0 .
\tag{NHR.5}
$$

The actual recorded-state transfer is exactly

$$
\mathcal P_m f(z)=
 E f\!\left(rz+\sqrt{1-r^2}\,C_N^{1/2}G\right),
\qquad C_N=C\otimes I_{3N},\quad G\sim N(0,I_{6N}).
\tag{NHR.6}
$$

It is positive, injective and self-adjoint on $L^2(\mu_N)$.
Its Hermite spectrum and native frequency Hamiltonian are

$$
\mathcal P_m|_{\mathcal H_k}=r^kI,\qquad
\mathsf H_m=-\frac1{mt_*h}\log\mathcal P_m,\qquad
\mathsf H_m|_{\mathcal H_k}=\frac{\gamma k}{2t_*}I.
\tag{NHR.7}
$$

The vacuum is unique. The exact complete-state gap
$\gamma/(2t_*)$, or $\hbar_{\rm eff}\gamma/(2t_*)$ in energy
units, is uniform in every admitted $N$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The original nonnegative fitness exponents permit zero:
each positive channel raised to exponent zero is one.
Thus every consumed positive fitness is equal, regardless of
the actual rewards, distances or sampled donors. Every living
acceptance score is zero, including ties and any clone schedule.
The all-alive boundary excludes revival. No accepted copy, applied
jitter or nontrivial collision component occurs for ANY original
source realization. Reserved donor, gate, jitter and Haar records
remain passive.

At zero viscosity the two actual B kicks use $-\lambda x$.
B1 gives $v_1=v-t\lambda x$; A1 gives
$p_1=Ex+tv$; O gives $z=cv_1+q\xi$; A2 gives
$y=p_1+tz$; B2 gives $u=z-t\lambda y$.
The terminal position map adds the original $s\zeta$ to $y$,
after B2; its configured diffusion does not enter that earlier
force evaluation. Hence $(y+s\zeta,u)=A(x,v)+q(t,E)\xi+(s,0)\zeta$.
This proves (NHR.4), including the stage placement of BOTH
original Gaussian sources.

Direct calculation gives $\det A=c$ and
$\operatorname{tr}A=(1+c)(1-2t^2\lambda)$.
Equation (NHR.3) puts its distinct eigenvalues at
$\sqrt c\,e^{\pm i\theta}$; it also gives $0<t^2\lambda<1$.
Its characteristic polynomial therefore proves $A^m=rI$
without changing any intermediate update.
The stable affine recursion has covariance
$\sum_{l\ge0}A^lQ(A^l)^\top$.
Grouping this convergent series into original $m$-step blocks
gives exactly (NHR.5).

Positivity of $C$ follows already from the original OU source.
For $B=q(t,E)^\top$,

$$
\det[B,AB]=-2tE q^2\ne0 .
$$

Thus $BB^\top+ABB^\top A^\top$ is positive definite;
the finite sum in (NHR.5) contains both terms.
The additional original $s^2$ contribution is nonnegative,
including its existing zero-amplitude branch.
Iteration of an invariant characteristic function, using
$A^n\to0$, gives the displayed unique Gaussian law.
It also gives convergence from any original initial state law.
Different pairs use their original independent source coordinates,
so their full invariant law is the product asserted, rather than
an assumed invariant relative law.

The actual $m$-step Gaussian innovation has covariance
$C-A^mC(A^m)^\top=(1-r^2)C$.
This proves the literal transition (NHR.6).
Its stationary pair law is Gaussian with covariance blocks
$C_N$ and $rC_N$, invariant under swapping the two times.
Whitening by the DERIVED positive covariance gives the same
Mehler generating-function calculation as
{prf:ref}`thm-ntc-mehler` in dimension $6N$.
Consequently its complete orthogonal Hermite basis has
eigenvalues $r^k>0$, finite multiplicities and no zero eigenvector;
zero belongs to the compact transfer's spectrum.
Taking the log on its actual reducing Hermite domains gives
(NHR.7), since $-\log r/(mh)=\gamma/2$.
There is no freely assigned transfer or Hamiltonian.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Full native recorded-field color reflection and reconstruction
:label: thm-nhr-color-reconstruction

At every recorded B1 input the original color is

$$
a_i=\mathbf1_{\{\lambda|x_i|>\delta\}},\qquad
(c_i)_a=-\frac{x_{ia}}{|x_i|}e^{i\kappa v_{ia}}

The literal zero extension and matched clone-deletion mask

Both the COMPLETE raw-color dictionary

For either dictionary their exact physical Hilbert space is

\mathcal K_D=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{
 M_{f_0}\mathcal P_m^{n_1}M_{f_1}\cdots

threshold and phase calibration of the configured instrument.

:::{prf:proof}
The emitted B1 fields are exactly $-\lambda x_i$ and $v_i$

normalization give (NHR.8). Their source masks cover every

available probability is positive at every finite threshold.

The complete recorded-state chain is the actual positive reversible
Gaussian chain (NHR.6). For each future color cylinder $F$ define

proved time reversibility give

$$
E[\overline{F\circ\theta_0}G]=\langle JF,JG\rangle,\qquad
E[\overline{F\circ\theta_{1/2}}G]
                         =\langle JF,\mathcal P_mJG\rangle .
\tag{NHR.10}
$$

In the second form future cylinders start at the next recorded

The first form's null space is exactly $\ker J$.
The actual Markov conditional-expectation formula produces the
words in (NHR.9), and finite cylinder products generate its

by the original stride correspond to $M_f$ and $\mathcal P_m$.
Thus this is the minimal closed complete-history sector under
the ACTUAL observation and transfer, not merely a one-time

It is invariant under the self-adjoint transfer, hence reducing.
Positivity, injectivity, the log, vacuum uniqueness and the full

:::{prf:definition} Derived original threshold moments and velocity residual
:label: def-nhr-color-moments

Put $X=C_{11}>0$, $V=C_{22}>0$, $B=C_{12}$,
$\beta=B/X$ and $\upsilon=V-B^2/X>0$.
These are the finite primitive matrix entries in (NHR.5).
For one original row, $x\sim N(0,XI_3)$ and
$v=\beta x+\sqrt\upsilon\,G$, with $G$ independent standard

Writing $R=|x|$, $u=\delta^2/(2\lambda^2X)$ gives

p_A=P(\lambda R>\delta)
      =\frac{\Gamma(3/2,u)}{\Gamma(3/2)}>0,\qquad
m_b=E[R^b\mathbf1_{\{\lambda R>\delta\}}]
      =(2X)^{b/2}
        \frac{\Gamma((3+b)/2,u)}{\Gamma(3/2)}
        \quad(b\ge0).
\tag{NHR.11}
$$

All moments retain the ORIGINAL unbounded Gaussian law.

:::{prf:theorem} Exact projector gap on a primitive positive phase interval
:label: thm-nhr-projector-gap

For arbitrary original $\sigma_x\ge0$ define

$$
C_0=\frac{\upsilon p_A}{15}+\frac{\beta^2m_2}{35}>0,\qquad
C_3=\frac{2\sqrt{30}}3V^2,\qquad
\kappa_{\rm ray}=\sqrt{C_0/C_3}>0 .
\tag{NHR.12}
$$

For every original fixed $0<\kappa\le\kappa_{\rm ray}$ the
complete native ray-color sector has exact frequency gap
$\gamma/(2t_*)$ and energy gap
$\hbar_{\rm eff}\gamma/(2t_*)$, uniformly in $N$.
For $a\ne b$ its original bounded squared-entry readout satisfies

$$
\left|E[v_a\Im(P_{ab}^2)]\right|\ge\kappa C_0>0 .
\tag{NHR.13}
$$

In the existing branch $\sigma_x=0$, this conclusion holds for
EVERY original finite positive phase: its exact coefficient is

$$
C=\begin{pmatrix}
q^2/[\lambda(1-c^2)]&0\\
0&E q^2/(1-c^2)
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
E[v_a\Im(P_{ab}^2)]
 =\frac{2\kappa Vp_A}{15}e^{-4\kappa^2V}\ne0 .
\tag{NHR.14}
$$

If a different original instrument allows zero phase, its
ray-projector history at that endpoint has exact gap $\gamma/t_*$.
The present positive-mass spectroscopy tag does not consume that
endpoint.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The original squared entry is
$P_{ab}^2=a\,x_a^2x_b^2R^{-4}e^{2i\kappa(v_a-v_b)}$.
Conditional on $x$,
$E[v_a(v_a-v_b)\mid x]=\upsilon+\beta^2x_a(x_a-x_b)$.
The angular identities
$E[n_a^2n_b^2]=1/15$ and
$E[n_a^4n_b^2]=1/35$ for $a\ne b$, and odd sign symmetry,
give derivative at phase zero exactly $2C_0$.
This derivative is computed from the known original Gaussian
formula; it does not require a zero-phase algorithm parameter.

Since $x_a^2x_b^2/R^4\le1/4$,
$|\sin z-z|\le|z|^3/6$ gives

$$
|E[v_a\Im(P_{ab}^2)]-2\kappa C_0|
\le\frac{\kappa^3}{3}E[|v_a||v_a-v_b|^3]
\le C_3\kappa^3 .
$$

The marginal velocities are independent across ambient components
with variance $V$, so Cauchy--Schwarz uses
$E[v_a^2]=V$ and $E[(v_a-v_b)^6]=120V^3$.
For the stated interval the error is at most $\kappa C_0$.
The bounded actual projector function has a nonzero projection
to the full transfer's degree-one Hermite space. Its isolated
spectral projection belongs to the complete color-history
sector, by polynomial approximation to that actual transfer's
spectral projection. The complete-state gap proves equality.

When $s=0$, substitution of the displayed diagonal covariance
into $C=ACA^\top+q^2(t,E)^\top(t,E)$ proves it exactly.
The stationary position and velocity are consequently independent.
Their angular/radial factor is $p_A/15$ and the original Gaussian
identity
$E[v_a\sin(2\kappa(v_a-v_b))]
 =2\kappa V e^{-4\kappa^2V}$ proves (NHR.14) for all phases.
At a permitted zero phase the dictionary is globally even,
so every odd-total-degree Hermite coefficient vanishes.
Its actual off-diagonal projector has
$E[x_ax_bP_{ab}]=m_2/15>0$.
It therefore contains degree two and its exact gap is twice
the full Mehler gap, as asserted.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact raw-color gap without changing its representative
:label: thm-nhr-raw-gap

For every original $\sigma_x\ge0$ put

       \left[\frac{m_1}{9\sqrt X\,V}\right]^{1/2}>0 .

$$

At every $0<\kappa\le\kappa_{\rm raw}$ the COMPLETE raw-color

 =-\frac{m_1}{3}e^{-\kappa^2V/2}\ne0 .

:::{prf:proof}
At phase zero the coefficient is $-m_1/3$ by angular integration.
Its change at positive phase is bounded, using the original

$\kappa^2 E[R v_a^2]/2\le
3\kappa^2\sqrt X\,V/2$.

The stated interval leaves a coefficient of magnitude at least

:::{prf:theorem} Complete harmonic recording-stride positivity classification
:label: thm-nhr-stride-classification

In the SAME existing harmonic/$\nu=0$/constant-fitness branch,
now retain any original $0<t^2\lambda<1$ and integer recording
stride $m\ge1$, without imposing (NHR.3).
Its full invariant covariance is the derived positive series
$C=\sum_{l\ge0}A^lQ(A^l)^\top$.
Put $\tau=(1+c)(1-2t^2\lambda)$.
The complete recorded-state transfer is self-adjoint if and only
if its $A^m$ is scalar. The scalar occurs exactly in the
complex-root regime $|\tau|<2\sqrt c$, where

$$
\theta=\arccos(\tau/(2\sqrt c))\in(0,\pi),\qquad
m\theta\in\pi\mathbb Z,\qquad
A^m=(-1)^{m\theta/\pi}c^{m/2}I .
\tag{NHR.17}
$$

It is a POSITIVE self-adjoint transfer if and only if
$m\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z$.
Distinct real roots or a repeated root give no self-adjoint
complete transfer at any finite stride.
At an odd scalar resonance the full transfer has actual negative
first-Hermite eigenvalues and fails the positive-transfer test.
These are exact native full-state tests, including every original
$q>0,s\ge0$; failure of one is not automatically assigned to a
smaller color-only observable sector.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The strict harmonic stability $0<t^2\lambda<1$, determinant
$c\in(0,1)$ and endpoint characteristic-polynomial tests give
spectral radius less than one, as already derived in
{prf:ref}`def-nct-lyapunov-budget`.
The same source controllability determinant above makes $C$
positive for every $s\ge0$.
The stationary Gaussian pair has cross covariance $A^mC$.
It is exchange invariant exactly when
$A^mC=C(A^m)^\top$; exchange invariance is equivalent to
self-adjointness of its actual observable kernel.
For necessity one may already test its original linear coordinates.

Let $S=AC-CA^\top$.
The stationary covariance equation gives
$S=ASA^\top+AQ-QA^\top$.
Every two-dimensional skew matrix satisfies $ASA^\top=cS$,
and the actual source vectors in (NHR.4) give

$$
S_{12}=\frac{2tE q^2-ks^2}{1-c}>0,\qquad
k=-t\lambda(1+c)E<0 .
\tag{NHR.18}
$$

Thus the original one-update kernel is never complete-state
reversible on this strict branch; extra terminal position noise
does not cancel its antisymmetric covariance.
By Cayley--Hamilton write $A^m=u_mA+v_mI$.
Then $A^mC-C(A^m)^\top=u_mS$, so the full recorded transfer is
reversible exactly when $u_m=0$.
For distinct roots $\lambda_\pm$,
$u_m=(\lambda_+^m-\lambda_-^m)/(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)$.
If they are real their positive product is $c$ and their signs
agree; distinct same-sign magnitudes cannot have equal $m$th
powers. For a repeated root $\lambda_0=\pm\sqrt c$,
$u_m=m\lambda_0^{m-1}\ne0$; $A$ is not scalar since $b>0$.
For complex roots,
$u_m=c^{(m-1)/2}\sin(m\theta)/\sin\theta$.
Its zero condition is exactly (NHR.17), and the scalar is
the displayed signed value.

At an even scalar resonance the actual Gaussian transfer is
the positive Mehler operator already derived.
At an odd resonance its first Hermite eigenvalue is the
negative scalar $-c^{m/2}$, although the stochastic kernel is
reversible. Its adjacent reflection quadratic form on that
native linear coordinate is negative.
Bounded truncations of that square-integrable coordinate
retain a negative form by $L^2$ continuity.
No other reversible case exists, proving the classification.
The argument tests the actual full state; it does not claim
that an untested color quotient contains this linear coordinate.
:::

:::{prf:corollary} Existing nontrivial stationary color family at every population
:label: cor-nhr-positive-family

Choose any $N\ge3$, $h=b_O=1$, $m=3,j=1$ and

:::{prf:proof}

:::{prf:theorem} Explicit native density and curvature coefficients
:label: thm-nasi-explicit-native-energy

On the complete register, the native compact-chart action

$$
A_N^f=\frac1N\sum_i f(Y_i)
       \sum_{(j,k)\in\mathcal T_i^N}r_N^{-4}W_{ijk}
$$

has the uncut $L^2$ limit

$$
\mathcal A(f)=C_{\rm Del}\int f(y)p_{\mu,s}(y)^{-1/3}
                                  E_\beta(y-\mu)\,dy,
\qquad C_{\rm Del}=c_{\rm Del}/24,
\tag{NASI.3}
$$

with the SAME positive original geometry constant
{prf:ref}`thm-nswt-isotropic-curvature-action`. Put $x=Rn$,
$R=|x|>0$, $|n|=1$. Its full line/complement curvature square is

$$
\begin{gathered}
E_\beta(Rn)=\sum_{a<b}\|\mathcal F_{\beta,ab}(Rn)\|_F^2
       =\frac2{R^4}+\frac{\beta^2}{R^2}C_2(n)
                       +\beta^4 C_4(n),\\
C_2(n)=2\sum_{a<b}n_c^2(n_a^2+n_b^2)
       +8\sum_{a<b}n_a^2n_b^2(n_a-n_b)^2,
\qquad C_4(n)=6n_1^2n_2^2n_3^2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{NASI.4}
$$

In the first sum $c$ is the index different from $a,b$.
$C_2\ge0$ and $C_2>0$ away from the six coordinate-axis directions;
$C_4\ge0$. This retains the native coordinate-phase calibration,
including its actual angular anisotropy. In particular

$$
\partial_\beta E_\beta
   =2\beta C_2/R^2+4\beta^3C_4,
\qquad
4E_\beta+x\cdot\nabla E_\beta=\beta\partial_\beta E_\beta.
\tag{NASI.5}
$$

The action is independent of $\lambda$, cap and terminal status except
through a consumed preparation parameter such as $\mu$; its local
unit-force field is independent of $\nu,\rho$ inside (NASI.2).
Their force norms and actual availability margins still depend on
those parameters. No threshold-crossing conclusion is silently removed.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The equal initial state makes every reward and diversity identical,
so the actual gate accepts no living clone. The original B1 common
potential kick and two A drifts give (NASI.1). Viscous differences
in B2 satisfy $z_j-z_i=(Y_j-Y_i)/t$, exactly in both normalizations.
Translating its original independent Gaussian rows by $\mu$ therefore
gives the same empirical force convolution as Chapter NSPC about that
center. Its count and row population forces are the negative radial
vectors with the norms in (NASI.2). The native unit color is, up to
one common diagonal unitary,
$-n\odot e^{i\beta x}$. Indeed
$z_i=(Y_i-p_0)/t$, so changing the common $p_0$ multiplies every
color by the same diagonal frame. Canonical transports and Wilson
traces are equivariant under it.

Translation leaves the actual Delaunay/CSR incidence, shielding and
star estimates unchanged. The Gaussian density is now
$p_{\mu,s}(y)=(2\pi s^2)^{-3/2}e^{-|y-\mu|^2/(2s^2)}$.
The proofs of Chapters NSPC and NSWT apply verbatim after this exact
coordinate translation, with every compact radius measured from
$\mu$. They prove (NASI.3) and all uniform-root finite moments,
not merely a formal field substitution.

To compute the coefficient, remove the native diagonal phase at
$x=Rn$ and put $Q=I-nn^T$, $q_a=Qe_a$. The horizontal color derivative
is $h_a=(R^{-1}+i\beta n_a)q_a$. Its curvature has line entry
$h_a^\dagger h_b-h_b^\dagger h_a$ and complement matrix
$h_ah_b^\dagger-h_bh_a^\dagger$, in orthogonal blocks. For
$z=(R^{-1}+i\beta n_a)(R^{-1}-i\beta n_b)$ their combined Frobenius
square is

$$
2|z|^2\bigl(|q_a|^2|q_b|^2-(q_a\cdot q_b)^2\bigr)
                         +8(\Im z)^2(q_a\cdot q_b)^2.
$$

For $a\ne b$, $q_a\cdot q_b=-n_an_b$ and the Gram determinant
is $n_c^2$. Also
$|z|^2=(R^{-2}+\beta^2n_a^2)(R^{-2}+\beta^2n_b^2)$ and
$\Im z=\beta(n_a-n_b)/R$. Sum over the three pairs.
Their constant terms sum to $2/R^4$ and their quartic terms
to $6\beta^4 n_1^2n_2^2n_3^2$, giving (NASI.4).
Every term in $C_2$ is nonnegative, and its first sum is
$2(1-\sum_a n_a^4)>0$ away from the coordinate axes.
Differentiation and radial homogeneity give (NASI.5).
The supported unit field and its masks have exactly the parameter
dependencies stated in the theorem.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Full primitive local action first variation
:label: thm-nasi-primitive-action-variation

Let an existing differentiable configuration branch vary through
the strict register, retaining the original full-slot unit readout.
Write a dot for its actual derivative, including every induced
thermostat and calibration dependence. The limiting native action has

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{\mathcal A}(f)=C_{\rm Del}\int p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}
 \biggl[& (\dot\mu\cdot\nabla f)E_\beta
   +\frac{\dot s}{s}f\left(1-\frac{|y-\mu|^2}{3s^2}\right)E_\beta
   +f\dot\beta\,\partial_\beta E_\beta\biggr]dy .
\end{aligned}
\tag{NASI.6}
$$

Equivalently, with $x=y-\mu$ it is

$$
C_{\rm Del}\int p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}
 \left[(\dot\mu\cdot\nabla f+\frac{\dot s}{s}x\cdot\nabla f)E_\beta
       +f(\dot\beta+\beta\frac{\dot s}{s})
                                         \partial_\beta E_\beta\right]dy.
\tag{NASI.7}
$$

The COMPLETE consumed chain rule is

$$
\begin{gathered}
\dot\mu=\dot x_0-[2t\dot t(1+c)+t^2\dot c]g_0
                         -t^2(1+c)\dot g_0,\\
\dot c=-c(h\dot\gamma+\gamma\dot h),\qquad
\dot t=\dot h/2,\qquad
\dot s/s=\dot t/t+\dot q/q,\qquad
\dot\beta=\dot\kappa/t-\kappa\dot t/t^2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{NASI.8}
$$

Here $\dot g_0$ is evaluated from the actual configured gradient
and entering position; for a centered quadratic it is
$\dot\lambda x_0+\lambda\dot x_0$. A nonexistent derivative at an
actual provider/clamp switch retains that branch's weak law derivative.
For an existing fixed physical calibration
$\kappa=m\ell_0/\hbar_{\rm eff}$, retain the derivatives of these
actual parameters, including any effective floor. A consumed current
calibration is not assigned an independent fixed-$\kappa$ derivative.

In the independent isotropic Rust diffusion-factor tag,
$q=b_O\sqrt{(1-e^{-2\gamma h})/(2\gamma)}$ for $\gamma>0$;
at zero friction it is $b_O\sqrt h$. Thus

$$
\frac{\dot q}{q}=\frac{\dot b_O}{b_O}
 +\frac{\gamma c^2}{1-c^2}\dot h
 +\left(\frac{hc^2}{1-c^2}-\frac1{2\gamma}\right)\dot\gamma,
\tag{NASI.9}
$$

with the derived $\gamma=0$ coefficients $1/(2h)$ and $-h/2$.
For the different inverse-temperature-linked tag
$q^2=(1-c^2)/\beta_{\rm eff}$, use instead
$\dot q/q=c^2(h\dot\gamma+\gamma\dot h)/(1-c^2)
-\dot\beta_{\rm eff}/(2\beta_{\rm eff})$ where $q>0$.
Its $\gamma=0$ finite-temperature endpoint has $q=0$ and does not
satisfy the positive Gaussian register. An automatic thermostat's
actual derivative of $\beta_{\rm eff}$ is retained.

The limiting expression is locally uniform in the parameters in
(NASI.2). Its displayed derivative is also the limit of original
parameter finite differences when $N\to\infty$ is taken first.
For arbitrary parameter paths it does not alone exchange a derivative
across finite-$N$ hard availability or calibration boundaries.
The strong original Gaussian source derivatives proved below have
that additional exchange argument.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
On a sufficiently small primitive parameter neighborhood,
$K^+$ remains away from $\mu$ and has one positive force margin,
positive Gaussian density lower bound, positive row mass lower bound
and finite calibration bound. The bounded Gaussian summand derivative
profiles, meshes, shielding constants and all star moments in NSWT
can therefore be chosen uniformly. A finite parameter mesh and their
uniform derivative bounds give locally uniform convergence of the
bounded protected empirical laws; their uniform moment bounds remove
the cutoffs exactly as in {prf:ref}`thm-nswt-uncut-face-limit`.
This proves the claimed locally uniform action limit.

Differentiate the explicit integral (NASI.3), whose support is compact
and excludes its actual singular point. At fixed $y$,

$$
\dot{\log p}_{\mu,s}
 =\frac{\dot s}{s}\left(\frac{|y-\mu|^2}{s^2}-3\right)
                       +\frac{(y-\mu)\cdot\dot\mu}{s^2},
\qquad
\dot E=\dot\beta\partial_\beta E-\dot\mu\cdot\nabla E.
$$

The mean terms are $-\dot\mu\cdot\nabla(p^{-1/3}E)$;
compact integration by parts moves them onto $f$. The other terms
give (NASI.6). Apply (NASI.5) and the same compact integration by
parts to obtain (NASI.7). Differentiating the actually executed
preparation gives (NASI.8). The original thermostat formula gives
(NASI.9); expanding $e^{-2\gamma h}$ at zero gives its stated
limits. The linked-temperature tag follows by differentiating its
different defining relation. These calculations leave every
consumed parameter dependency visible. Finally apply the locally
uniform convergence at each fixed parameter displacement before
taking its ordinary difference quotient. This proves that sequential
scope without an unjustified finite-$N$ derivative exchange.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Exact native mean and noise-amplitude score correspondence
:label: thm-nasi-native-gaussian-score

The raw terminal array has its ORIGINAL Gaussian source action

$$
S_N(Y)=\frac1{2s^2}\sum_i|Y_i-\mu|^2
                         +\frac{3N}{2}\log(2\pi s^2).
\tag{NASI.10}
$$

At fixed $t,\rho,\nu,\delta_c,\kappa$ its full-slot unit composite
observable, as a function of physical $Y$, is independent of $\mu,q$
up to common color conjugation. For an original common source shift
$G_i\mapsto G_i+\theta a$,

$$
E\left[A_N^f\sum_i a\cdot G_i\right]
                         =sE A_N^{a\cdot\nabla f}.
\tag{NASI.11}
$$

For the ACTUAL existing noise-amplitude path $q\mapsto e^\theta q$,
with these other parameters and preparation mean fixed,

$$
\left.\partial_\theta E A_N^f(e^\theta q)\right|_0
               =E\left[A_N^f\sum_i(|G_i|^2-3)\right].
\tag{NASI.12}
$$

Their original unbounded scores have the pointwise limits

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_N E[A_N^f\sum_i a\cdot G_i]
 &=s C_{\rm Del}\int(a\cdot\nabla f)p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}E_\beta\,dy,\\
\lim_N E[A_N^f\sum_i(|G_i|^2-3)]
 &= C_{\rm Del}\int f p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}
                    \left(1-\frac{|y-\mu|^2}{3s^2}\right)E_\beta\,dy.
\end{aligned}
\tag{NASI.13}
$$

Thus mean/noise-amplitude weak likelihood response of the original
finite law equals the full native curvature-energy variation,
including its density coefficient. It is not replaced by a constant
coupling or a pointwise equality of two different log actions.
For any existing landscape parameter changing only $g_0$ and hence
$\mu$, its exact first variation is (NASI.11) with
$a=\dot\mu/s$. In particular changing $\lambda$ at nonzero $x_0$
gives the actual response $\dot\mu=-t^2(1+c)x_0\dot\lambda$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Equation (NASI.1) gives (NASI.10). At fixed physical coordinates,
the original viscous force is $\nu/(tN)$ times the weighted
position-difference sum, or $\nu/t$ times its nonself row quotient.
Its masks use those same physical quantities. The source velocity
is $(Y_i-p_0)/t$, whose common $p_0$ phase only conjugates every
projector and transport by one diagonal unitary. Thus $q,\mu,p_0$
do not enter the physical-coordinate Wilson observable. The actual
terminal potential force/cap/status may change but are not consumed
by this full-slot B2 channel.

A common source translation changes all positions by $s\theta a$,
leaves all kernel differences and force differences identical, and
conjugates all colors by one common diagonal unitary. Delaunay
geometry is exactly translated. Its native action changes only
$f$ to $f(\cdot+s\theta a)$. Gaussian change of variables and the
finite deterministic bound $|A_N|\le2\|f\|_\infty N^{10/3}$
give (NASI.11), including its unbounded original score. The NSWT
$L^2$ theorem for $a\cdot\nabla f$ proves its first limit.
Changing $q$ at fixed physical $Y$ changes only the Gaussian variance;
differentiating that density proves (NASI.12), with no smoothness
assumption on the original masked observable.

We give the additional argument needed to pass the growing amplitude
score. It also prevents an inference from $L^2$ action convergence
alone. Restrict $q$ to a small compact positive interval satisfying
one common strict chart margin. The Gaussian shielding, root star
moments and empirical force events in NSWT are uniform on it.
Under an actual original all-row dilation
$Y_i^\theta=\mu+e^\theta(Y_i-\mu)$, its Delaunay/CSR incidence
and multiplicity are EXACTLY constant. Its original count force
obeys

$$
F_i^\theta=e^\theta F_i(Y;\rho e^{-\theta}),
\qquad
\dot n_i=-\rho(I-n_in_i^T)\partial_\rho F_i/|F_i|,
\tag{NASI.14}
$$

with the same formula for the unregularized row force. All kernels
and their mixed dilation/spatial derivatives are polynomials in
$Y_l-y$ times their Gaussian. On a compact root chart their bounds
are global in the original $Y_l$, including one dilation derivative
and three spatial derivatives. Multiplication by $Y_l-\mu$
remains bounded after using $Y_l-\mu=(Y_l-y)+(y-\mu)$.
The NSWT bounded-summand mesh proof therefore applies to these mixed
derivatives too, with explicit Hermite-polynomial maxima and one
exponentially probable event. Its population force is radial for
EVERY nearby $\rho,q$; its $\rho$ derivative is consequently parallel
to it. Its normalized derivative in (NASI.14) is zero. On this event
the pulled-back native fields and their dilation derivatives converge
in $C^3$ to $P_{\beta e^\theta}(y-\mu)$, after removing their
one harmless common diagonal frame.

All constants in this derivative proof are computable from the
retained parameters. For example set $R_+=\sup_{K^+}|y-\mu|$,
$L_F=e\nu R_+(6+e^2R_+^2/\rho^2)/t$, and choose
$\theta_0\le\min\{1,\log(1+r_0/(1+R_+)),
\eta/[4(1+L_F)]\}$. The radial force formulas in (NASI.2),
evaluated at $\mu+e^\theta(y-\mu)$ and $q e^\theta$,
have $|\theta|\le1$ derivative bounded by $L_F$ for BOTH
normalizations: the count logarithmic derivative is
$1-5s^2e^{2\theta}/B_\theta
 -e^{2\theta}R^2\rho^2/B_\theta^2$, and the row one is
$1-2s^2e^{2\theta}/B_\theta$, where
$B_\theta=\rho^2+s^2e^{2\theta}$.
The fixed-physical-root logarithmic derivatives omit the leading
one and, for count, replace the last term by
$+R^2s^2e^{2\theta}/B_\theta^2$; the same larger $L_F$ bounds
their norm derivatives. The displayed choice therefore retains
both the dilated and fixed-physical margins and chart for
$q\in[qe^{-\theta_0},qe^{\theta_0}]$.
Then use the exact summands

$$
a_\theta(y,Y)=e^{-e^{2\theta}|Y-y|^2/(2\rho^2)},\qquad
b_\theta(y,Y)=\frac{e^\theta}{t}(Y-y)a_\theta(y,Y).
$$

For $|\alpha|\le4$ and $0\le m\le2$, differentiate in $y$ and
$\theta$. With $u=e^\theta(Y-y)/\rho$, each component is an
EXPLICIT polynomial $\sum_\zeta d_\zeta(\theta)u^\zeta$
times $e^{-|u|^2/2}$. An admissible summand bound is

$$
M_{\alpha,m}=\sum_\zeta
  \max_{|\theta|\le\theta_0}|d_\zeta(\theta)|
  \left(\frac{|\zeta|}{e}\right)^{|\zeta|/2},
\tag{NASI.21}
$$

with order-zero factor one and the finite vector-component sum.
This retains every power of $t^{-1},\rho$ and $e^\theta$.
Use the exact NSWT tolerance from the common force margin and
row mass floor, with these enlarged profiles. Its finite mesh
union gives $A_F,c_F,N_0$ by the formulas in
{prf:ref}`lem-nswt-smooth-event`; the $m=2$ bounds control the
mixed $\theta$ mesh. The positive interval $q\in[q_-,q_+]$
gives $s_-=tq_-$, $s_+=tq_+$ and the common shield density
lower bound
$\beta_*=(2\pi s_+^2)^{-3/2}
 \exp[-(R_++1)^2/(2s_-^2)]$, with
the already evaluated $R_+$. Thus its NSWT shield constants are
$c_*=\beta_*v_3/(2\cdot16^3)$ and $M_*=17^3$.

For a derivative calculation only, construct a smooth bounded
observable $\widetilde A_N(Y)$ from the ORIGINAL physical readout.
For each face multiply its defect by smooth force-norm cutoffs
which vanish below $\delta_c+\eta/8$ and equal one above
$\delta_c+\eta/4$, where $\eta$ is its common strict margin.
Use smooth overlap cutoffs supported strictly above the actual
$\delta_\ell$, equal to one above another fixed value below one.
In row normalization also use mass cutoffs vanishing below a
positive fixed fraction of the common population mass lower bound.
On their support the ORIGINAL normalization and polar transports
are used exactly; extend the product by zero elsewhere. These are
proof cutoffs, not a changed algorithm, force or reported action.

Except when the smooth force event fails or a chart root has an
edge longer than a fixed primitive chart radius, all these factors
equal one. The latter event has exponentially small probability
by the finite-binomial shield, uniformly at each root; union over
its $N$ possible roots retains a polynomial times exponential bound.
For example take overlap transition levels
$b_0=(1+\delta_\ell)/2$, $b_1=(3+\delta_\ell)/4$ and choose
the local edge radius at most
$\min\{r_0,\sqrt{1-b_1^2}/[4(1+L_1)]\}$, where $L_1$ is the
uniform original projector derivative bound. The exact identity
$\|P_i-P_j\|=\sqrt{1-|c_i^\dagger c_j|^2}$ then proves the
required overlap margin from the original short-edge event.
Call that radius $\ell_*$. One can use $C=A_F+M_*$ and
$c=\min\{c_F,c_*(\ell_*/2)^3\}$ for $N\ge N_0$, increasing
$N_0$ by the exact mesh/shield thresholds. Thus for these
fully parameterized $C,c>0$,

$$
P(A_N\ne\widetilde A_N)\le CNe^{-cN},\qquad
|A_N-\widetilde A_N|\le4\|f\|_\infty N^{10/3}.
\tag{NASI.15}
$$

The cutoffs are fixed physical-coordinate functions, independent of
$q$. Both original and smoothed expectations have Gaussian variance
derivatives. Since the original amplitude score has variance $6N$,
Cauchy--Schwarz gives

$$
\left|E[(A_N-\widetilde A_N)\sum_i(|G_i|^2-3)]\right|
 \le4\|f\|_\infty N^{10/3}\sqrt{6N}\sqrt{CNe^{-cN}}
                                                        \longrightarrow0.
\tag{NASI.16}
$$

This pays the entire original missing/threshold sector even in the
derivative; its probability is not merely declared negligible.

For the smoothed observable, differentiation along the actual
dilation is legitimate. Gaussian row maxima have every finite
moment. Force/mass/overlap inverses on the cutoff support are bounded
by primitive constants; all differentiated Gaussian sums are bounded
there by finite polynomials in $N$ and $1+\max_i|Y_i|$.
The fixed-face dilation leaves the Delaunay incidence unchanged,
including all null geometric tie cases. These bounds dominate its
finite-$N$ derivative under the original Gaussian law. Therefore
its Gaussian score expectation equals its actual path derivative.

For an explicit cutoff use $\zeta(u)=e^{-1/u}$ when $u>0$,
zero otherwise, and
$S(u)=\zeta(u)/(\zeta(u)+\zeta(1-u))$ on $[0,1]$, extended
by zero and one. Its finite derivative profile is
$\max_{0\le u\le1,\,k\le4}|S^{(k)}(u)|$. Scale it by the
actual force width $\eta/8$, row mass width $d_0/4$, and overlap
width $(1-\delta_\ell)/4$; $d_0$ is the common population
mass minimum, unused by count normalization. Exact quotient,
product and inverse-norm derivatives using (NASI.21) give
finite $L_j,\dot L_j$ for $0\le j\le3$ from the actual
force floor $\delta_c+\eta/8$, row floor $d_0/4$, chart radius
$R_+$, phase $|\beta|e^{\theta_0}$ and these cutoff profiles.
Equivalently these are finite maxima of the explicit derivative
expressions over their bounded jet boxes with these positive
denominators. They depend on $q,t,\rho,\nu$, all chart/mask
margins and phase/cutoff data, not on an unknown law.

On the common smooth local-star event, the original polar/parallel
triangle expansion can be differentiated using the bounded mixed
$C^3$ field profiles. Its first-order terms still cancel.
With $\mathscr L=1+\sum_{j\le3}(L_j+\dot L_j)$ and $D_\chi$
the sum of the finite scaled cutoff derivative profiles above,
for example enlarge the NSWT polar/ODE absolute-coefficient bound
to $L=10^{12}e^{64\mathscr L\ell_*}(1+\mathscr L)^{24}
(1+D_\chi)^4$. It gives
the completely parameterized bound

$$
\|\dot H\|_F\le L r_N^2(R_N^*)^2,
\qquad
r_N^{-4}|\dot W|\le L^2(R_N^*)^4.
\tag{NASI.17}
$$

Indeed differentiate each of the convergent polar binomial factors
on its half-norm projector ball and each projected ODE coefficient;
the differentiated quadratic coefficients are bounded products of
the mixed profiles, and every cubic remainder is bounded by the
same products times total edge length cubed. The quadratic loop
bound in NSWT applies to $H-I$ and this differentiated loop bound
to $\dot H$. The EXACT identity
$\dot W=\Re\operatorname{tr}[(H-I)^\dagger\dot H]/3$
proves the last estimate. The $f$ derivative costs only
$\|\nabla f\|_\infty\sup_K|y-\mu|$ times the original loop bound.
Thus each derivative root summand is bounded by a primitive constant
times $K_N^2(R_N^*)^4$. It has every finite moment uniformly by NSWT.
Outside the event its smoothed derivative has the polynomial bound
just described; exponential failure probabilities and Gaussian
maxima pay all those moments by Cauchy--Schwarz.

On bounded protected cores the mixed field convergence and exact
native triangle expansion now give the derivative-face limit
$\beta\partial_\beta\|\mathcal F_\beta(u,v)\|_F^2/24$.
The field is PULLED BACK by the actual all-row dilation, hence
its limiting phase coefficient is $\beta e^\theta$ and its
old face vectors are fixed. A separate extra $4E$ term is
not added to that derivative.
The root test contributes $(y-\mu)\cdot\nabla f$.
The determining-neighborhood and two-root proof in NSPC applies
to these bounded differentiated functions of the same root star.
The derivative moments just proved remove radius, degree, protection
and input truncations by the same Jensen/Cauchy--Schwarz argument
as NSWT. Isotropic Poisson area averaging therefore gives

$$
\lim_N E\dot{\widetilde A}_N
 =C_{\rm Del}\int p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}
  \left[((y-\mu)\cdot\nabla f)E_\beta
                         +f\beta\partial_\beta E_\beta\right]dy.
$$

Use (NASI.5) and compact integration by parts to turn this into
the second expression of (NASI.13). Equation (NASI.16) removes
the proof cutoffs in the ORIGINAL score expectation. This proves
the required derivative exchange and the theorem.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Primitive correspondence and evaluated mismatch regimes
:label: thm-nasi-correspondence-regimes

Within the complete strict register the following are properties
of the actual source and original unit composite action.

First, existing landscape/preparation mean variations and independent
noise-amplitude variations satisfy the full weak response (NASI.13),
including the native $p^{-1/3}$. For a nonnegative nonzero $f$ supported
where $|y-\mu|<\sqrt3s$, the noise-amplitude response is strictly
positive; where $|y-\mu|>\sqrt3s$ it is strictly negative.
Both are included parameter regimes whenever their annular chart
passes (NASI.2). Their sign is computed from the original parameters.

Second, a finite existing calibration change at fixed $\mu,s$ has
the actual limiting action response

$$
\partial_\kappa\mathcal A(f)
 =\frac{C_{\rm Del}}t\int f p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}
                         \left(\frac{2\beta C_2}{R^2}
                                           +4\beta^3C_4\right)dy.
\tag{NASI.18}
$$

For nonnegative nonzero $f$ and $\kappa\ne0$ this is nonzero with
the sign of $\kappa$. At $\kappa=0$ its first derivative is zero
and its second derivative is strictly positive.
The ORIGINAL raw Gaussian likelihood (NASI.10) has zero calibration
score. These two first variations therefore differ in this actual
included regime; a pushed-forward descriptor Jacobian is not assumed
to be absent or identified with the curvature action.

Third, even in the exact common-source correspondence, the actual
pointwise source log-action derivative is not the variation of the
normalized measured curvature action. For every nonzero real $a$,
write $J_N=\sum_i a\cdot G_i$ and
$V_N=s A_N^{a\cdot\nabla f}$. Then

$$
\frac1N E|J_N-V_N|^2\longrightarrow|a|^2>0.
\tag{NASI.19}
$$

Thus $E[A_NJ_N]=EV_N$ is an exact native weak source response,
whereas $J_N=V_N$ is not a native likelihood identification.
The literal ray channel has its separate positive and mismatch
results in Chapters NSAV/NTFG; it is not replaced by these composite
Wilson coefficients.

Finally the existing simultaneous parameter scaling
$q_\theta=e^\theta q$, $\rho_\theta=e^\theta\rho$,
$\delta_{c,\theta}=e^\theta\delta_c$,
$\kappa_\theta=e^{-\theta}\kappa$, with $t,\mu,\nu$ fixed,
preserves every native projector, force/overlap mask and unit Wilson
defect up to its common frame. Its exact finite-$N$ action obeys

$$
A_N^f(\theta)=A_N^{f(\mu+e^\theta(\,\cdot-\mu))}(0),
\qquad
\left.\partial_\theta EA_N^f(\theta)\right|_0
                         =EA_N^{(\,\cdot-\mu)\cdot\nabla f}.
\tag{NASI.20}
$$

This is a path through existing configured parameters, not a new
per-face weight. If an actual readout clamps the threshold at a fixed
positive floor, this exact scaling claim requires that the effective
threshold follow the displayed scaling on its actual unclamped branch;
otherwise its clamp/mask variation is retained. Its limiting derivative
is precisely (NASI.7), with $\dot s/s=1$ and $\dot\beta=-\beta$.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
The first response is proved by the ORIGINAL uncut source theorem.
$E_\beta>0$ and $p^{-1/3}>0$ on every strict chart. Its displayed
radius test makes the second integrand in (NASI.13) strictly of the
stated sign. The count and row force margins determine whether that
annulus is consumed; for sufficiently small positive original
threshold they both include such annuli below and above $\sqrt3s$,
subject to the fixed box. No different sample law is introduced.

Differentiate (NASI.4) on the compact chart to obtain (NASI.18).
$C_2>0$ away from a Lebesgue-null union of coordinate rays, and a
nonzero continuous nonnegative $f$ has positive-volume support there.
This proves the strict sign at $\beta\ne0$. At zero, its second
derivative is $2C_{\rm Del}t^{-2}\int f p^{-1/3}C_2/R^2>0$.
The raw Gaussian density contains no $\kappa$, proving its zero
raw score without a claim about an unknown coarse density.

The original common score has $EJ_N^2=N|a|^2$.
NSWT gives $\sup_N EV_N^2<\infty$. Hence Cauchy--Schwarz bounds
$|EJ_NV_N|$ by a constant times $\sqrt N$. Divide the expansion
of $E|J_N-V_N|^2$ by $N$ to obtain (NASI.19).
The sign convention is $\dot S_N=-J_N$ under the translated
Gaussian mean; changing that sign leaves the same mismatch.

Under the final actual scaling, every original difference in $z$
and $Y$ is multiplied by $e^\theta$, while its kernel bandwidth
has that same factor. Count or row force is multiplied by
$e^\theta$, and its effective force threshold has that factor.
The phase product $\kappa_\theta z_i^\theta$ differs from its old
value only by a common diagonal phase because the common pre-O
velocity is retained. Thus native projectors are common-conjugate,
all force/overlap masks agree, and canonical unit Wilson defects
are identical. Delaunay geometry is exactly dilated about $\mu$,
with every rooted cycle unchanged. Only $f$ changes, proving
(NASI.20). Its finite deterministic bound permits differentiation.
The uncut NSWT theorem for $x\cdot\nabla f$ gives its limit.
Formula (NASI.7) yields exactly that same limit; the native density
factor cancels the spatial Jacobian and curvature scaling as derived,
without changing any face coefficient.
:::

:::{prf:theorem} Weighted Yang--Mills pullback, actual radial solution and nonzero calibrated residual
:label: thm-nasi-native-weighted-yang-mills

On the actual strict chart set $w=p_{\mu,s}^{-1/3}$,
$\omega_a=[P,\partial_aP]$,
$\mathcal F_{ab}=[\partial_aP,\partial_bP]$,
and $D_aT=\partial_aT+[\omega_a,T]$. For an EXISTING primitive
configuration variation, let $\dot P,\dot\omega,\dot w$
be its derived field/density variations, rather than an independent
new gauge sample. The original curvature action first variation is

$$
\dot{\mathcal A}(f)=
C_{\rm Del}\int f\dot w E_\beta\,dy
-2C_{\rm Del}\sum_b\int
 \left\langle\sum_a D_a(fw\mathcal F_{ab}),
                                   \dot\omega_b\right\rangle_Fdy,
\tag{NASI.22}
$$

where the real Frobenius inner product is used and $f$ is fixed.
This is exactly the weighted Yang--Mills variational form pulled
back to the native projector support. All original density and
calibration responses remain in (NASI.22).

For the existing supplied-phase-coefficient tag admitting
$\kappa=0$, the actual radial projector has NONZERO curvature but
is an exact weighted vacuum solution away from its origin:

$$
\mathcal F_{0,ab}(Rn)=-\epsilon_{abc}\frac{n_c}{R^2}J_n,
\qquad J_nv=n\times v,
\qquad
\sum_aD_a\mathcal F_{0,ab}=0,
\qquad
\sum_aD_a(w\mathcal F_{0,ab})=0.
\tag{NASI.23}
$$

This tag includes the canonical force/projector instrument and
the existing supplied `angle` range including zero. A different
spectroscopy branch requiring positive calibrated mass retains
its actual restriction; it is not assigned a zero coefficient.
The consumed stage is still matched B2, not the unavailable
literal origin-consensus B1 archive reader.

For $\kappa\ne0$, choose an actual available point
$y-\mu=Re_1$. In the constant ambient frame removing its phase,
the native weighted Yang--Mills residual has the explicit component

$$
\sum_aD_a(w\mathcal F_{a1})
 =-\frac{2i\beta w}{R^2}
           (2E_{11}-E_{22}-E_{33})\ne0.
\tag{NASI.24}
$$

It persists on an open actual available neighborhood. Thus the
nonzero calibrated native connection, including its previously
proved noncommuting curvature, has an evaluated local source;
it is not an unforced weighted vacuum field in this included
regime. More generally for $\kappa\ne0$ its residual cannot vanish
identically on ANY nonempty open available chart. Within this
native supported family, being a local weighted vacuum field
on such a chart is therefore equivalent to $\kappa=0$ in the
zero-admitting phase tag. No extra forcing term is inserted into
the gas.
:::

:::{prf:proof}
Differentiate the executed projector identity $P^2=P$.
It gives
$\dot\omega=[\dot P,dP]+[P,d\dot P]$.
Since $\mathcal F=d\omega+\omega\wedge\omega=dP\wedge dP$,
ordinary differentiation gives
$\dot{\mathcal F}_{ab}=D_a\dot\omega_b-D_b\dot\omega_a$.
It is the derivative of the same native connection, with every
primitive $\dot P$ retained. Differentiating
$E=\sum_{a<b}\|\mathcal F_{ab}\|_F^2$ and using antisymmetry
gives
$\dot E=2\sum_{a,b}\langle\mathcal F_{ab},D_a\dot\omega_b\rangle_F$.
The anti-Hermitian commutator is skew adjoint for the real
Frobenius product. Compact integration by parts against $fw$
therefore gives (NASI.22), including the separate native
$\dot w$ term. It uses no unrestricted gauge measure and no
stationarity of an unknown physical law.

At zero phase $P=nn^T$, $\partial_an=q_a/R$ and
$\omega_a=n(\partial_an)^T-(\partial_an)n^T$.
Its action on $n$ is $-\partial_an$, so $D_an=0$.
The real antisymmetric matrix $J_n$ consequently satisfies
$D_aJ_n=0$: the cross-product representation is equivariant
under these real rotation matrices. Direct multiplication gives
$[\partial_aP,\partial_bP]
 =(q_aq_b^T-q_bq_a^T)/R^2
 =-\epsilon_{abc}n_cJ_n/R^2$.
Now $n_c/R^2=x_c/R^3$ and

$$
\sum_a\epsilon_{abc}\partial_a(x_c/R^3)
 =\sum_a\epsilon_{abc}
       (\delta_{ac}/R^3-3x_ax_c/R^5)=0.
$$

This proves the unweighted covariant divergence in (NASI.23).
The actual weight has
$\partial_aw=w x_a/(3s^2)$.
Its additional divergence term vanishes because
$\sum_a x_a\mathcal F_{ab}=0$ by that same antisymmetry.
The curvature norm is $2/R^4>0$ from (NASI.4). The existing
zero supplied-angle tag therefore gives an actual nonzero
native solution, with its singular origin and chart scope retained.

For the calibrated residual, put $x=Re_1$ and remove the fixed
diagonal phase at THIS point. Write
$A_a=\partial_aP$ in that constant frame. Its actual jets are

$$
\begin{gathered}
P=E_{11},\quad A_1=0,\quad
A_a=(E_{1a}+E_{a1})/R\quad(a=2,3),\\
\partial_aA_1
 =-(E_{1a}+E_{a1})/R^2
                  +(i\beta/R)(E_{1a}-E_{a1})\quad(a=2,3).
\end{gathered}
$$

They follow by twice differentiating the literal entries
$P_{ij}=x_ix_j|x|^{-2}e^{i\beta(x_i-x_j)}$.
At that point $\mathcal F_{a1}=[A_a,A_1]=0$.
Thus the actual density derivative and the connection commutator
in $D_a(w\mathcal F_{a1})$ both vanish there. Only
$w\partial_a\mathcal F_{a1}=w[A_a,\partial_aA_1]$
remains. The real term commutes, and

$$
[E_{1a}+E_{a1},E_{1a}-E_{a1}]
                         =-2(E_{11}-E_{aa}).
$$

Summing $a=2,3$ gives exactly (NASI.24), with the PLUS
$\mathcal F_{ab}=[A_a,A_b]$ convention of the native connection.
All expressions are smooth on the strict available chart, so its
nonzero norm persists on a neighborhood. Such a chart is an
actual primitive regime: count normalization permits any axis
radius with $\nu a_*b_*R e^{-R^2/(2B)}/t>\delta_c$,
and row normalization one with $\nu b_*R/t>\delta_c$,
subject to the consumed box. No native potential or score has
been replaced by this evaluated curvature residual.

For the stronger chart characterization, the explicit $P_\beta$,
$\omega$, $\mathcal F$ and $w$ are real analytic on the connected
set $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ in centered coordinates. Each
matrix entry of the residual consequently has that analyticity.
If it vanished on a nonempty open available chart, the power-series
identity theorem would extend zero to that whole connected set:
successive overlapping balls along a polygonal path propagate the
zero Taylor series, by the one-variable power-series identity on
each line. This contradicts its explicit nonzero axis value.
Using the derived analytic formula for this argument does not
declare unavailable original records available. It merely proves
that the native formula cannot solve the vacuum equation on an
open chart where it IS originally available. The zero coefficient
case was already established by (NASI.23).
:::

:label: rem-nasi-remaining-identification

The same executed record now supplies an explicit supported

An unrestricted non-Abelian gauge-field likelihood, a local spacetime

Finite-$N$ pointwise derivatives in calibration/force-threshold

## 2_fractal_set/26_native_interacting_color_clock_test.md

:::{prf:definition} Positive-count-viscosity color-clock register
:label: def-nic-register

Retain the complete original execution record of

$$
t^2\lambda(1+c)=1,\quad E=1-t^2\lambda=c/(1+c)>0,\qquad

$$

These are actual configured parameter branches, with a derived
strict positive-viscosity interval; neither force kick is removed.

tag. Finite streams, rounding, numerical failures and different

Consume the actual spectroscopy
`ColorSource::ViscousForce { alignment: MatchedKick { B1 }, threshold }`,

to $\delta_{\rm eff}\ge10^{-15}$; it only inherits the later positive

No strictly positive threshold is silently replaced by zero.

The tested actual dictionary is the retained B1 color projector
matrix entries, availability marks and original entering positions.
It is a primitive color-and-geometry dictionary of the recorded
component-frame color, not the common-$SU(3)$ scalar orbit quotient
or an identification with that smaller quotient. Section 5 separately

No phase-space ray or hypothetical
fermionic field is used.
